source: cross-examiner verdicts from the research fleets (one agent per contested claim, both lenses)

verdicts.dateTest: Claim: MoRD's Lakhpati Didi initiative targets DAY-NRLM SHG women, as stated in the LS reply of 22 Jul 2025 and the backgrounder of 23 Oct 2025. DAY-NRLM has run since 2011 and the Lakhpati Didi target was announced in Aug 2023 (raised to 3 crore in the Feb 2024 interim budget), so the windows overlap. The claim is a standing definition, not a dated act, so no chronology problem.
verdicts.identityTest: Pass. The scheme node is MoRD's Lakhpati Didi initiative, run under DAY-NRLM (not a state scheme with a similar name). The target node, DAY-NRLM SHGs/VOs/CLFs, is the entity PIB names. One nuance: PIB PRID 2146870 says 'The Lakhpati Didi initiative focusses on the individual SHG women and not on the Self-Help Group (SHG)'. So the target population is individual SHG members, and the federations are the delivery chain. The claim text ('SHG membership') gets this right. The edge target 'ngo:day-nrlm-shg-federations' should be read as the delivery chain, not the beneficiary.
verdicts.baseRate: Not a discriminating claim, and it isn't meant to be: it is a scheme definition. Opposition-run states (Kerala 4,12,441; Tamil Nadu 5,63,242; West Bengal 11,59,682; Karnataka 2,54,698; Telangana 8,00,407; Punjab 31,191) all report Lakhpati Didis in the same Annexure I, so the program applies the same way across states. The SPEC controls (UPA vs NDA FCRA cancellations; domestic philanthropy) do not apply to a definitional edge.
verdicts.denialFound: Not applicable, because the claim alleges no wrongdoing. The government's own statement (PIB PRID 2146870, 22 Jul 2025) confirms it rather than disputing it. None found; not asked.
verdicts.innocentReading: Lakhpati Didi is simply an income-outcome target set inside the existing DAY-NRLM SHG program. MoRD says it has no separate budget and is funded under DAY-NRLM. Being both beneficiary class and delivery chain is how the program is designed, and implies no diversion. The record's existing innocentReading is correct.
verdicts.reason: The claim survives on the substance. MoRD's own Lok Sabha reply (PIB PRID 2146870, 'LAKHPATI DIDI SCHEME', 22 Jul 2025) states it directly: 'Lakhpati Didi initiative is an outcome of Deendayal Antyodaya Yojana-National Rural Livelihoods Mission (DAY-NRLM)... Lakhpati Didi initiative is to empower and enable Self-Help Groups (SHG) Women, earn a minimum income of Rupees one lakh per annum'. It also says 'the community institution structures i.e. SHGs, Village Organizations (VOs) and Cluster Level Federations (CLFs) spearhead the engagements' and 'There is no separate budget allocated for the Lakhpati Didi initiative... funded under the DAY-NRLM Scheme.' The problem is the source chain. Neither cited release says this. PRID 2146872 gives only the SHG counts ('10.05 crore rural women household have been mobilized into more than 90.90 lakh Self-Help Groups') and never mentions Lakhpati Didi. PRID 2181702 mentions it only as a reference link (lakhpatididi.gov.in/about-lakhpati-didi/) plus an anecdote about an SHG woman whose 'annual income crossed Rs. 1 lakh'. The record admits it is inferring from sources that do not name the scheme, when a primary Parliament answer states the fact outright. With that source substituted, the claim meets the documented tier (Parliament answer / PIB release) and no longer needs to be an analytic inference.
verdicts.corrections: 1) Add as primary source: ["PIB (MoRD), 'LAKHPATI DIDI SCHEME' — LS written reply, 22 Jul 2025", "https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=2146870"]. Keep PRID 2146872 for the 90.90 lakh SHGs / 10.05 crore households figures. Demote PRID 2181702 to background, or drop it. 2) Change tier to 'documented', and pred from 'analytic' to a definitional predicate (e.g. 'targets'/'delivered-through'). 3) Rewrite d: drop 'Own inference... the PIB texts opened do not use the phrase Lakhpati Didi'. Quote PRID 2146870 instead: the initiative targets individual SHG women (not SHGs as units), SHGs/VOs/CLFs 'spearhead the engagements', there is no separate budget and it is funded under DAY-NRLM, and 1,48,32,258 self-reported Lakhpati Didis as of Jul 2025. 4) The '3 crore' target in d is not in any cited source. Add a source (Interim Budget speech, 1 Feb 2024, or a PIB release) or remove it. 5) The upgradeIf condition ('Lakhpati Didi counts by SRLM') is already met by Annexure I of PRID 2146870. Update upgradeIf to cover only the ₹-per-SHG attribution, which is still missing. 6) The entity scheme:in-lakhpati-didi should cite PRID 2146870 as well.

verdicts.dateTest: Passes. PIB release 2181702 is "Posted On: 23 OCT 2025 10:24AM by PIB Delhi" (MoRD backgrounder on DAY-NRLM). The 47,952 figure is current as of that release. No tenure issue arises because this is a scheme-level statistic.
verdicts.identityTest: Fails. The source gives the 47,952 figure only for Bank Sakhis, not BC Sakhis: "47,952 Bank Sakhis deployed in the bank branches to facilitate credit linkage of the SHGs". The same page defines a Bank Sakhi as "a trained Self-Help Group (SHG) member stationed at a bank branch to support SHGs with financial services. She helps open SHG savings accounts ... enabling credit linkage". That is a branch-based CRP role for SHG credit linkage. It is not a business correspondent. "Banking Correspondent Sakhis" appear in the page only in a list of CRP types ("Krishi Sakhis, Pashu Sakhis, Bank Sakhis, Bima Sakhis, Banking Correspondent Sakhis, etc.") and in the line that both "act as liaisons between SHGs and formal banking institutions". No count is given for them. BC Sakhis are a separate cohort. PIB 1759946 (1 Oct 2021) says 50,000 were "dedicated to the nation as B C Sakhi" under "One GP one B C Sakhi". So the label "47,952 Bank Sakhis / BC Sakhis" merges two different cohorts under one number. The actor is also misidentified. PIB 1759946 says SRLMs were "advised to coordinate with different banks ... to engage SHG members as their BCs", which makes BC Sakhis individual BC agents of banks (or CSC DigiPay Sakhis). They are not a business-correspondent layer run by the federation or association, which is what the t-node ngo:day-nrlm-shg-federations and the word "association-run" say.
verdicts.baseRate: Non-discriminating. By RBI rules, every business correspondent in India is an agent of a bank or a corporate BC (BCNM) and earns the same transaction-based commission (reported at about 0.20–0.32% of amount transacted). SHG-member BC Sakhis are one small subset of about 1.5 million+ BC points, and any BC agent in a village handles AePS/DBT cash-outs. So "sits at the DBT last mile and earns commission" is true of about 100% of BCs. It says nothing specific about SHG federations. Symmetry with the SPEC controls (Azim Premji / Tata / Reliance / Adani foundations as scale controls): none of them runs a BC network either, so the lens adds nothing distinctive.
verdicts.denialFound: None found. MoRD/NRLM was not asked, and nothing needs denying: the official record itself separates Bank Sakhis (branch-based, SHG credit linkage) from BC Sakhis (bank-engaged individual BCs). That separation contradicts the claim's framing.
verdicts.innocentReading: Bank Sakhis are SHG women placed in bank branches to help SHGs open accounts and get credit linkage. BC Sakhis are individual SHG women whom banks engage and certify through IIBF as their BC agents. They earn standard BC commissions that go to them as individuals, plus a 6-month ₹4,000/month stabilisation stipend. DBT cash-out is incidental to being a BC. It is not a mandate or revenue stream awarded to SHG federations.
verdicts.reason: The claim has no support in its only source. PIB 2181702 gives 47,952 for Bank Sakhis "deployed in the bank branches to facilitate credit linkage of the SHGs". It never mentions DBT, business-correspondent commissions, or any association/federation running a BC layer. The claim merges Bank Sakhis with BC Sakhis, attaches the Bank Sakhi count to the BC function, and assigns the BC role to federations. Yet the official record (PIB 1759946) says banks engage individual SHG members "as their BCs". The file's own killIf condition ("BC Sakhis are shown to be individual bank agents with no revenue to SHGs/federations") is met on the face of PIB 1759946. The edge scheme:dbt-apb-pfms -> ngo:day-nrlm-shg-federations is a conjunction of true facts: Sakhis exist, BCs cash out DBT, and SHGs have federations. Together they imply a flow of money that no source states. The harness copy also carries pred "award" while the file has pred "analytic". No award document exists, so "award" is wrong in any case.
verdicts.corrections: Kill the edge darpan-welfare-join:c004 (scheme:dbt-apb-pfms -> ngo:day-nrlm-shg-federations). If a node is still wanted, replace it with a documented fact-only statement: "PIB (MoRD), 23 Oct 2025: 47,952 Bank Sakhis deployed in bank branches to facilitate SHG credit linkage". Its s should be ngo:day-nrlm-shg-federations or scheme:day-nrlm, and it should have no DBT target. Separately, a documented BC Sakhi statement can cite PIB 1759946 (1 Oct 2021): 50,000 SHG members dedicated as B C Sakhi, engaged by banks as their BCs. Fix the d field: delete "some as Banking Correspondent Sakhis" (the source gives no such breakdown of the 47,952) and delete "association-run". Set the benefit.who beneficiary to individual BC Sakhis, not federations, or drop the benefit block. Make pred consistent: the harness has "award" and the file has "analytic", and neither is supported for this edge.

verdicts.dateTest: Pass. The claim reads: Ministry of Culture (a jury chaired by PM Modi) conferred the Gandhi Peace Prizes for 2015–2018 on 16 Jan 2019. PIB 1560246 (opened with curl and a browser user-agent; it redirects to &reg=48&lang=2) says: "Posted On: 16 JAN 2019 ... The Gandhi Peace Prize for the years 2015,2016,2017 and 2018 has been conferred on the following Vivekananda Kendra, Kanyakumari for the year 2015 ... For 2016 jointly to AkshayaPatra Foundation ... and Sulabh International ... EkalAbhiyan Trust for the year 2017 ... Shri YoheiSasakawa for the year 2018." Modi (PM since May 2014), CJI Gogoi (from Oct 2018) and Speaker Mahajan (2014–19) all held office on the decision date. The dates line up.
verdicts.identityTest: Laureates confirmed: the PIB names "Vivekananda Kendra, Kanyakumari" and "EkalAbhiyan Trust". Ekal Abhiyan Trust is the legal entity; Wikipedia's "Ekal Vidyalaya" is a looser name, and the file correctly keeps it separate from EVFI. The count is wrong. Four years produced FIVE laureates, because 2016 was shared by Akshaya Patra and Sulabh. The label says "Three of the four 2015–2018 ... laureates", which is false. The file's own d field and baseRates entry say "3 of 5 laureates", so the label contradicts the file. Affiliation is not in the cited source: the PIB release says nothing about Sangh or ISKCON links. ThePrint (Unnati Sharma, 20 Jun 2023) supports only Vivekananda Kendra: "founded by former RSS pracharak Eknath Ranade". It calls Akshaya Patra and Ekal just "child welfare-focused nonprofits". Ekal's Sangh link rests on investigative reporting (Caravan) and Ekal denies it. Akshaya Patra's ISKCON-Bangalore link is on its own site and in the file's entity record. The claim therefore combines a documented award fact with an affiliation coding that the listed source does not support.
verdicts.baseRate: The pattern does separate this batch from earlier ones. 1995–2014 laureates (15 counting the joint 2000 award): Nyerere, Ariyaratne, Fischer, Ramakrishna Mission, Baba Amte, Mandela/Grameen Bank, Hume, Bharatiya Vidya Bhavan, Havel, C. S. King, Tutu, C. P. Bhatt, ISRO. That is 0/15 Sangh-affiliated and 1–2/15 Hindu-religious or cultural bodies. The 2015–18 batch is 3/5 on the "Sangh or ISKCON" coding, but only 2/5 if you count strictly Sangh, since ISKCON is not a Sangh body. The killIf condition (a similar pre-2014 share) is not met. Symmetry: the NDA-I (Vajpayee) juries of 1998–2004 chose no Sangh bodies, and neither did the UPA juries (2004, 2005, 2013; the prize was withheld 2006–12). So the skew belongs to this period, not to any NDA government. Caveats: n=5 is one batch from one jury sitting, and the "Sangh-or-ISKCON" category was built by the analyst in a way that raises the numerator. Later Modi-era laureates (Qaboos 2019, Mujib 2020) are not aligned; Gita Press 2021 is a Hindu publisher but not a Sangh body.
verdicts.denialFound: Ekal: "The FTS or the Ekal Abhiyan is not affiliated to the RSS", said Nirmalya Bhattacharya, Ekal's West Bengal head, quoted in The Caravan (https://caravanmagazine.in/politics/ekal-vidyalaya-abhiyan-rss-fts-vhp-hindutva-west-bengal-trinamool-bjp). The file does not record this denial. I found no statement from the Ministry of Culture or the jury on why these laureates were chosen, and none was asked for. Kharge, the opposition member, voted with the unanimous decision (PIB 1560246).
verdicts.innocentReading: The jury is set by statute, spans parties (the CJI, the Speaker and Congress leader Kharge) and voted unanimously. The batch was clearing four years of backlog in one sitting. Each laureate runs a large, checkable service network (school meals, one-teacher schools, rural development), and Sulabh (not aligned) got the same purse. However, the file's innocentReading contains factual errors: "earlier batches under UPA also went to religious/ideological organisations (e.g. Ramakrishna Mission 1998, ISRO 2014)" is wrong. Ramakrishna Mission's 1998 award came under Vajpayee's NDA. ISRO's 2014 award was chosen by a Modi-chaired jury on 27 Mar 2015 (PIB relid 117790) and ISRO is not religious or ideological. UPA-era laureates (King 2004, Tutu 2005, C. P. Bhatt 2013) include no religious organisation.
verdicts.reason: The headline number is false as worded: the 2015–2018 batch has five laureates, not four, and the file's own d field and baseRates say "3 of 5". The only cited source (PIB 1560246) confirms the laureates but says nothing about Sangh or ISKCON affiliation, so the analytic coding lacks a source for affiliation. Ekal's documented denial is also missing. The innocentReading misdates both examples it uses: Ramakrishna Mission was NDA-I and ISRO 2014 was a Modi-chaired jury. The underlying comparison does hold: 0/15 Sangh laureates before 2015 against 2–3/5 in this batch. So after correction the claim can stay analytic. It is not a kill, and it does not name a religion or family as the actor; the actors are organisations.
verdicts.corrections: 1) lab: change to "Three of the five 2015–2018 Gandhi Peace Prize laureates (covering three of the four prize years) are Sangh- or ISKCON-affiliated organisations; two of five are Sangh-affiliated". Fix the same "three of the four ... laureates" wording in narrative:0 strongestCase. 2) srcs: add affiliation sources: ThePrint 20 Jun 2023, https://theprint.in/theprint-essential/nelson-mandela-to-sheikh-mujib-a-history-of-the-gandhi-peace-prize-before-gita-press-row/1632973/ (Vivekananda Kendra founded by RSS pracharak Eknath Ranade); Caravan on Ekal-RSS links, https://caravanmagazine.in/politics/ekal-vidyalaya-abhiyan-rss-fts-vhp-hindutva-west-bengal-trinamool-bjp; and Akshaya Patra's own ISKCON-Bangalore attribution. 3) Add a contra/denial field: Ekal states it "is not affiliated to the RSS" (Caravan). 4) innocentReading: remove "earlier batches under UPA ... Ramakrishna Mission 1998, ISRO 2014". Replace with: Ramakrishna Mission 1998 (NDA-I) and Bharatiya Vidya Bhavan 2002 (NDA-I) were the only earlier Indian religious or cultural laureates; ISRO 2014 was chosen by a Modi-chaired jury on 27 Mar 2015 (PIB relid 117790); UPA-era juries chose none. Keep the cross-party, unanimous jury and the four-year backlog as the innocent reading. 5) Add the pre-2015 base rate to d or baseRates: 0 of 15 laureates 1995–2014 Sangh-affiliated. Note that the Sangh/ISKCON grouping is the analyst's coding (strict Sangh count = 2/5). 6) Edge anchoring: s=min:ministry-of-culture, t=ngo:ekal-abhiyan-trust carries a claim about three organisations. Consider making it a baseRates/narrative item rather than a single edge, or attaching it to all three targets.

verdicts.dateTest: Written as: Government of Karnataka paid ₹72 cr to Akshaya Patra Foundation in FY2017-18. The source dates it to 2017-18 ("accounted for 55 per cent of the total government support that Akshay Patra received in 2017-18"), and the figure comes from AP's 2017-18 annual report, which the article calls "the latest that the NGO has filed". The claim window of 2017-04-01 to 2018-03-31 matches. Passes.
verdicts.identityTest: The recipient checks out: the article names Akshaya Patra and quotes its official TV Mohandas Pai. The payer does not quite match. The source only says "Karnataka" and counts it among "10 state governments". It never names the School Education Department. That department runs mid-day meals in Karnataka through the Akshara Dasoha scheme, so the node is a reasonable inference, but it is not what the source says. The "(mid-day meal state share)" gloss is also not in the source. The article calls the ₹72 cr "government support" from the state. Under the 60:40 mid-day meal cost-sharing, the Union's share is paid through the state treasury, so ₹72 cr from Karnataka probably includes central money routed via the state. It is not only the state's own share.
verdicts.baseRate: Every NGO that delivers mid-day meals under a state MoU (Akshaya Patra, ISKCON Food Relief, Naandi, Adamya Chetana) gets per-meal payments from the state. That is close to 100%, so it tells you nothing that would single anyone out. The claim is a descriptive money-flow edge and alleges no wrongdoing, so a non-discriminating base rate does not undermine it. It does mean the edge cannot support any favouritism inference without a per-meal cost comparison. On the scale control in SPEC: AP's ₹205 cr in government grants against ₹170 cr in donations makes it a government-contract caterer as much as a philanthropy, unlike Azim Premji Foundation or Tata Trusts. No religion, family or ethnicity is framed as the actor.
verdicts.denialFound: No denial needed. The figure comes from AP's own annual report as reported by Business Today. The same article quotes AP's TV Mohandas Pai: "Each unlimited meal costs us Rs 11-11.5, the government (Union and state governments) provides 60 per cent of it and the rest is raised by us through donations." That supports the payment rather than disputing it. https://www.businesstoday.in/latest/story/without-onion-garlic-akshaya-patra-mid-day-meals-funding-issue-turns-sour-203019-2019-06-07
verdicts.innocentReading: Karnataka is where Akshaya Patra is headquartered and where it has the most kitchens. Paying a contracted mid-day meal provider per meal (cooking cost plus FCI grain) under a statutory scheme naturally makes Karnataka its largest government funder. It is a price-times-volume payment, not a discretionary grant.
verdicts.reason: The source confirms the amount, year, payer state and recipient. Business Today (Dipak Mondal, 7 Jun 2019) says, citing AP's 2017-18 annual report: "Karnataka (Rs 72 crore) and Gujarat (Rs 41.5 crore) accounted for 55 per cent of the total government support that Akshay Patra received in 2017-18." The arithmetic holds: 113.5/205 = 55.4%. The UP 12%, Telangana 10%, ₹205 cr of ₹391 cr income and ₹170 cr donations figures in the 'd' field are all in the article. One credible outlet reporting a named primary document justifies 'reported'. The claim cannot be 'documented' because the annual report itself is registration-gated and was not seen. The claim survives, but its "state share" wording and the department-level payer are glosses the source does not support, so sourceCheck is 'partially'.
verdicts.corrections: 1) lab/text: change "(mid-day meal state share)" to "(mid-day meal payments; source says 'government support', may include Union share routed via state)". Under 60:40 cost-sharing the Union portion reaches NGOs through the state treasury, so "state share" is unsupported. 2) Add to 'd' that the source names only "Karnataka" (state government), not the School Education Department. Mapping the payer to ngo:karnataka-school-education-department is our inference. Alternatively, re-point s to a Government of Karnataka node. 3) Add the byline "Dipak Mondal" and AP's 'the latest that the NGO has filed' provenance to srcs/d. 4) Keep tier 'reported', benefit.confidence 'estimated' (or 'reported'), and the existing upgradeIf/killIf.

verdicts.dateTest: Written as a sentence: the Karnataka government (School Education Dept / mid-day meal authority) signed an MoU with The Akshaya Patra Foundation, reported 18 Mar 2019. Akshaya Patra has run Karnataka mid-day meals continuously since 2000, so the dates overlap. The claim's from=2019-03 is the reporting date, not a documented signing date. TNM says the MoU "has now been accepted", so the signing was on or just before 18 Mar 2019. The MoU period (2018-19 vs 2019-20) is not stated in the article.
verdicts.identityTest: TNM names "The Akshaya Patra Foundation" and "the Karnataka state government". It also mentions the Zilla Panchayat, Bangalore Urban CEO, who had refused to sign. The target entity matches. The source is a little looser than the edge on the other side: it says "Karnataka state government", not specifically the School Education Department. The ZP (district) level is part of the signing chain, and the article is ambiguous about whether the counterparty was the state or the ZP.
verdicts.baseRate: This is not discriminating as evidence of favour. Under PM-POSHAN/MDM, state governments routinely sign MoUs or annual agreements with centralised-kitchen NGOs: Akshaya Patra in about 15 states, and also Adamya Chetana, ISKCON Food Relief, Naandi and others. A state renewing an existing NGO provider's MoU is the default outcome, not an outlier. The only unusual feature is that the renewal happened while a dispute over the state-mandated menu (onion and garlic) was still open.
verdicts.denialFound: Akshaya Patra's side is in the article itself. TAPF's Naveena Neerada Dasa is quoted as saying "We had put forth an MoU last year, and that has now been accepted by the government" and stressing the foundation's commitment to nutritious meals. The article gives no TAPF explanation for leaving out onion and garlic. I found no contrary reporting saying the MoU was not signed.
verdicts.innocentReading: This was a routine annual renewal with an incumbent large-scale kitchen provider that feeds hundreds of thousands of children. Cutting off the supply mid-year over a menu dispute would have left meals undelivered. So the government signed and kept negotiating the onion/garlic question separately, which the Food Commission was also pursuing.
verdicts.reason: The claim survives. TNM (18 Mar 2019) states verbatim that "the Karnataka state government has signed a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) with The Akshaya Patra Foundation" and that "a conclusion has yet to be reached regarding the inclusion of garlic and onions in the midday meals." This is one credible outlet with a named source (Naveena Neerada Dasa of TAPF), which meets the 'reported' tier. The edge frames the state department as actor and the foundation as counterparty, not a religion, so no kill is needed. The weak point is the 'benefit.how' annotation, which goes beyond the source.
verdicts.corrections: 1) benefit.how: remove "exclusive district-level mandate" because the article says nothing about exclusivity or districts. Remove or soften "despite non-compliance with the state menu" to "while the state-mandated onion/garlic inclusion remained unresolved"; per the source, the dispute was open, not adjudicated as non-compliance. 2) s: the source says "Karnataka state government"; either keep the School Education Dept with a note, or state that the counterparty is the state government / ZP Bengaluru Urban. 3) from: mark "2019-03 (reporting date; signing date and MoU period not stated)". 4) d: add the TAPF quote (Naveena Neerada Dasa) as the party's response. 5) pred 'award' is acceptable, but no ₹ amount or duration is in the source; keep amountCr null. upgradeIf/killIf are fine as they stand.

verdicts.dateTest: Written out, the claim is: CAG found that 187 mid-day-meal samples prepared by Akshaya Patra failed standards, with 75% negative feedback, in 2015. The dates fail on three points. (1) The report is CAG Report No. 36 of 2015, a Union performance audit of the whole Mid Day Meal Scheme submitted to MHRD. It is not a "2015 CAG report on Karnataka's mid-day meal programme", as the record's `d` field says. (2) The 187 samples were tested over 2010-14, not in 2015. (3) The `srcs` title "In Karnataka, Akshaya Patra once again defies government on nutritional norms" is not what the linked Scroll page carries. That page is the Dec 2018 piece published as "ISKCON-run NGO refuses to follow Karnataka order to include onion, garlic in mid-day meals".
verdicts.identityTest: FAIL. Neither the Scroll source nor the CAG report names Akshaya Patra for either figure. Scroll says: "found that 187 test samples of meals prepared by ISCKON failed to meet prescribed standards, with negative feedback from 75% children and teachers." In the CAG report, §4.7 "Excess payment to ISKCON, Mumbai" (PDF p.87, report p.78) says: "the test results of 187 meal samples prepared by ISKCON during 2010-14 revealed that meals failed to meet the prescribed standards". The data comes from the Municipal Corporation of Greater Mumbai. Footnote 15 (p.74) names this entity as "ISKCON Food Relief Foundation a public charitable trust formed in July 2004 and registered under Bombay Public Trust Act, 1950 catering MDM in eight states under the brand name 'Annamrita'". That is a different legal entity from The Akshaya Patra Foundation of Bengaluru. The 75% figure is a separate finding about a separate state. Table 3.4 (report p.49), Haryana: "Out of 24 selected schools where cooked MDM was being supplied by ISKON, teacher feedback ... positive only in 6 (25 per cent) schools ... Thus, there was a negative feedback in 75 per cent schools." That is 75% of schools, not 75% of children and teachers, and the supplier is again unnamed beyond "ISKON". So the claim joins a Mumbai finding (IFRF, 2010-14) and a Haryana finding (unidentified ISKCON supplier) and attaches both to Akshaya Patra. Neither source makes that attribution. The one CAG passage that might concern Akshaya Patra is Annex p.116: "ISKCON, an NGO supplies MDM to the children of 305 schools in the taluks Ballari and Hosapete", with rice under-utilised by 12.70-23.79% in 2011-14. Karnataka is Akshaya Patra's home state, but that passage is not this claim and still needs an entity match.
verdicts.baseRate: The report finds quality and quantity failures in almost every audited state, with every kind of supplier. In Mumbai, 96% of 1,304 samples (1,250) failed calorie norms across all suppliers in 2009-14. CITCO (Chandigarh) drew 75% negative child feedback. Goa, Assam and others show calorie or protein shortfalls. So a failed-sample finding does not set ISKCON-linked kitchens apart. The fair reading of the report is that MDM quality failed system-wide.
verdicts.denialFound: None found for Akshaya Patra on this point, and it was not asked. That is expected, because the finding is not about Akshaya Patra. The CAG report records state departmental replies in places. No reply from IFRF/ISKCON Mumbai on the 187 samples was located in the excerpt read. Scroll did not put the CAG point to Akshaya Patra.
verdicts.innocentReading: This is an attribution slip, not suppressed wrongdoing. Scroll's 2018 opinion piece used "ISKCON" loosely for several ISKCON-affiliated MDM providers. The pipeline then attached the claim to Akshaya Patra because the article was about Akshaya Patra. The underlying CAG observations are real and documented, but they concern ISKCON Food Relief Foundation (Mumbai, "Annamrita") and an unnamed ISKCON supplier in Haryana. They also sit inside a report that finds similar failures across government and NGO suppliers in general.
verdicts.reason: The claim's own killIf is met: "The CAG report attributes the failed samples to other kitchens." CAG Report 36 of 2015, §4.7 with footnote 15, attributes the 187 failed samples to ISKCON Food Relief Foundation, Mumbai. That is a separate Bombay Public Trust operating as "Annamrita", not The Akshaya Patra Foundation. The 75% figure comes from a different state (Haryana), covers schools rather than children and teachers, and names only "ISKON". The Scroll source says "ISCKON", not Akshaya Patra. The predicate is also wrong: an audit observation is not an `enforce` action (cancellation, suspension, freeze, investigation, sanction or debarment). The edge cag -> ngo:akshaya-patra-foundation should be killed.
verdicts.corrections: 1. Kill edge darpan-welfare-join:c020 (cag -> ngo:akshaya-patra-foundation). 2. verdicts.dateTest: Pass. Restated: "Akshaya Patra Foundation received ₹205 cr of ₹391 cr income (52%) from government in FY2017-18, and excluded onion and garlic from its Karnataka meals during the 2018-19 dispute." The FY2017-18 accounts were the latest filed when Business Today reported on 7 Jun 2019. The Karnataka MoU relationship and the onion–garlic dispute (Dec 2018 to Jun 2019) fall in the same window. Business Today also gives FY2016-17 at 55%, so the share was falling and "majority" is a narrow and shrinking margin.
verdicts.identityTest: Mismatch. The source entity, The Akshaya Patra Foundation (ISKCON-Bangalore-promoted trust), is correct. The target, Karnataka School Education Department, is not the body the "majority" figure describes. Business Today puts Karnataka at ₹72 cr, about 18% of income. ThePrint puts the Karnataka state share per meal at ₹5.87 of ₹14.33, about 41%, which is a minority. The 52% is spread across nine or ten states plus central money routed through them. The record's `d` also misattributes Pai: he said "the government (Union and state governments) provides 60 per cent", not the state. His 60% conflicts with ThePrint's 41% for Karnataka, and the record presents the two as if they agree.
verdicts.baseRate: Having government money as most of its income is not a distinguishing feature. Mid-day-meal implementing NGOs are paid under the scheme (cooking cost plus FCI grain), so close to all of them draw most of their income from government. Akshaya Patra is at the low end at 52%, because it raises donations to pay for kitchens and logistics. The only distinguishing element is the menu restriction, and on that point the evidence is contested. Symmetry: the same lens ("state pays most, religion shapes practice") would give the same reading for aided Christian or Muslim minority schools and grant-receiving madrasas, where the state pays most costs and a religious body sets the ethos. The lens flags religious management in general, not something specific to this organisation. The SPEC controls (Ekal, Vivekananda Kendra, Sulabh, DRI) are not run through this lens anywhere in the record.
verdicts.denialFound: Found, and the claim leaves it out. ThePrint, 6 Jun 2019 (https://theprint.in/theprint-essential/akshaya-patras-midday-meal-runs-into-yet-another-controversy-over-missing-onion-garlic/246491/): "Neerada Dasa, meanwhile, refuted the allegation of their decision having religious connotations. 'We also serve madrasas, so where is the imposition of religion coming in?' he said." Business Today, 7 Jun 2019, quoting Mohandas Pai: "We don't put onion and garlic in our food as we follow Ayurveda system (Indian system) to make sure that we give healthy food to kids." He adds that states may supply eggs directly. ThePrint: "The organisation justifies this as stemming from its belief in the Ayurvedic principle of 'sattvic' food." The foundation was asked and gave its answer: Ayurveda/sattvic, not religion.
verdicts.innocentReading: The foundation is a paid scheme implementer. The state pays the cooking cost and supplies grain, as it does for every mid-day-meal agency, so a government-majority income share is simply how the contract works. The foundation pays for kitchens (₹400 cr for 43 kitchens), 5,500 staff and 550 vehicles from donations (Pai). The menu restriction is a sattvic/Ayurvedic dietary policy that the foundation says meets MHRD nutrition norms, with substitutes (turmeric, drumsticks, greens) and added curd and fruit. Where states insist on eggs, it lets the state supply them directly (Odisha). Whether this dietary policy counts as "religious doctrine" is the contested point. Critics say yes and point to ISKCON's teaching on the modes of nature. The foundation says no.
verdicts.reason: The funding half holds at reported level. Business Today, citing the foundation's 2017-18 annual report: "it received Rs 205 crore, or 52 per cent of the total funding from 10 state governments… In 2017-18, the total income for Akshaya Patra was Rs 391 crore." The second half, "the menu is set by religious doctrine", states a contested characterisation as fact. It comes from an activist opinion piece in Scroll by Karpagam and Prasad of Right to Food / Jan Swasthya Abhiyan ("its religious beliefs contradict the government's nutritional guidelines") and the activists quoted in ThePrint ("imposing their religious beliefs on children"). The foundation explicitly denies it (Neerada Dasa) and gives a different reason (Pai: Ayurveda). An analytic label cannot adopt one side's wording on the disputed point and leave out the recorded denial. That is an alleged claim written as analysis. The edge also points at Karnataka, whose share is 18% of income and about 41% per meal, not a majority. The third source, the FCRA reports page, is JS-rendered, returned no documents and supports nothing in the claim. The record's innocentReading contains a false line, "the same doctrine applies in the 11 other states without recorded dispute". The Scroll source already in the file records disputes in Mangaluru (worker protests), Chandigarh (contract not awarded), Rajasthan and Andhra Pradesh (eggs) and Odisha (egg concession). The juxtaposition of funding and menu is itself in the Business Today source, so the comparison is fair once reworded. Neither the rewording nor the split with a contra removes the religious element, so the claim does not need to be killed.
verdicts.corrections: 1. Replace `lab` with: "Government grants were 52% of Akshaya Patra's FY2017-18 income (₹205 cr of ₹391 cr; Karnataka ₹72 cr) while the foundation keeps a sattvic menu (no onion, garlic or eggs) that critics call ISKCON religious doctrine and the foundation says is Ayurvedic." 2. Either change `t` to a multi-state government-funders node, or restate the Karnataka edge as "Karnataka paid ₹72 cr (≈18% of income); ₹5.87 of ₹14.33 per meal (≈41%)". Do not say "majority" on a Karnataka edge. 3. Note that Business Today says the ₹205 cr includes grain in kind ("cash and free grains"). 4. Add a contra: Neerada Dasa, ThePrint 6 Jun 2019, "refuted the allegation of their decision having religious connotations… 'We also serve madrasas'"; Pai, Business Today 7 Jun 2019, "we follow Ayurveda system". 5. Both sources say the opposite (Ayurveda; religious connotation denied). Fix it there too.

verdicts.dateTest: The claim reads as: the six MP THR plants supplied take-home ration to 49.58 lakh registered beneficiaries over 2018–21. Neither source dates 49.58 lakh as a 2018–21 figure. The Quint gives it as a snapshot: "The most stark irregularities were found in the Take Home Ration (THR) programme in 2021, which was aimed at providing nourishing meals for 49.58 lakh registered women and children" (34.69 lakh children aged 6 months to 3 years, 14.25 lakh pregnant or lactating mothers, 64,000 out-of-school adolescent girls). Scroll says only "a programme under which 49.58 lakh children and women are registered". The 2018–21 window is the audit period, not a registration count. I could not confirm when the SHG-federation plants began production, so whether the six plants ran for all of 2018–21 is unverified (web search budget exhausted). That gap should be recorded.
verdicts.identityTest: The six plant locations (Sagar, Badi, Mandla, Dhar, Rewa, Shivpuri) appear only in Scroll. The Quint says only "six ration manufacturing plants" and names none. Scroll uses the six names in a different context: "Six plants in the areas of Sagar, Badi, Mandla, Dhar, Rewa and Shivpuri said they supplied 821 metric tons of rations that cost Rs 4.95 crore but did not have the capacity to produce at such a large scale, the report claimed." Scroll also says the network is larger than six: "Rs 141 crore was paid in advance to the Madhya Pradesh State Rural Livelihood Mission for establishing seven plants" (Scroll attributing this to the Hindustan Times). So six is the audited subset, and the whole beneficiary base cannot be credited to these six. The operator node is "MPSRLM-linked SHG federations / MP Agro". Scroll links MPSRLM to the ₹141 cr advance. It mentions MP Agro only as the body whose "investigation" found the vehicle-registration errors were "clerical". It never calls MP Agro an implementing agency or plant operator. No federation, society registration or CIN is named in either source.
verdicts.baseRate: Centralised THR production through state-designated plants, increasingly run by SHG federations under the 2017 SNP guidelines and NRLM convergence, is the normal ICDS arrangement across states (compare the Maharashtra 2016 tender control in the same file). So an award of a THR supply mandate to a state or SHG body tells you nothing about wrongdoing on its own; almost every state has one. The only thing that could set this edge apart is the audit's capacity and transport findings, and those sit in the separate audit claim, not here.
verdicts.denialFound: This is not a denial of this edge. It is the state's response to the audit it comes from. Scroll, citing the Hindustan Times, quotes WCD Additional Chief Secretary Ashok Shah: "The transport of THR is mentioned by motorcycle, car, auto and tanker instead of trucks ... it was found in MP Agro's investigation that the above errors have been made in clerical form." He also called the report "an interim one". Source: https://scroll.in/latest/1032051/madhya-pradesh-large-scale-irregularities-found-in-nutrition-scheme-claims-audit-report. I found no response from MPSRLM or the plant federations, and there is no record that they were asked.
verdicts.innocentReading: MP WCD runs a statewide THR programme with about 49.58 lakh registered beneficiaries (as of 2021). Production is spread across about seven plants that MPSRLM set up with a ₹141 cr advance. The AG's draft audit examined six of them. The edge simply records a state supply arrangement. Read innocently it implies neither exclusivity nor that these six plants supplied every beneficiary.
verdicts.reason: This claim joins two separate facts from the sources. Fact 1 is the size of the statewide programme (49.58 lakh registered, per The Quint "in 2021"). Fact 2 is Scroll's list of six plants, which appears only in a sentence saying they claimed to supply 821 MT (₹4.95 cr) beyond their capacity. The label merges them into "six plants supplied THR for 49.58 lakh beneficiaries, 2018–21", which neither source says. Scroll itself refers to seven plants, and The Quint dates the 49.58 lakh figure to 2021, not 2018–21. The underlying award relationship (MP WCD/MPSRLM to the THR plants) is supported at reported tier. The label as written is not.
verdicts.corrections: 1. Replace lab with: "MP WCD's THR programme (49.58 lakh registered beneficiaries, 2021) was produced through about seven MPSRLM-established plants (₹141 cr advanced). The AG draft audit (2018–21) examined six, at Sagar, Badi, Mandla, Dhar, Rewa and Shivpuri." 2. Put the six plant names on Scroll only; The Quint does not name them. Attribute the ₹141 cr / seven-plant figure to Scroll citing the Hindustan Times. 3. In d, remove "MP Agro Industries Development Corporation" as an implementing agency per Scroll. Scroll names MP Agro only as the body that investigated the transport errors. Keep MP Agro in the operator label only if a source that says so is added. 4. from/to: keep 2018–2021 as the audit period, but state that 49.58 lakh is a 2021 registration figure, not a 2018–21 total. 5. Record as a gap that the start date of SHG-federation production at the six plants was not verified. 6. Tier stays reported (Scroll citing NDTV/HT citing an unpublished draft audit; The Quint accessed the document). The upgradeIf is fine as written.

verdicts.dateTest: The claim, written out: the AG (MP) draft audit (s: cag) flagged THR irregularities for 2018–21, and NDTV reported it on Sunday 4 Sep 2022. Scroll and The Quint followed on 5 Sep, and ThePrint/PTI carried the state's denial on 7 Sep. The audit period (2018–21) overlaps the period the findings describe, so there is no chronology break. Two small problems. 'Sep 2022' is when the report leaked, not when it was issued. The draft's own date is unknown. The label should say 'draft AG (MP) audit, reported 4–5 Sep 2022'. There is also no evidence that the draft was ever finalised or tabled as a CAG report. The state said the AG had asked for factual replies within two weeks before deciding whether to include the findings.
verdicts.identityTest:
This test fails for the edge as drawn. The target node is ngo:mp-thr-plant-operators, but the sources pin only some of the findings on the plants.

Findings that are about the plants:
- The ₹6.94 cr transport finding. Scroll: 'trucks were used in six manufacturing plants for transporting 1,125.64 metric tons of rations costing Rs 6.94 crore ... the vehicles were registered as motorcycles, cars, auto rickshaws and tankers'.
- The ₹58 cr over-capacity production finding. Quint: 'ration manufacturing plants ... reporting a production rate which was well beyond their permitted capacity ... Rs 58 crore was found to be fabricated'.

Findings that are about the WCD department, not the plants:
- The 36.08 lakh vs 9,000 girls figure. Quint: 'the School Education Department estimated that there were only 9,000 out-of-school girls in 2018-19, the WCD Department estimated the number to be 36.08 lakh'.
- The ₹110.83 cr figure. It is beneficiary-data manipulation tied to the WCD listing 63,748 girls at 49 centres where only 3 were registered.
- The ₹62.72 cr shortfall. It is a district-to-anganwadi distribution gap. PTI/ThePrint: 'eight districts had received 97,656 MT ... but in anganwadis only 86,377 MT was transported'. That is downstream of the plants.

The plant node also has no CIN, registration number or named federation (identity is all null). The sources name MPSRLM (₹141 cr advance) and MP Agro, not individual operators.

The predicate is also wrong. An unpublished draft AG observation is not 'enforce' (cancellation, suspension, freeze, investigation, sanction or debarment). It is an audit finding.
verdicts.baseRate: Not quantified. No web search budget was left, and the repo has no cross-state THR/ICDS audit table. Audit findings of inflated beneficiary counts and leakage in supplementary nutrition are commonly reported across many states, so on its own the finding does not single out MP or any ruling party. That is an impression, not a count. The symmetry control (the same THR/ICDS audit lens applied to states run by opposition parties) was not run and is not recorded in the file.
verdicts.denialFound: Yes, and it is already recorded as contra c024. ThePrint/PTI, 7 Sep 2022, quoting MP Home Minister Narottam Mishra: 'Just because bills for transportation were not paid doesn't mean it (food material) was not transported'. He also said the report 'was not final' and cited a vehicle-number mismatch: 'MP 15 AV 3835' in the report vs 'MP 15 LA 3835' in department records (https://theprint.in/india/no-corruption-in-nutrition-scheme-ag-audit-report-not-final-mp-home-minister/1119984/). Scroll, citing Hindustan Times, quotes ACS (WCD) Ashok Shah: 'it was found in MP Agro's investigation that the above errors have been made in clerical form', and says the report is 'interim'. I found no response from the plant operators or SHG federations themselves. Whether they were asked is unknown.
verdicts.innocentReading:
The draft is a preliminary audit observation. At that stage the audited department has not yet sent its replies, and the AG had asked for factual information within two weeks. Some of the flags could fall away or shrink:
- The vehicle flags could be transcription errors in registration numbers (the state gives one specific example).
- The stock gap could reflect unpaid transport bills that were left out of the auditors' stock reconciliation.
- The 36.08 lakh vs 9,000 gap could reflect a late or poor WCD survey and mismatched definitions of 'out-of-school girls' between two departments, rather than deliberate fabrication by the plants.

Final CAG reports often drop or restate figures from such drafts.
verdicts.reason: I checked each figure against the sources, and every one matches. Scroll and The Quint both give 110.83, 6.94, 58, 62.72 and 36.08 lakh vs 9,000, all attributed to the NDTV-accessed 36-page AG draft. So the numbers are fine; the edge is not. The label attaches all five figures to 'MP THR plant operators' under an 'enforce' predicate. By the sources' own wording, three of the five (₹110.83 cr beneficiary-data manipulation, 36.08 lakh vs 9,000 girls, ₹62.72 cr district-to-anganwadi shortfall) are findings against the WCD department's identification and distribution, not the plants. Only the ₹6.94 cr transport and ₹58 cr over-capacity findings concern the six plants, and those plants are not identified beyond their locations (Sagar, Badi, Mandla, Dhar, Rewa, Shivpuri). A leaked, unfinalised draft audit is also not enforcement. On sourcing: Scroll and The Quint are not independent. Both rest on NDTV's access to the draft, so 'reported' is the right ceiling. ThePrint/PTI confirms that the report exists, the vehicle finding and the 97,656/86,377 MT gap, but none of the rupee amounts.
verdicts.corrections:
1. Split the edge in two.
   - (a) s: cag (better a node for AG MP / IA&AD), t: ministry:mp-wcd. Carries ₹110.83 cr beneficiary-data manipulation; 36.08 lakh (WCD) vs 9,000 (School Education Dept) out-of-school girls, 2018-19; 3 registered vs 63,748 listed at 49 anganwadis; ₹62.72 cr shortfall, where 8 districts received 97,656 MT and 86,377 MT reached anganwadis.
   - (b) t: ngo:mp-thr-plant-operators. Carries only ₹6.94 cr / 1,125.64 MT transport by vehicles registered as motorcycles, cars, autos and tankers (add 'tankers'), and ₹58 cr production beyond capacity, using raw-material and electricity comparisons, at six plants.
2. Change pred from 'enforce' to an audit-finding predicate, or to 'analytic'/'law' as the schema allows. A draft AG observation is not enforcement. If 'enforce' must stay, write 'draft audit observation, not adjudicated' in d.
3. Relabel as 'Draft AG (MP) audit, reported by NDTV 4 Sep 2022 (Scroll/Quint 5 Sep)'. Note that Scroll and The Quint both derive from NDTV and are not independent.
4. Keep tier 'reported'. Do not upgrade unless a tabled CAG report with the same figures is found.
5. Add to d that the ₹141 cr unrecovered advance went to MPSRLM for seven plants. That is the one finding that names the plants' parent body.
6. Keep contra c024 and record that the plant operators themselves were not quoted: 'asked/not asked unknown'.
7. Add a symmetry note that the same THR/ICDS audit test has not been run on opposition-ruled states.

verdicts.dateTest: Pass. Restated claim: INC (with CPI(M) and TMC) alleged a ₹100+ cr "poshan scam" and demanded a central-agency probe, around 5 Sep 2022. Scroll's datePublished is 2022-09-05T10:10+05:30 and The Quint's is 2022-09-05T14:52+05:30. Babul Supriyo was in the TMC by then (he joined in Sep 2021). Sitaram Yechury was CPI(M) General Secretary (2015 to 2024). Chouhan was CM and held WCD, so the target existed at that date. from=2022-09-05 is correct. The denial (c026, ThePrint, 7 Sep 2022) comes after the allegation.
verdicts.identityTest: Partly fails. Each actor made a different statement, and the claim merges them under INC. Scroll: "Opposition leaders have demanded an inquiry by a central agency into the alleged scam. 'Why not CBI for this?' asked Trinamool Congress leader Babul Supriyo". Yechury (CPI(M)) "asked if central agencies would take any action". Congress's own statement was different: "The Congress tweeted that the Shivraj Singh Chouhan-led government had earlier conspired to 'ruin the future of youth' by committing the Vyapam scam and was now 'killing the rights of poor children and pregnant women' through the latest alleged corruption scandal." ThePrint (7 Sep) says Congress "demanded the resignation of Chief Minister Shivraj Singh Chouhan, who heads the WCD department". It does not say Congress asked for a central-agency probe. So the probe demand belongs to TMC and CPI(M), not INC. The ₹100+ cr figure (₹110.83 cr) comes from the AG draft as reported by NDTV and The Quint, not from anything Congress said. The phrase "poshan scam" appears in neither cited source (0 matches in Scroll or The Quint). The Quint says nothing at all about Congress, CPI(M), TMC or any probe demand, so it supports only the amount.
verdicts.baseRate: Close to 100% and so non-discriminating. Opposition parties in India almost always call a leaked adverse AG/CAG draft a "scam" and ask for a CBI or central-agency probe. The same pattern shows up with the parties reversed: the BJP demanded CBI probes in Congress- or TMC-run states (for example the Bengal ration and recruitment cases). An opposition demand tells us nothing about wrongdoing on its own. At most it records the political reaction.
verdicts.denialFound: Yes. ThePrint, 7 Sep 2022 (https://theprint.in/india/no-corruption-in-nutrition-scheme-ag-audit-report-not-final-mp-home-minister/1119984/). MP Home Minister Narottam Mishra: "There were no irregularities in the poshan-aahar programme" and "The report in question was not final." This is already recorded as contra c026. Scroll also quotes the state's reply to the audit: "it was found in MP Agro's investigation that the above errors have been made in clerical form."
verdicts.innocentReading: This is ordinary opposition messaging after a leaked draft AG audit. The state called the draft interim and put some findings down to clerical and transcription errors. The AG itself asked the state government for an independent-agency investigation. No FIR, EOW/Lokayukta case or central-agency action followed on the record in hand. A demand from an opposition party is not an enforcement action.
verdicts.reason: Two problems, and either one is enough to refute. (1) Wrong predicate. The CONTRACT defines `enforce` as agency→subject (cancellation, suspension, freeze, investigation, sanction, debarment). A political party demanding a probe is none of these, so the edge implies an enforcement action that never happened. The CONTRACT also bars "alleged" as a stand-in predicate, and no predicate fits a political demand. (2) The sources back a looser version of the claim. INC did not demand a central-agency probe in the cited sources. TMC (Supriyo: "Why not CBI for this?") and CPI(M) (Yechury) did. INC made a Vyapam comparison and, per ThePrint, demanded Chouhan's resignation. Neither source attributes the ₹100+ cr figure or the phrase "poshan scam" to Congress. The Quint does not mention the opposition at all. The underlying facts (an opposition outcry and a demand for a central probe) are real and reported by Scroll with named quotes. They belong in a node description or the narrative at tier reported, not as an INC→mp-wcd enforce edge.
verdicts.corrections: Kill c025 as an edge. Its contra c026 then has nothing to attach to; point it at the audit claim or the narrative instead. Keep the content as text at tier `reported` with Scroll as the only source: "After the leaked AG draft (5 Sep 2022), TMC's Babul Supriyo asked 'Why not CBI for this?' and CPI(M)'s Sitaram Yechury asked whether central agencies would act; Congress likened it to Vyapam and (ThePrint, 7 Sep 2022) demanded CM Chouhan's resignation." Remove The Quint as a source for the opposition statements; it supports only the ₹110.83 cr AG-draft figure. Drop the quotation marks around 'poshan scam', since neither cited source uses the phrase, and attribute ₹100+ cr to the AG draft, not to Congress. In the party:inc node, change the d line "With CPI(M), TMC and others demanded a central-agency investigation citing the Vyapam precedent" to separate the Congress statement (Vyapam comparison, resignation demand) from the TMC/CPI(M) CBI demand. Apply the same wording fix to the narrative claim at line ~2499 ("₹100+ crore 'poshan scam'"). verdicts.dateTest: Claim: Chouhan, as CM, held the MP WCD portfolio on 7 Sep 2022. He was CM of Madhya Pradesh from 23 Mar 2020 to 13 Dec 2023, so the dates overlap. The claim is scoped to one day (from/to 2022-09-07), and on that scope the date test passes. The problem is the joining context. The audited THR period, 2018–21, does not match the portfolio date. That period includes the Kamal Nath (INC) government, Dec 2018 to Mar 2020. From memory, and not checked in this pass, WCD minister Imarti Devi also held the portfolio for part of Chouhan's term (roughly Jul 2020 to Jan 2021). The entity's sub-field says 'CM of MP (2020–23), holding WCD'. That stretches a single-date PTI line into a 2020–23 tenure, and the source does not support it. The Quint's 'under the supervision of CM Chouhan since 2020' is looser than a portfolio claim, and the Imarti Devi period may contradict it.
verdicts.identityTest: Pass. The person is Shivraj Singh Chouhan, Chief Minister of Madhya Pradesh, and the source names him with that office. The department is the state Women and Child Development department that runs poshan-aahar/THR. The article says 'the supplementary nutrition scheme implemented by the women and child development (WCD) department', which matches ministry:mp-wcd. The person and the office are not ambiguous.
verdicts.baseRate: Not discriminating, and the claim doesn't need it to be. Indian CMs often keep departments that aren't allocated to a cabinet minister. This is a role edge that shows accountability. It does not claim wrongdoing, so a base-rate test would not add anything. On symmetry: the same lens would make the Kamal Nath government's WCD arrangements (Dec 2018 to Mar 2020) accountable for the part of the 2018–21 audited period that falls in its term. The edge should not be read as giving Chouhan ownership of the whole audited period.
verdicts.denialFound: Nobody disputes the portfolio fact itself. The response on record from the state government is about the audit findings, not the portfolio. MP Home Minister and government spokesperson Narottam Mishra (7 Sep 2022, PTI via ThePrint, https://theprint.in/india/no-corruption-in-nutrition-scheme-ag-audit-report-not-final-mp-home-minister/1119984/) said 'The report in question was not final', that there were 'no irregularities', and cited the MP 15 AV 3835 vs MP 15 LA 3835 plate discrepancy and pending bills. No statement from Chouhan on holding WCD was found. None was needed.
verdicts.innocentReading: The CM held the WCD portfolio because no minister had been given it, which is routine in MP cabinet allocation. The edge records who was formally accountable for the department when the audit became public. It does not suggest personal involvement in THR plant operations, which the AG attributed to MPSRLM and MP Agro.
verdicts.reason: I opened the source and it says what the claim says. PTI copy on ThePrint, dated 7 Sep 2022, states in the agency's own voice: 'the Congress demanded the resignation of Chief Minister Shivraj Singh Chouhan, who heads the WCD department.' The Quint (5 Sep 2022) gives partial independent support: 'The ration distribution programme in the state has been functioning under the supervision of CM Chouhan since 2020.' That is enough for 'reported': a credible wire service stating the portfolio fact directly. It is not 'documented', because no GAD or Raj Bhavan portfolio-allocation notification was retrieved, and the Quint line is looser wording, not a second statement of the portfolio. The claim is scoped narrowly enough (Sep 2022 only) to survive. The linked entity record over-extends it; see corrections.
verdicts.corrections: 1. Source label: the ThePrint piece is auto-generated PTI wire copy, and ThePrint disclaims its content. Change the source title to 'PTI via ThePrint, ... 7 Sep 2022' and quote the exact sentence in d: 'Chief Minister Shivraj Singh Chouhan, who heads the WCD department'. 2. CAG and AG performance audits of ICDS/SNP in many states (MP's THR audit in 2022, plus Jharkhand, Maharashtra, Karnataka and UP) regularly report weak supplier eligibility, missing stock registers and breaches of catering norms. Record-keeping failures of this kind probably show up in most state ICDS audits. The more specific points (13 addresses with no kitchen or office, male non-members cooking) are sharper, but they are one audit's findings on a sample of districts (7 of 13 test-checked). These SHGs supplied meals worth Rs 8.1 crore to 252 anganwadi centres," and "13 SHGs in Alirajpur, Sehore and Tikamgarh had neither kitchens nor offices at the addresses mentioned in bills." verdicts.baseRate: Weak ICDS supplementary-nutrition compliance, with SHGs or mahila mandals that are ineligible or fronts, shows up again and again in CAG and state audits across both BJP- and opposition-ruled states. Maharashtra (Vaishnorani, c031) and Karnataka/UP take-home-ration contractor findings are examples. So the property does not discriminate as evidence of anything MP-specific or partisan. That does not matter here: this edge is a sized money flow taken from an audit finding, not an inference drawn from how rare the finding is. The symmetry control holds. verdicts.reason: The source says what the claim says. FPJ quotes: "54 unregistered self-help groups (SHGs) were engaged in supplying HCM in seven of the 13 test-checked districts" and "These SHGs supplied meals worth Rs 8.1 crore to 252 anganwadi centres." The amount, count, period and sample framing all match. The edge's own description correctly limits it to a sample, not a state total. The tier is right: one credible outlet reporting a named primary document (a CAG audit). It stays reported, not documented, until the CAG report PDF itself is cited. The only weakness is wording: the article says "supplied meals worth", not "paid". Payment by the DPOs is the natural reading, but it is an inference.
verdicts.corrections: 1) The lab should follow the source's wording: "54 unregistered SHGs supplied hot cooked meals worth ₹8.1 cr to 252 anganwadis (CAG test-check, 7 of 13 districts)". Alternatively, keep "paid" and add to d: "article states value of meals supplied; payment by DPOs inferred". 2) Add upgradeIf: "CAG report on establishment and functioning of anganwadi centres, MP (period to Mar 2024) located on cag.gov.in, which confirms the ₹8.1 cr and gives the government's reply", and add killIf: "report shows the ₹8.1 cr was not paid, or the SHGs were registered". 3) In benefit.how, "regulatory-moat breach" overstates what is in hand. verdicts.dateTest: Claim: Maharashtra WCD issued a tender on 15 Jul 2017 for packaged ready-to-cook (RTC) mixes that would displace hot-cooked meals supplied by SHGs. Scroll (Aarefa Johari, 25 Aug 2017): "Scroll.in has a copy of the tender which was issued on July 15. It invites bids for the supply of ready-to-cook food mixes for a contract period of five years in all 34 rural and tribal sectors." from=2017-07-15 matches, and the actor (state WCD under the Fadnavis government, minister Pankaja Munde) held office then. PASS. Outcome is unresolved. I found no award or cancellation record for the RTC tender. The 2019 SC judgment (Vaishnorani Mahila Bachat Gat v. State of Maharashtra, 26 Feb 2019) quashed the 2016 take-home-ration tenders, not this 2017 RTC tender. The Sept 2017 "put on hold" (Scroll 850746) was a different tender: the ₹38 cr therapeutic-food/EDNF tender of 17 Jul 2017. killIf is still open.
verdicts.identityTest: s=ministry:mh-wcd is correct: the Maharashtra WCD department issued the tender. t=ngo:mh-icds-mahila-mandals is a loose aggregate. The source names "around 45,000 small self-help groups ... employing at least 1.5 lakh women", which is a class of groups, not a registered entity. It also names one example, Mauli Mahila Bachatgat in Wardha (annual turnover ₹60,000), and one federation, Maharashtra Mahila Bachatgat Mahasangha (Kirti Karwa). No registration number is available. That is acceptable for an aggregate node if it is labelled as one. The bigger identity problem is the counterparty: the ₹575 cr goes to the RTC manufacturers ("the few who can manufacture"), not to node t.
verdicts.baseRate: Moving from decentralised hot-cooked meals or THR to centralised fortified packaged supply was a common ICDS pattern in 2015–19, pushed by the 2015 MoWCD certification requirement against the 2009 fortification norms. UP, Karnataka and others had RTC/THR episodes, and several later went back to hot-cooked meals. The claim is not discriminating as evidence of intent. It is a documented policy choice with a clearly identified losing class. The FCRA/association controls in the SPEC do not map onto this edge, so the symmetry check is n/a. No family, religion or ethnicity is framed as the actor.
verdicts.denialFound: No denial found, and the department was asked but did not answer. Scroll: "Despite several attempts, Scroll.in was unable to meet or speak with senior officials from the state's Women and Child Development department. Scroll.in's email queries to the officials in the Union Ministry for Women and Child Development also went unanswered." An anonymous ICDS official gave the state's rationale on the record: "The Centre has fixed the rate of Rs 6 per child per day ... suppliers who feel they cannot produce the food at that rate need not apply for the tender." The tender also formally excludes private contractors, which is the state's implicit defence. https://scroll.in/article/848000/maharashtra-does-away-with-hot-cooked-meals-for-children-in-anganwadis
verdicts.innocentReading: The 2015 MoWCD rule made states certify that meals met the 2009 fortification norms, and thousands of small SHGs cannot certify micronutrient levels. Factory-made fortified mixes that can be lab-tested were a way to comply. The per-child budget (₹6/day) stayed the same, and the tender formally barred private contractors. On this reading the switch was about compliance and quality control, not about moving money to particular firms. The loss of livelihood for SHGs was a side-effect, not the aim.
verdicts.reason: The source supports the component facts: ₹575 cr annual business, the 15 Jul 2017 tender, 34 rural/tribal sectors, ~45,000 SHGs, 1.5 lakh women, Dipa Sinha's NFSA objection, and no answer from WCD. It does not support how the claim combines them. The ₹575 cr is the annual value going "to the few who can manufacture the ready-to-cook meals". The same source says the SHGs "currently earn small amounts by serving hot cooked meals". The label "₹575 cr/yr business that 45,000 SHGs stood to lose" is therefore a conjunction the source never states. The edge encoding (pmout, ministry:mh-wcd → ngo:mh-icds-mahila-mandals, a=575) is worse: it asserts a ₹575 cr flow to the SHGs, the opposite of the article. The d field also misquotes the child count: the source says 17 lakh children aged 0–6 in SNP, while the headline says 3 million children aged 3–6. The facts hold at "reported" (one credible outlet with the tender document in hand), but the edge as encoded is refuted until its amount and direction are fixed.
verdicts.corrections:
1. The label should read: "Jul 2017 Maharashtra WCD tender for packaged ready-to-cook mixes (~₹575 cr/yr to manufacturers) would displace hot-cooked-meal supply by ~45,000 SHGs (≥1.5 lakh women)". Do not describe ₹575 cr as the SHGs' business.
2. Set a=null on this pmout→SHG edge, or retarget t to an RTC-mix supplier/tender-bidder node and keep a=575 there. As encoded, s→t with a=575 says money flows to the SHGs.
3. benefit.who should be the RTC manufacturers/tender bidders, keeping amountCr 575, confidence "estimated". Record the SHGs as the losing party in d, not in benefit.who.
4. In d, replace "~17 lakh enrolled children aged 3–6" with "the ICDS office said ~17 lakh children aged 0–6 get supplementary nutrition; Scroll's headline puts children aged 3–6 losing hot meals at 3 million".
5. In d, make the non-response precise: "state WCD senior officials unavailable despite several attempts; Union MoWCD email queries unanswered; an anonymous state ICDS official defended the ₹6/child/day rate".
6. upgradeIf should read: "Maharashtra WCD GR/tender award record for the 15 Jul 2017 RTC tender, or any Bombay HC order on it". The 2019 SC Vaishnorani judgment concerns the 2016 THR tenders, not this one. killIf stays.
7. Pred: if you keep the SHG target, consider analytic (displacement) with an innocentReading, or put a narrative in place of the money edge.

Drawing WCD → mahila mandals as an edge for 2019–24 puts on the graph the very supply link the record says is unverified. It also contradicts 2024 reporting that points to a contractor. verdicts.dateTest: The claim, restated: Maharashtra WCD authorised Community Resource Persons to take Ladki Bahin applications, from July 2024. The dates hold. The scheme GR is dated 28 Jun 2024 and was amended on 3 Jul and 12 Jul 2024; the Nashik page is dated 31/07/2024. The date is not what breaks the claim. The payment terms are. The 12 Jul 2024 GR, issued under the 11 Jul 2024 cabinet decision, adds a Rs 50 incentive per successful beneficiary for every authorised intake person. By 12 Mar 2025 the WCD Minister told the Assembly that Rs 31.33 crore had been disbursed for these incentives. So the intake work was never unpaid, and the claim's 'from 2024-07' framing ignores an incentive that covered that same month.
verdicts.identityTest: This test fails. The claim says the CRPs are 'SHG cadre under MSRLM (Umed)/DAY-NRLM' and points the edge at ngo:day-nrlm-shg-federations. The record itself flags that link as 'own inference'. The operative GR (3 Jul / 12 Jul 2024, reproduced at msdhulap.com) names them differently, in para 6: 'नागरी व ग्रामीण भागातील बालवाडी सेविका /अंगणवाडी सेविका, NULM यांचे समूह संघटक (CRP), मदत कक्ष प्रमुख व CMM (City Mission Manager)...यांना पात्र महिलांचे अर्ज भरुन घेण्यासाठी प्राधिकृत करण्यात येत आहे.' In English: the CRPs are the community organisers of DAY-NULM, the urban livelihoods mission. They are not the rural NRLM/Umed SHG federations. The listing next to CMM (City Mission Manager), which is also a NULM post, supports the same reading. The record's own killIf condition, 'GR shows CRPs here are ... not SHG cadre', is therefore essentially met for the NRLM node. NULM organisers do work with urban SHGs, so the claim is at best wrong about which mission, and the target entity is wrong.
verdicts.baseRate: The property does not discriminate. Every large women's DBT scheme routes intake through the frontline cadre: Ladli Behna in MP, Gruha Lakshmi in Karnataka, Mahalakshmi in Telangana, Magalir Urimai in Tamil Nadu, Lakshmir Bhandar in West Bengal. That cadre means anganwadi and ASHA workers, SHG/NRLM/NULM staff and common service centres, and it applies whichever party runs the state (BJP, Congress, DMK or TMC). Close to 100% of comparable schemes share the property, far above the 80% threshold. Nothing about this scheme or this network stands out.
verdicts.denialFound: No denial is needed, and none was sought or found. The government record contradicts the claim directly. The 12 Jul 2024 GR, para 12, grants Rs 50 per successful beneficiary to 'NULM यांचे समूह संघटक (CRP)' and the other intake agents. In the Assembly on 12 Mar 2025, answering Rohit Pawar and Varun Desai, WCD Minister Aditi Tatkare said Rs 31.33 crore had been released for the incentive (Pune Prime News, https://puneprimenews.com/mumbai/anaganwadi-sevika-and-parvikeshika-to-get-remuneration; the Mahasamvad copy at https://mahasamvad.in/159037/ returned 403).
verdicts.innocentReading: The state authorised all of its existing frontline and outreach workers to fill in forms: urban NULM community organisers, anganwadi and ASHA workers, gram sevaks and Aaple Sarkar/Setu centres. It paid each of them a small Rs 50 per-beneficiary incentive. That is ordinary scheme delivery. It is not an unpaid mandate and not an award to an NGO network.
verdicts.reason: Two separate problems each refute the claim on its own. (1) Identity: the operative GR (3 Jul / 12 Jul 2024) calls the CRPs 'NULM यांचे समूह संघटक (CRP)'. They belong to DAY-NULM, the urban mission, not the DAY-NRLM/Umed SHG federations the edge points to. The record's own killIf is met. (2) 'Unpaid': the 12 Jul 2024 GR, para 12, pays all authorised intake agents, CRPs included, Rs 50 per successful beneficiary, and the Minister told the Assembly in March 2025 that Rs 31.33 crore had been disbursed. The Nashik page does list CRPs, but its line 'No fee will be charged for this application' is about fees charged to applicants. It says nothing about paying intermediaries, so reading it as 'unpaid' is a misreading. Separately, the ≥80% base rate means the edge would tell us nothing even if corrected. There is also a predicate inconsistency: the task payload says pred 'award' while the file says pred 'analytic'. No award document exists.
verdicts.corrections: Kill darpan-welfare-join:c036 as written. If a replacement is wanted, make it a documented edge built on the GR. Suggested fields: s: scheme:mh-ladki-bahin; t: a DAY-NULM community-organiser node, not ngo:day-nrlm-shg-federations; pred: law (the GR governs the authorised intake agents) or pmout (the incentive payment); tier: documented.
