NGOs are the second-largest host category after State Agricultural Universities (487). The other hosts are ICAR institutes 67, State Governments 38, Central Agricultural Universities 22, Deemed Universities 7, Other Educational Institutions 5, Central Universities 3 and PSUs 2. A Lok Sabha-derived breakdown reported by Agriculture Post gives 103 NGO-hosted. So hosting a KVK is not discriminating among NGOs: about 100 hold one. The file's statement that "the base rate cannot be stated" is out of date.
verdicts.denialFound: Not applicable. This is an exculpatory denominator note, not an accusation, so there is no party to respond. None found, not asked.
verdicts.innocentReading: ICAR sanctions KVKs to NGOs as a standing category (about 100 of 731). DRI's four KVKs were sanctioned in 1989–1992 under non-BJP governments, so today's hosting is continuity of an old sanction, not a post-2014 award. Still unverified: whether annual KVK releases to DRI grew faster after 2014 than releases to comparable NGO hosts. No budget figures were found.
verdicts.reason: Not refuted, and the claim is stronger than the file states. The cited source supports only DRI's hosting. It does not support "routine ICAR model" or "across ideological lines", which is why sourceCheck is partially. However, ICAR's own host-distribution page puts NGO hosting at 100 of 731 KVKs. DRI's four KVKs date from 1989–1992, which rules out a post-2014 favour reading of the hosting itself. Analytic is the right tier for an inference that implies no wrongdoing. The one open falsifier is post-2014 annual releases to DRI's KVKs compared with other NGO hosts, and no figures were found either way.
verdicts.corrections: 1) Add ICAR's host-distribution page as a source: https://icar.org.in/en/agricultural-extension-division/host-institution-wise-distribution-kvks (NGOs 100 / 731, about 13.7%; SAUs 487; ICAR institutes 67; State Govt 38; CAUs 22; Deemed 7; Other educational 5; CU 3; PSU 2). 2) Rewrite `d`: remove "without the ATARI list (not fetched) the base rate cannot be stated" and state the base rate as 100 of 731 per ICAR. Remove "across ideological lines" unless named examples from other traditions are added, such as Ramakrishna Mission or BAIF host KVKs. 3) Fix innocentReading: "DRI's KVKs were sanctioned 1989 (Gonda) and 1992 (Ganivan/Chitrakoot, Majhgawan/Satna, Ambajogai/Beed), before any NDA government". Cite https://gonda.kvk4.in/index.html, https://chitrakoot.kvk4.in/ and https://www.dri.org.in/beed/, replacing the "1991/2005" anchor. 4) Across the file (c-row at line ~2320 and entity at ~1006): DRI hosts four KVKs (Gonda UP, Ganivan/Chitrakoot UP, Majhgawan/Satna MP, Ambajogai/Beed MH), not two. 5) Change upgradeIf to "annual ICAR releases to DRI's four KVKs vs NGO-host median, pre- and post-2014". Change killIf from "n/a" to "DRI KVK releases shown to exceed comparable NGO-hosted KVKs without a stated technical basis".

verdicts.dateTest: The claim is "NDA government steered grants and honours to Sangh-affiliated NGOs, 2014–26". Honours: PIB 1560246 is dated 16 Jan 2019, which falls inside NDA-II, so the honour part passes. KVK/DRI: the chitrakoot.kvk4.in page gives no KVK sanction year. The only dates on it are DRI's founding "in 1972 by Nanaji Deshmukh" and the Chitrakoot Project "launched on 26th January 2005", which was under the UPA. Nothing on the page ties an ICAR sanction or release to the NDA period, so this source fails the date test. It even suggests the relationship began before 2014. Grants: the DoSJE page carries no date and no data, so there is nothing to test.
verdicts.identityTest: Vivekananda Kendra, Kanyakumari and "EkalAbhiyan Trust" match the PIB text exactly. Akshaya Patra, listed in strongestCase as the third aligned laureate, is run by ISKCON Bangalore and is not a Sangh affiliate. The file's "Sangh- or ISKCON-affiliated" wording is a merged category, and the claim text itself leaves Akshaya Patra out. Vidya Bharati and Sewa Bharati are named in the claim, but none of the three sources mentions them. The file's own void says: "No Union or state grant ₹ to Ekal Abhiyan/Ekal Vidyalaya, Vidya Bharati, Sewa Bharati or Deendayal Research Institute was found in Parliament answers or PIB". DRI is correctly identified as host of Tulsi KVK, Ganivan, Chitrakoot. The claim names organisations, not a religion or family, so it does not trigger the kill rule for identity-group actors.
verdicts.baseRate: Gandhi Peace Prize, NDA-II period: 8 announced years (2014 to 2021) have 9 laureates: ISRO, VK, Akshaya Patra, Sulabh, Ekal, Sasakawa, Qaboos, Mujib, Gita Press. 2 are Sangh-linked (VK, Ekal), 3 if ISKCON is counted, and 4 if Gita Press, a Hindu religious publisher, is added. That is roughly 22–44%, which is well short of the 80% non-discriminating threshold. The overlap is real but only moderate. Earlier years show similar picks: 1998 Ramakrishna Mission and 2002 Bharatiya Vidya Bhavan, both under the Vajpayee NDA-I. Under UPA the prize went to Coretta Scott King (2004), Tutu (2005) and Chandi Prasad Bhatt (2013), and was withheld for 2006–12. The grants base rate cannot be computed because no recipient list is reachable for either period. For KVKs, NGO hosting is a standard ICAR model, but the ATARI denominator was not fetched (file gap).
verdicts.denialFound: No specific denial of "steering" was found, and I cannot tell whether the government was ever asked. The government's framing is on the record in PIB 1560246: the jury "comprising the Chief Justice of India, Justice Ranjan Gogoi, Speaker of LokSabha Smt. Sumitra Mahajan, Leader of the single largest Opposition Party in LokSabha Shri. Mallikarjuna Kharge and Member of Parliament, Shri L.K. Advani after detailed discussions on 16th January, 2019 unanimously decided to select the above organisation/persons" (https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=1560246). I could not check contrary reporting, such as the Congress criticism of the 2021 Gita Press award: the web search budget was used up and no URL was opened.
verdicts.innocentReading: The Gandhi Peace Prize is chosen by a statutory jury that includes the opposition. The 2015–18 batch was decided unanimously with Kharge (INC) on the jury, and each winner runs a large service network whose scale can be checked. Hindu-cultural or religious laureates also appear under NDA-I (Ramakrishna Mission 1998, Bharatiya Vidya Bhavan 2002), so the pattern is not specific to 2014 onward. DRI's KVK follows ICAR's routine NGO-host model and appears to predate 2014, given DRI's Chitrakoot work since 1972/2005. As for grants, the lack of a recipient list is a transparency gap that affects both periods equally. It does not show favouritism.
verdicts.reason:
None of the three sources says what the claim says. The claim asserts a pattern ("grants and honours ... are steered") and names five groups of organisations. Taking each source in turn:
- **PIB release:** it documents three one-off ₹1 cr prizes, two to Sangh-linked organisations, chosen by a unanimous cross-party jury. That is an award, not a grant stream, and not evidence of steering.
- **KVK page:** it has no sanction date and no amount, so it cannot put DRI's ICAR funding in the NDA period.
- **DoSJE page:** it says "Grants Released to NGOs Data is not available The page looking for does not exist". This is an absence, and the file correctly records it as a void.

The file's own void says no grant to Ekal, Vidya Bharati, Sewa Bharati or DRI was found, so the "grants" half and two of the five named groups have no evidence at all. The overall claim stitches true facts together (some laureates are Sangh-linked; DRI hosts a KVK; grant lists are missing) into an intent none of them shows. It survives only as an analytic observation limited to the prize. "Speculative" is not a tier in the contract.
verdicts.corrections:
1. Change status "speculative" to tier "analytic" and add an innocentReading field.
2. Rewrite the claim as: "Of the five laureates of the 2015–18 Gandhi Peace Prize batch (announced 16 Jan 2019 by a unanimous jury of PM Modi, CJI Gogoi, Speaker Mahajan, INC leader Kharge and L.K. Advani), two are Sangh-linked (Vivekananda Kendra, Ekal Abhiyan Trust) and one is ISKCON-run (Akshaya Patra). No Union or state grant-in-aid to Ekal, Vidya Bharati, Sewa Bharati or DRI was found; recipient lists are unpublished for both UPA and NDA periods."
3. Drop "Vidya Bharati, Sewa Bharati" from the claim text, or add a source for them.
4. Drop "steered", which asserts intent without evidence.
5. Relabel the socialjustice.gov.in/common/69586 source as evidence of a void, not support.
6. Mark the KVK source "sanction year unknown; not shown to be NDA-era".
7. In strongestCase, change "Sangh- or ISKCON-affiliated" to "two Sangh-linked, one ISKCON-run".
8. Add the symmetry point to strongestCounter: NDA-I laureates Ramakrishna Mission (1998) and Bharatiya Vidya Bhavan (2002); UPA withheld the prize for 2006–12.
9. Add "Gita Press 2021" to whatWouldChangeThis as a later data point to check, with its jury composition and any opposition dissent.

verdicts.dateTest: Actor: Akshaya Patra Foundation (ISKCON-run). Action: kept onion and garlic out of Karnataka mid-day meals against a state direction. Window: Dec 2018 to Jun 2019. That overlaps with its MDM contract, so the dated core passes. The present tense "imposes" does not pass. Every source is from 2018-19, nothing after Jun 2019 was checked, and ThePrint says the contract was "extended by another five years" (Jairaj). The 2019 renewal was signed by Karnataka's JD(S)-Congress coalition government, not an NDA one.
verdicts.identityTest: Pass. All four sources name The Akshaya Patra Foundation, "an initiative of ISKCON", serving about 4.43-4.5 lakh students in five Karnataka districts. No registration number is needed to disambiguate a narrative.
verdicts.baseRate: The property is discriminating, not generic. Most MDM kitchens (school-cooked, SHG or other centralised NGOs) follow the state menu. Akshaya Patra is the largest centralised provider and is unusual in excluding eggs, onion and garlic on doctrinal grounds. No count of other CSO providers with doctrinal menu limits was found, so the denominator is unknown. The SPEC controls are FCRA and grant controls and do not map onto a menu dispute. A like-for-like symmetry check (whether any Christian- or Muslim-run MDM provider restricts the menu on doctrine) was not done and could not be done here because the web-search budget was exhausted.
verdicts.denialFound: Yes, three responses on record. (1) ThePrint, 6 Jun 2019: Naveena Neerada Dasa "refuted the allegation of their decision having religious connotations. 'We also serve madrasas, so where is the imposition of religion coming in?'" He also said: "When it comes to children, we follow what the MHRD and state government say." (https://theprint.in/theprint-essential/akshaya-patras-midday-meal-runs-into-yet-another-controversy-over-missing-onion-garlic/246491/) (2) Business Today, 7 Jun 2019: Mohandas Pai said "We don't put onion and garlic in our food as we follow Ayurveda system", and that states may supply eggs directly. (3) ThePrint also reports the National Institute of Nutrition (NIN) report of Feb 2019, which found the meal "certainly meets and often exceeds the prescribed energy and protein requirements". The party was asked, and its denial is on record.
verdicts.innocentReading: The Union MDM norms set calories, protein and grams but, per ThePrint, do not "specify what items are to be provided". Akshaya Patra says it is upfront about its sattvic menu when it signs with a state. States choose to contract with it anyway and renewed in Mar 2019. In Karnataka it pays more of each meal than the state does (₹8.46 of ₹14.33). NIN found the meals nutritionally adequate. On this reading, a vendor has a menu limitation that the buyer knowingly accepts, and nothing is being imposed.
verdicts.reason: The narrative joins three clauses, and no source supports all three. (a) The funding clause "paid for mostly by the state" is contradicted by the only Karnataka-specific figure. ThePrint's corrected text reads: "a plate of the hot meal served costs Rs 14.33, of which Rs 5.87 comes from the state government while the remaining Rs 8.46 is raised by Akshaya Patra through donations". That puts the state at 41%. Business Today's 52% is organisation-wide income from 10 state governments, and Pai's 60% covers Union and state together. Depending on which measure you use, "mostly" is either marginal or false. (b) "Imposes a religious diet" is the framing of a named advocacy party. ThePrint quotes it as "Right to Food activists say Akshaya Patra is 'imposing their religious beliefs on children'". The Scroll source is not independent reporting: it is an opinion piece by Sylvia Karpagam (Right to Food Campaign) and Vandana Prasad (JSA). Prasad is also the activist ThePrint quotes, so the two sources carrying the framing come from one party. The foundation's denial and the NIN adequacy report are on record. (c) The documented core stands on two independent outlets (Scroll and ThePrint): Akshaya Patra excludes onion and garlic on sattvic grounds and resisted Karnataka's direction. The characterisation layered on top of it is alleged. Status "well-supported" overstates the evidence. It should be "contested", and the claim must not become an edge.
verdicts.corrections: 1. Change narrative:1 status from "well-supported" to "contested". 2. Reword the claim: "Akshaya Patra (ISKCON) excludes onion, garlic and eggs from mid-day meals on sattvic grounds, against a Karnataka direction (2018-19). Right to Food campaigners call this imposing a religious diet on a statutory programme." Drop "paid for mostly by the state", or replace it with "government sources supplied 52% of its FY2017-18 income (BT); in Karnataka the state paid ₹5.87 of a ₹14.33 meal (ThePrint)". 3. Relabel the Scroll source as an opinion piece by Sylvia Karpagam (Right to Food Campaign) and Vandana Prasad (JSA), not a news report. The headline stored in the file ("once again defies government...") should be checked against the page. 4. In strongestCase, attribute the CAG 2015 sample finding as "per an op-ed; CAG report not opened". Note that the claim that Akshaya Patra refused to sign the MoU also rests only on that op-ed. 5. strongestCounter is wrong that "the same menu runs in 11 other states without recorded dispute". The Scroll op-ed records disputes in Andhra Pradesh (NIN egg directive), Rajasthan, Mangalore and Chandigarh (contract not given), and ThePrint records an Odisha egg concession. Delete that clause. Delete "children may opt out (which is the officials' own complaint)", since no source says it. Add the NIN Feb 2019 finding and the Neerada Dasa quote ("We also serve madrasas...") to the counter. 6. The religion framing is kept only as a narrative. Do not turn "imposes a religious diet" into a graph edge. The existing edges c017 and c018 (documented directive plus contra) are the correct edge-level form. 7. Add upgradeIf: the Karnataka MoU text with its menu clause, and a post-2019 status check on whether the menu dispute persists. Add killIf: the MoU records state consent to a sattvic menu, or state funding per meal is below 50% across states.

verdicts.dateTest: Claim: the MP WCD Department / THR plant operators ran a ₹100+ crore fraud in THR during 2018–21. Tenure: WCD was under CM Shivraj Chouhan (The Quint: "functioning under the supervision of CM Chouhan since 2020"). The AG audit covers 2018–21 and was reported 5 Sep 2022 (Scroll, Quint). The state denied it on 7 Sep 2022 (ThePrint/PTI). The 2026 CAG item (FPJ, 22 Jul 2026) covers a different period ("ending March 2024") and a different component, hot cooked meals rather than THR. The windows line up for each part, but the claim joins two audits of two components from two periods into one "scam".
verdicts.identityTest: This test fails for "SHG federations". None of the three 2022 sources says SHG federations ran the THR plants, and none says they were responsible for the irregularities. Scroll's only link is: "Rs 141 crore was paid in advance to the Madhya Pradesh State Rural Livelihood Mission for establishing seven plants, but it was not allegedly recovered." The ACS pointed to "MP Agro's investigation". The ₹110.83 cr figure belongs to the WCD Department's own beneficiary data: "the Women and Child Development listed 63,748 girls in these 49 centres... The alleged data manipulation would have led to the falsified distribution of rations worth Rs 110.83 crore" (Scroll citing NDTV). That is anganwadi-level data, not plant operators. The file's own entity ngo:mp-thr-plant-operators concedes that "the individual federations/societies are not named in the sources opened". The FPJ piece names "54 unregistered self-help groups" supplying hot cooked meals. Those are individual unregistered SHGs, not federations, and not THR.
verdicts.baseRate: Audit findings of irregularities in supplementary nutrition are common across states. Maharashtra's THR tenders were found rigged by the Supreme Court in 2019, and CAG ICDS performance audits routinely flag unverified beneficiaries and quality failures. A draft AG observation therefore does little to single MP out. The symmetry control in this same file, Maharashtra, gets "established" only because a Supreme Court order exists. Applying the same standard to MP gives no adjudication: no FIR, no EOW or Lokayukta case and no tabled final THR chapter was located. (Web search budget was exhausted, so I could not look again for later developments.)
verdicts.denialFound: Yes, found. (1) ThePrint/PTI, 7 Sep 2022: "The Madhya Pradesh government on Wednesday denied irregularities in implementation of a supplementary nutrition scheme and said the Accountant General's audit report on the programme was not final". Home Minister Narottam Mishra also cited the MP 15 AV 3835 vs MP 15 LA 3835 transcription error. https://theprint.in/india/no-corruption-in-nutrition-scheme-ag-audit-report-not-final-mp-home-minister/1119984/ (2) Scroll, 5 Sep 2022: WCD ACS Ashok Shah called them clerical errors, citing "MP Agro's investigation", and said "the audit report is an interim one". https://scroll.in/latest/1032051/... No response from SHG federations or MPSRLM was found, and nothing shows they were asked.
verdicts.innocentReading: This was a draft or interim AG report. Some of the vehicle findings were transcription errors (AV vs LA plates). The ₹110.83 cr is a computed exposure from inconsistent beneficiary counts, not traced money ("would have led to"). The ₹141 cr MPSRLM advance is an unrecovered advance, not proven theft. The 2026 CAG finding is about individual unregistered SHGs in 7 of 13 sampled districts supplying ₹8.1 cr of hot cooked meals. That is a registration and eligibility breach, not proof of a federation-run THR fraud.
verdicts.reason: The "₹100+ crore" element holds only as an allegation. It comes from an unfinalised AG draft, reported by The Quint ("alleged high levels of corruption of more than Rs 100 crore, a document accessed by The Quint") and by Scroll via NDTV/HT, and the state explicitly denied it. The "run through SHG federations" element appears in none of the four sources. It is the file's own join: an MPSRLM advance for plants, plus a WCD beneficiary-data loss, plus a 2026 hot-cooked-meal finding about unregistered individual SHGs. None of those says SHG federations ran a THR scam. The narrative's "contested" status and its strongestCounter are honest. But the claim sentence as worded attributes the scam to SHG federations with no source, so it is refuted in that form. Reworded to drop the federation attribution, it survives at the alleged tier with the contra already recorded.
verdicts.corrections: (1) Reword the claim to: "An unfinalised Accountant General audit (2018–21) of MP's Take Home Ration programme alleged irregularities worth over ₹100 crore (₹110.83 cr of beneficiary-data manipulation); the state denied it and called the report interim." (2) Remove "run through SHG federations", or replace it with "plants set up with a ₹141 cr advance to MPSRLM (unrecovered, per AG draft)". (3) In strongestCase, change "₹110.83 cr of data manipulation" to "data manipulation that 'would have led to' falsified distribution worth ₹110.83 cr (NDTV via Scroll)". (4) In strongestCase, state that the 2026 CAG item concerns hot cooked meals, not THR, and "54 unregistered SHGs" rather than federations. Note that FPJ lists only six district names for "seven districts". (5) Add the ACS Ashok Shah "clerical/interim" response (Scroll) next to the Narottam Mishra denial. (6) Carry a tier of alleged, not contested or reported, for the ₹100 cr element. (7) Add upgradeIf: a tabled CAG report with the THR chapter, or an EOW/Lokayukta FIR. Add killIf: a final report that drops the ₹110.83 cr observation.

verdicts.dateTest: Claim restated: "Maharashtra WCD awards (present tense) anganwadi food contracts to industrialist-fronted 'women's cooperatives'". The sources support only a bounded window. The three sanstha (Venkateshwara/Latur-Udgir, Mahalaxmi/Nanded, Maharashtra Mahila Sahakari Grahudhyog/Dhule) were chosen c.2009–10 and upheld in Shagun (2011). Vaishnorani para 21 says: "in 2010 three Mahila Mandals, which were chosen, were found to be fake and were only acting as fronts for existing companies and industrialists." Their supply was the "existing system" that the 26 Feb 2019 order restrained. The 8 Mar 2016 tender was challenged and struck down (paras 50–51). The judgment does not say the 2016 tender was awarded to these three, so strongestCase's "three 2016 contractors" is a chronology error. The 2017 RTC tender (Scroll, 25 Aug 2017) was still at bid stage. Scroll reports that "the tender states that private contractors and manufacturers will not be eligible" and that activists only "fear" the same outcome. No source covers anything after Feb 2019, and the file's own c035 records that post-2019 supply was not verified. The present-tense "hands" therefore fails the date test. A 2009–2019 past-tense version passes.
verdicts.identityTest: The actor is correctly Maharashtra WCD/ICDS, which is the respondent in the judgment. The three entities are named consistently in the SC judgment (paras 7, 21, 24) and match file claim c032. No CIN or registration numbers are given. The judgment cites only a Deputy Registrar, Udgir registration certificate for Venkateshwara, and names Deepak Dinkarrao Lakhangonkar as its authorised agent from 12.7.1999. "Industrialists" is not tied to any named person or company except "private agro-companies" owned "by the same family" (Commissioner's report, para 7). The Court's own finding is generic: "it is not for the big players/industrialists in the field to cater to the needs of the Scheme as they have usurped in past" (para 52). There is also an attribution error. The "fake business units" and "male members" language comes from (a) the petitioners' submissions (para 3: "the State is entertaining fake business units"), (b) the State of Maharashtra's own earlier reply (para 22: Venkateshwara "is actually managed by all male members"), (c) the PUCL Commissioner's report (para 7), which itself says the nexus is "not specifically proven", and (d) an Aurangabad Bench judgment noted at para 24. The Supreme Court did not itself make a finding that the three were fake units controlled by men and industrialists. Its holdings are that the 25% turnover condition was arbitrary and left "only big players" in the field (para 50), that the Court had been "misled" in Shagun on extrusion (para 31), and that the big players had "usurped" supply in the past (para 52).
verdicts.baseRate: Non-discriminating as to Maharashtra or party. The PUCL Commissioner's report quoted in the judgment (paras 7–8) records contractor capture of supplementary nutrition in Maharashtra, Karnataka, UP (Great Value Foods, Ponty Chadha), Gujarat and Meghalaya (Continental Milkose), and says "This state of affairs prevails across many States/UTs." The sibling file records the same pattern in MP (c023, c028). Across parties, the three sanstha were selected under the Congress-NCP government (2009–10), and the arbitrary 2016 tender and the 2017 RTC tender came under the BJP-led government. Using MP (BJP) or UP (SP/BSP-era Chadha contracts) as the control gives the same reading. The claim does not frame a family, religion or ethnicity as the actor (the Commissioner's "same family" remark is about the ownership of specific agro-units), so no kill on that ground.
verdicts.denialFound: No denial from the three sanstha found in either source. The state was asked: Scroll 25 Aug 2017 says "Despite several attempts, Scroll.in was unable to meet or speak with senior officials from the state's Women and Child Development department. Scroll.in's email queries to the officials in the Union Ministry for Women and Child Development also went unanswered." One named ICDS official defended the Rs 6/child/day rate anonymously. In court, the State "fairly conceded" through ASG Nadkarni and senior counsel Vijay Thora that it must follow the Union policy (Vaishnorani para 50), and the State's own earlier affidavit (para 22) said Venkateshwara was male-run. Web search budget was exhausted, so no later statement by the sanstha or by Maharashtra WCD (2019–26) could be searched. Source: https://indiankanoon.org/doc/67854246/ and https://scroll.in/article/848000/maharashtra-does-away-with-hot-cooked-meals-for-children-in-anganwadis
verdicts.innocentReading: Centralised, fortified, lab-tested THR/RTC production under MWCD's 2009 norms and the 2015 certification requirement pushes states towards large extrusion-capable units. Scroll notes that the Centre's "conflicting instructions" created the loophole. Turnover and machinery bars are a crude but common way to screen for food-safety capacity. Under that reading, big suppliers winning is a predictable result of the tender design, not a deliberate disguise. However, the disguise element (women's cooperatives run by men, with production leased from family-owned agro-companies) is set out in the Commissioner's report and in the State's own affidavit, so the innocent reading covers the tender design but not the front arrangement.
verdicts.reason: The historical core survives. From about 2009–10 until the Supreme Court's 26 Feb 2019 order, Maharashtra's take-home-ration contracts went to three nominally women's cooperatives that sources on record describe as fronts for family-owned agro-companies and industrialists. The support is primary (the SC-appointed Commissioner's report, the State's own affidavit and the Court's para 52 "usurped in past") plus Scroll's independent report of the 2012 committee finding. That is documented. The narrative as written fails on three counts. (1) The present tense "hands" asserts a continuing practice that no source covers after Feb 2019, and the file itself (c035) records that period as unverified. (2) strongestCase attributes to the Supreme Court a finding ("found the three 2016 contractors were fake business units controlled by male members and industrialists") that the judgment only recites from petitioners, the Commissioner and the State's affidavit. The Court's holdings are that the tender was arbitrary, it had been misled on extrusion, and industrialists had "usurped" supply in the past. (3) The three were 2009–10 contractors, not 2016 awardees, and the 2017 tender's outcome is not reported (Scroll records only activists' fears). The tier "established" is also not a contract tier.
verdicts.corrections: claim: rewrite in past tense and bound the dates, e.g. "From c.2010 until the Supreme Court's Feb 2019 order, Maharashtra's take-home-ration supply was held by three nominally women's cooperatives that the SC-appointed PUCL Commissioner, the State's own affidavit and the Aurangabad High Court described as fronts for family-owned agro-companies; the SC held the 2016 tender's 25% turnover bar arbitrary and said industrialists had 'usurped' supply." status/tier: "established" → "documented" (bounded to 2009–2019). strongestCase: replace "The Supreme Court found the three 2016 contractors were fake business units controlled by male members and industrialists" with "The judgment records the Commissioner's finding of common family ownership of the sanstha and the leased agro-units, the State's own averment that Venkateshwara was 'managed by all male members', and the Aurangabad Bench's note that the three 'were not really Mahila Mandals'. The Court itself held the 25% turnover condition arbitrary (para 50), said it had been misled on extrusion (para 31) and said big players had 'usurped' supply in the past (para 52)." Drop "2016" as the date of the three contractors (they date from 2009–10 and were the existing supply that the 2019 order restrained). Change "the 2017 ready-to-cook tender was framed the same way" to "the 2017 RTC tender carried the same 25% turnover bar and a 27-machine list; the tender excluded private contractors, and its award was not reported." strongestCounter: add that the Commissioner's own report says the political-contractor nexus is "not specifically proven", and that the pattern is multi-state and spans both Congress-NCP and BJP governments. Add denial: "State WCD did not respond to Scroll (2017); in court the State conceded it must follow the Union policy (para 50); no response from the three sanstha on record." c032: fix "awarded" in the 2016 tender. The award to the three sanstha predates 2016, so the label should read "2009/10 THR contracts (continued until the 2019 order)" unless an award document for the 2016 tender is produced.

verdicts.dateTest: The claim as a sentence: <state governments (MP BJP; Maharashtra Mahayuti)> <used SHG cadre as intake> <for Ladli Behna (from Mar 2023) and Ladki Bahin (GR 28 Jun 2024, intake Jul–Aug 2024)>. For Maharashtra the dates line up. The Mahayuti government was in office. PTI Latur, 16 Jul 2024, reports SHG CRPs being "roped in". Shiv Sena's Nirupam (PTI, 30 Jul 2024) notes the scheme "was launched months before the Assembly elections". For MP no act is dated at all: the file's own void (line ~780/2437) says no document shows SHGs or Aajeevika in Ladli Behna registration. The PIB source is a 22 Jul 2025 LS reply with capitalisation figures to 30 Jun 2025. It is cumulative since 2011 and national, and it does not date any registration role. So the date test passes for Maharashtra and fails (no act to date) for Ladli Behna.
verdicts.identityTest: Partial. The Nashik page lists "Community Resource Person (CRP)" next to "CMM (City Mission Manager)". CMM is a DAY-NULM urban post. So the CRP in that list may be urban NULM cadre and not rural MSRLM/Umed cadre, but both are SHG cadre. The file's "CRP = SHG cadre" step was only its own inference. It is now independently supported by PTI (Latur, 16 Jul 2024): "motivators (CRPs) from women's self-help groups are being roped in to expedite the processing of applications" (https://theprint.in/india/more-than-81000-applications-received-in-latur-under-mazi-ladki-bahin-scheme/2177562/). The ₹58,714.44 cr is national DAY-NRLM rural RF/CIF capitalisation that is on-lent to members. It is not money spent building the intake cadre, and it is not Maharashtra-specific or NULM. Linking it to the Nashik intake list is a conjunction.
verdicts.baseRate: Non-discriminating, at 80% or more. In Maharashtra, SHG CRPs were one channel among about 12 on the Nashik list: anganwadi sevika, supervisor, chief sevika, Setu kendra, gram sevika, CRP, ASHA, ward officer, CMM, balwadi sevika, help desk and Aaple Sarkar. PTI Latur lists anganwadi and ASHA workers, gram sevaks, ration shopkeepers, talathis, agriculture assistants and SHG coordinators. In practice every village-level public functionary was drafted, and SHG cadre are not singled out. The original GR (28 Jun 2024, per PTI via ThePrint) named only anganwadi sevika, gram sevak and ward officer. Using frontline cadre for intake is the normal way any state delivers a mass DBT scheme. The file says opposition-run states (Karnataka guarantees) do the same, but no source was opened for that, so the control is asserted, not tested.
verdicts.denialFound: None found; not asked. No statement from Maharashtra WCD (Minister Aditi Tatkare) or MSRLM/Umed on the CRP role was located. No statement from the MP government or MP Aajeevika Mission either, and none was needed there because no act is documented. The absence is the record. WebSearch budget was exhausted, and Bing, DDG, Brave and Mojeek were blocked or rate-limited. The checks were done by site search on ThePrint and the Google News RSS index. A Hindu story headlined "Anganwadi workers await dues for role in Ladki Bahin scheme roll-out" (2 Jan 2025) was indexed but could not be opened (403/429). It may bear on a per-form honorarium.
verdicts.innocentReading: A newly announced mass DBT scheme had about 2.4 crore target women and a tight intake window. The district administration drafted every village-level public functionary it had for offline form-filling: anganwadi, ASHA, gram sevak, talathi, ration shop, agriculture assistant and SHG CRP. The SHG cadre was used because it reaches the poorest women and is literate in the scheme's KYC requirements. No fee was charged, and nothing shows party direction, targets for particular voters, or cadre choosing whom to enrol. The election timing is a fact about the scheme, not about the SHG network.
verdicts.reason: Both sources say what the file says they say. The Nashik page reads: "the facility of filling online / offline application will be available with Anganwadi Sevika/.../Community Resource Person (CRP)/Asha Sevika/.../Aaple Sarkar Seva Kendra. No fee will be charged for this application." The PIB reply reads: "As of 30th June 2025, a total of Rs. 58714.44 Crore of capitalization support has been provided to SHGs and their federations since inception." But neither source says what the claim says. The claim bundles three things. (1) Ladli Behna: nothing supports this, and the file itself records a void. (2) "Ruling-party" machinery: no party direction, no targets and no per-form honorarium are documented. The PTI line was written by the scheme's own party spokesman, which shows political ownership of the scheme, not party control of SHGs. (3) A thin true core: in Maharashtra, SHG CRPs were one of about 12 intake channels (documented by the district portal and reported by PTI). That core fails the base-rate test, because every available village functionary was used. The Karnataka control is asserted without a source. As worded, the claim is a conjunction that implies partisan capture, which none of its sources states. Only the thin Maharashtra descriptive version survives, as an analytic linkage with an innocentReading.

verdicts.dateTest: Written out, the claim is: MHA (as FCRA administrator) put OSF in the prior-reference category in 2016. The date holds. The MHA affidavit quoted in the Delhi HC order of 21.02.2023 (W.P.(C) 238/2020, https://indiankanoon.org/doc/167147408/) says MHA "under section 46 of the FCRA, 2010 directed the Reserve Bank of India ... vide this Ministry's letter dated 30th May, 2016". RBI then relayed it to banks by letter DBR.AML.No.15320/14.08.001/2015-16 dated 07.06.2016, and Punjab National Bank issued a circular on 14.06.2016. The Hindu reported the listing at the time (published 2016-06-09, https://www.thehindu.com/news/national/Three-American-donors-put-under-watch-list/article14392124.ece). The Tribune piece is dated 2025-03-19 and says "2016", which matches. 'from' can be narrowed to 2016-05-30. On the relevant timeline, 13 of the 21 listed donors were added under the NDA and 8 under the UPA.
verdicts.identityTest: The entity name is loose but the node holds. The Tribune calls it "Open Source Foundation (OSF)", which is a misnomer. TOI (2025-03-19) names "Open Society Institute, US". The RBI/PNB text says MHA decided to add "Open Society Foundation (OSF), World Movement for Democracy (WMD) and National Endowment for Democracy (NED), United States of America" for not allowing credits without prior approval. The petitioner in the Delhi HC case is "Open Society Institute as registered owner of the trademark Open Society Foundations", joined by Open Society Foundation London and Foundation to Promote Open Society. The listing therefore covers the OSF network through its US legal entity (OSI), so the edge target ngo:open-society-foundations is acceptable if the node records OSI, OSF London and FPOS as covered legal entities. The actor is MHA, Foreigners Division, FCRA Wing, acting under s.46 FCRA 2010. Correct.
verdicts.baseRate: This is not discriminating as evidence of targeting OSF. In 2016, 21 foreign donors were under the prior-permission category: 8 added under the UPA and 13 under the NDA (The Hindu 2016-06-09). Two other US democracy-promotion donors, NED and WMD, were added in the same order. Ford (2015) and Compassion International and FFWPU (March 2016) were added in the same period. Among foreign donors that fund rights or advocacy work, the listing is common. The Gates Foundation and the Sangh-linked US charities are not listed, which the file already records in symmetryCheck.
verdicts.denialFound: OSF challenged the listing in court rather than denying it. OSF filed W.P.(C) 238/2020 in the Delhi HC in January 2020. It challenges the unpublished MHA/RBI circulars of 15.01.2015 and 07.06.2016 on two grounds: they were not notified in the Gazette as required by s.11(3)/46, and they reach remittances that are not foreign contribution. It also asked for the reasons for the listing and why no prior notice was given. OSF spokesperson Jonathan Birchall told The Hindu: "The Open Society Foundations confirm the filing of a petition in the Delhi High Court ... will be making no further statement on the matter" (https://www.thehindu.com/news/national/george-soros-open-society-foundations-moves-hc-against-mha/article61638640.ece). MHA's stated ground, from its affidavit: "incriminating reports from security agencies against the Open Society Foundation, which impinges on the our national security"; the material was filed in a sealed envelope. The case was still pending on 06.01.2026 (https://indiankanoon.org/doc/185169269/). The court asked the Union to say whether the circulars apply only to FCRA-covered remittances and listed the matter for 15.04.2026. I did not find an OSF statement on the 2025 ED searches; my web search budget was exhausted, so this is not a finding that none exists.
verdicts.innocentReading: This is a routine use of s.46 FCRA, which MHA has applied to about 21 foreign donors across both governments, including two other US democracy-promotion funders in the same order. The practical effect is that each remittance to an Indian association needs MHA clearance; it is not a ban. MHA says the trigger was intelligence input. The Hindu (2016) reports the alleged conduct as funding associations not registered under FCRA. No court has tested either the ground or the listing.
verdicts.reason: The underlying fact stands, but the claim's stated evidentiary position is false, and the tier depends on that position. The claim says the listing is "known only via ED's 2025 account; the order and stated ground not opened". In fact, (1) The Hindu reported it on 2016-06-09 with the co-listed donors and the "adverse intelligence inputs" ground. (2) A Delhi HC order dated 21.02.2023 in OSI v Union of India, W.P.(C) 238/2020, quotes the RBI letter of 07.06.2016 citing the MHA decision under s.46 and the MHA affidavit giving the date (30.05.2016) and the ground ("incriminating reports from security agencies ... national security"). (3) OSF confirmed its challenge on the record in 2020. A court order plus two independent credible outlets (The Hindu 2016 and TOI/Tribune 2025) meets the documented tier. The 'reported' tier and the "only via ED" framing should go, and the existing gap entry is closed by these sources.
verdicts.corrections:
1. Change tier from reported to documented.
2. Replace text/d with: "MHA, by letter to RBI dated 2016-05-30 under s.46 FCRA 2010, directed that remittances from 'Open Society Foundation (OSF) ... USA' (with NED and WMD) be credited only after MHA clearance; RBI relayed this to banks on 2016-06-07 (DBR.AML.No.15320/14.08.001/2015-16). MHA's stated ground (affidavit in Delhi HC W.P.(C) 238/2020): 'incriminating reports from security agencies ... impinges on national security', with material in a sealed envelope. OSF (as Open Society Institute, with OSF London and FPOS) has challenged the circulars since January 2020 as unpublished and over-broad; the case was pending as of 2026-01-06."
3. Set from = "2016-05-30".
4. Add sources: https://indiankanoon.org/doc/167147408/ (DHC order 21.02.2023); https://indiankanoon.org/doc/185169269/ (DHC order 06.01.2026); https://www.thehindu.com/news/national/Three-American-donors-put-under-watch-list/article14392124.ece (2016-06-09); https://www.thehindu.com/news/national/george-soros-open-society-foundations-moves-hc-against-mha/article61638640.ece; TOI 2025-03-19 https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/india/ed-searches-bengaluru-offices-of-soross-foundation-and-entities-linked-to-it/articleshow/119185811.cms. Keep the Tribune but note that it misnames the entity as "Open Source Foundation".
5. Add innocentReading: "one of ~21 donors under s.46 prior reference (8 under UPA, 13 under NDA); NED and WMD were listed in the same order."
6. Add contra/response: OSF's pending Delhi HC petition and the Birchall statement.
7. Change killIf to "Delhi HC quashes the 2016 circulars or MHA withdraws the listing". Change upgradeIf to "the 30.05.2016 MHA letter itself is released, or the DHC reaches a final judgment".
8. Follow-on fixes in the same file: close the gap entry "2016 MHA order ... not found; known only through ED's 2025 account and a 2020 Delhi HC petition reported by a partisan outlet". The petition is in the DHC record and was reported by The Hindu, not only by a partisan outlet. Also change "(reported)" to "(documented)" in the OSF entity 'sub', 'publicRole' and facts, and in the Soros narrative strongestCase.

verdicts.dateTest: Pass. Restated: the ED searched eight Bengaluru premises linked to Soros' EDF/SEDF and OSF on Tuesday 18 March 2025 (a Tuesday, checked). The Tribune published at 2025-03-19T03:30+05:30 and says "The Enforcement Directorate (ED) on Tuesday conducted searches at eight premises in Bengaluru". The News Minute also gives "Tuesday, March 18" and Scroll also has "on Tuesday". The 2016 prior-reference listing comes before the alleged workaround, so the order of events holds. Nothing has been adjudicated as of 2026-09. Setting the claim start date to 2025-03-18 is correct.
verdicts.identityTest: Mostly passes. Three things to note. (1) The Tribune names the wrong entity: it calls it "Open Source Foundation (OSF)" and "Economic Development Fund (EDF)". Scroll names it correctly: "the Open Society Foundations was placed under the 'Prior Reference Category' by the Ministry of Home Affairs in 2016". So ngo:open-society-foundations is the right node, but the record should say the Tribune misnamed it. (2) The reports do not show that OSF's own offices were searched. The premises named are Aspada Investments Pvt Ltd ("investment adviser-cum-fund manager of Soros Economic Development Fund (SEDF) in India", which Scroll calls "a wholly owned subsidiary of a Mauritius entity"), Rootbridge Services Pvt Ltd and ASAR Social Advisor Pvt Ltd (per TNM). No CIN is given for any of them. The edge should name SEDF/Aspada as the entity searched, and OSF as the entity the allegation is about. (3) The FDI/consultancy allegation comes from unnamed "ED sources", not an ED press release or a named officer.
verdicts.baseRate: The allegation does not single OSF out, so it tells us little about intent. The 2016 MHA prior-reference measures also hit other large foreign donors, including Compassion International (a Christian evangelical donor, not critical of the government) and, for a time, the Ford Foundation. ED FEMA searches are routine: the agency runs thousands of FEMA cases. Moving foreign money into India as FDI into for-profit companies plus consultancy fees is the normal structure for any foreign impact investor, including Omidyar, Gates-linked vehicles and SEDF. That structure only becomes a problem if the money ends up paying for NGO activity. The discriminating question is the end use, and that is exactly what has not been adjudicated. Symmetry check against the SPEC controls: I found no reporting of equivalent FEMA searches on the Indian vehicles of government-neutral or aligned foreign donors. That gap is consistent with selective enforcement, but it does not prove it.
verdicts.denialFound: None found. The Tribune, Scroll (https://scroll.in/latest/1080421/ed-raids-eight-george-soros-linked-entities-in-bengaluru) and The News Minute (https://www.thenewsminute.com/karnataka/bengaluru-ed-raids-eight-locations-linked-to-george-soros-open-source-foundation) carry no statement from OSF, SEDF or Aspada, and none says it contacted them. So in the reports I checked they were not asked. I found no statement in the OSF newsroom or in Google News results. WebSearch was over budget, so the search for a response was partial.
verdicts.innocentReading: SEDF invests in Indian for-profit companies through Aspada, which is its SEBI/RBI-regulated fund manager and wholly owned by a Mauritius entity. This is lawful FDI and can go through the automatic route. Consultancy fees paid to Indian advisory firms such as ASAR are ordinary services income. The 2016 prior-reference listing controls FCRA donations to NGOs, not FDI into companies. The funds contravene FEMA only if they can be shown to have paid for NGO activity in breach of end-use conditions. ED has asserted that through unnamed sources and has not proved it. No show-cause notice or adjudication order has been published.
verdicts.reason: The one source was opened and quoted, and it says what the claim says: the date, eight premises, FEMA, the 2016 prior-reference category, and the FDI plus consultancy-fee workaround attributed to "ED sources". Scroll and The News Minute independently confirm it. The allegation is unadjudicated and comes only from unnamed agency sources, so tier "alleged" is right for the FEMA-violation part, and there is a contra edge (c010). The fact that the searches happened would qualify as documented, since at least three outlets report it. Nothing in the chronology, the identity of the entities, or the sources refutes the claim. The weaknesses are a naming error in the source, OSF being treated as the searched entity when the premises searched were SEDF/Aspada and linked firms, and a missing innocentReading.
verdicts.corrections: 1. Add second and third sources: ["Scroll 2025-03-18","https://scroll.in/latest/1080421/ed-raids-eight-george-soros-linked-entities-in-bengaluru"] and ["The News Minute 2025-03-19","https://www.thenewsminute.com/karnataka/bengaluru-ed-raids-eight-locations-linked-to-george-soros-open-source-foundation"]. 2. In "d", note that the Tribune misnames OSF as "Open Source Foundation" and that the allegation comes from unnamed "ED sources", not an ED release. 3. Name the premises searched (Aspada Investments Pvt Ltd, Rootbridge Services Pvt Ltd, ASAR Social Advisor Pvt Ltd) and state that the reports do not show OSF's own office being searched. Consider pointing the enforcement edge at an SEDF/Aspada node and keeping OSF as the subject of the allegation. 4. Fill innocentReading: lawful FDI into for-profit companies plus consultancy fees; prior-reference controls FCRA donations, not FDI; a violation depends on unproven end use. 5. Change c010 "d" from "asked/not asked unknown" to "No response recorded; Tribune, Scroll and TNM reports carry no OSF/SEDF/Aspada comment and do not say they were contacted (not asked, per available reporting)". 6. Optionally split the fact of the searches (documented, three outlets) from the FEMA allegation (alleged). 7. Keep upgradeIf and killIf as written.

verdicts.dateTest: Claim restated: "Omidyar Network (India arm) made equity investments and grants in India from 2010, and announced on 2023-12-11 (US time) that it would exit." TechCrunch is bylined "Manish Singh 10:11 PM PST · December 11, 2023", which is 2023-12-12 in IST. Business Today is "Updated Dec 12, 2023 7:27 PM IST". Both carry the start year: TC says "since first making investments there in 2010" and BT says "began its investment activities in India in 2010". The exit date overlaps the actor's window. The field "to":"2024-12" is only the planned end ("will completely transition out of the market by the end of 2024", BT). None of the sources I opened confirm the exit was actually completed, and Inc42/Outlook report a 3–5 year horizon for exiting portfolio holdings. So 2024-12 is a stated intention, not an observed end date. The US$673m is dated "As of July this year" (2023-07), which fits the window.
verdicts.identityTest: The entity is resolved only by its name. Both sources name "Omidyar Network India" / "Omidyar Network" (backed by Pierre Omidyar). The Indian advisory entity's CIN is not verified (the record says so). ONI is the donor, not an FCRA registrant, so it has no FCRA number. There is no identity collision. The target does not match, though. "ngo:domestic-grantees-aggregate" is labelled as grantees, but BT says ~70% of the money was equity in start-ups (Indifi, Doubtnut, FarMart, DrinkPrime…), and those are not grantees.
verdicts.baseRate: The claim carries no accusation, so there is no discriminating property to test. Foreign funders winding down country programmes are common, and Omidyar Network has closed other geographies before. The SPEC's domestic-philanthropy control puts the scale in context: ONI's >US$500m deployed over 13 years (~30% grants, i.e. about US$150m) is small next to annual Azim Premji Foundation or Tata Trusts spending. The same lens applied to a domestic foundation would record the same kind of edge, so the reading is symmetric.
verdicts.denialFound: No denial is needed, because the claim reports the firm's own statement. The firm was asked: TC says "The firm didn't respond to a request for comment Monday but confirmed the development after the publication of this story." It gave the market-maturity reason and said it had "achieved our primary objective of catalysing impact". The firm's own statement page (omidyargroup.com) returns 404 (recorded as a void).
verdicts.innocentReading: A global impact investor closed a 13-year country programme after India's domestic VC and philanthropy grew. Its 2023 write-downs (Doubtnut, ZestMoney) also made the programme less attractive. The claim as worded implies no wrongdoing and makes no enforcement-causation assertion; that question sits separately in c013 as analytic.
verdicts.reason: Every element of the claim appears word for word in the sources: start year 2010; "about $673 million of cumulative assets under management" as of July 2023 (TC, citing an investor presentation); exit announced 11/12 December 2023; the market-maturity reason ("significant change in context… more Indian led philanthropic and venture capital than ever before"); and the end-2024 transition (BT). The claim does not stack facts to imply something the sources don't say. Tier "reported" is right for a grant/investment edge whose amount comes second-hand from an investor presentation and a press summary. The announcement facts alone could reach documented, since TC, BT, Business Standard and YourStory each covered them. The claim survives, but its fields need fixing: the predicate and target mislabel mostly-equity capital as grants, the record wrongly says no grant amount was stated, and the AUM figure is not a flow to grantees.
verdicts.corrections:
1. Claim "d" says "Amount not stated as grants". That is wrong. BT states: "It has invested over $500 million in India, of which 70 percent is equity investment and 30 per cent is grants." Replace it with that sentence, and give the implied grant figure as ~US$150m (≈₹1,250 cr at ~83 INR/USD, 2023; marked as derived). Set benefit.amountCr to that derived figure or leave it null with a note; set benefit.confidence to "low".
2. Keep US$673m labelled as cumulative AUM (TC, investor presentation, 2023-07). It is not grants or disbursements. Do not put it in "a".
3. Pred "grant" plus target "domestic-grantees-aggregate" misstates a mix that was ~70% equity. Either split the edge into invest→start-up portfolio (~70%) and grant→grantees (~30%), or change pred to a generic fund/invest predicate and relabel the target.
4. Change "to":"2024-12" to be marked as the planned transition date ("announced intent; completion not verified"). Portfolio exits were reported to run on a 3–5 year horizon.
5. The entity "d" line cites BT for the "several months of deliberation" statement. That phrase appears in TC only, not in BT. Cite TC alone for it; BT does carry the market-maturity quote.
6. Add Business Standard (https://www.business-standard.com/companies/news/omidyar-network-decides-to-exit-indian-market-after-a-decade-of-operations-123121200399_1.html) as an independent outlet for the exit announcement.
7. innocentReading is null. It should be filled with the market-maturity/portfolio-strategy reading, even though the claim is not accusatory.

verdicts.dateTest: Claim: the CBI (actor) put Omidyar Network and nine other NGOs under scrutiny for alleged FCRA violations in 2022. The date holds. TechCrunch (11 Dec 2023) says: "The move comes a year after Omidyar Network and nine other NGOs came under the radar of India's Central Bureau of Investigation ... over alleged violation of the nation's Foreign Contribution Regulation Act." Google News RSS dates the underlying event to 11–12 May 2022, with these headlines: The Hindu, "CBI names 'promoters of NGO Omidyar' in FIR"; NDTV, "10 NGOs Under CBI Scanner In Foreign Regulation Act Bribe Case"; Rediff, "CBI names Omidyar among 10 NGOs in FCRA scam case"; Indian Express, "CBI arrests 6 MHA officials, 8 others in FCRA corruption case". Omidyar Network India was operating in India throughout this window (it announced its exit in Dec 2023), so the dates overlap. The insider-trading matter is dated June 2021 (Inc42), which is before the CBI case, and it was a SEBI matter.
verdicts.identityTest: This part partly fails. (1) Inc42 names SEBI, not the CBI, as the agency in the insider-trading matter: "in June 2021, SEBI alleged that Franklin Templeton's Asia Pacific head Vivek Kudva and his wife Roopa — ONI's former managing partner — had violated insider trading laws." The record's `d` field says "a CBI probe involving a former managing partner over alleged insider trading", which gets the agency wrong. The matter concerned Roopa Kudva personally, over Franklin Templeton debt-fund redemptions, and was not an ONI enforcement matter. (2) The Hindu's headline says the FIR names "promoters of NGO Omidyar", and PGurus says "India promoters of Omidyar Network". So the named accused may be persons connected to Omidyar or its Indian vehicle (Omidyar Network India Advisors Pvt Ltd, a for-profit advisory company, not an FCRA NGO), not "Omidyar Network" as such. The edge target `ngo:omidyar-network-india` needs to state which entity or persons the FIR names. I could not open the FIR text or the article bodies to settle this. (3) Inc42 also says "Central Bureau of Intelligence", which is a garble of Central Bureau of Investigation.
verdicts.baseRate: The property is discriminating. About 10 NGOs were named in one CBI FIR, out of roughly 16,000 active FCRA registrants (well under 1%). The May 2022 case was mainly an anti-corruption case against officials in the MHA's FCRA division and middlemen (6 MHA officials and 8 others arrested). The NGOs were named as alleged bribe-givers seeking clearances. It was not a general FCRA compliance sweep. I found nothing equivalent under UPA (the SPEC control): the 2012 Kudankulam-linked action was cancellations, not a CBI bribery FIR. So on the evidence in hand the symmetry question is unresolved, not answered either way.
verdicts.denialFound: None found. Omidyar's public exit statement (quoted in TechCrunch) gives only "significant change in context" and the growth of Indian capital, and does not mention the CBI case. Inc42 says it has no statement from Omidyar on the investigations. Neither source says whether Omidyar was asked about the FIR. So the record is: none found, not shown to have been asked.
verdicts.innocentReading: This was a bribery case centred on MHA FCRA-division officials and middlemen, who allegedly took hawala payments to clear registrations and renewals (ThePrint headline: "Fake invoices, impersonation, hawala bribes: How 'nexus' of officials & NGOs ran FCRA scam"). NGOs and their "promoters" may have been named in the FIR because they appeared in middlemen's client records, without any finding that they paid bribes. An FIR is an unadjudicated allegation, and I found no chargesheet or conviction against Omidyar. Omidyar's Indian vehicle was mainly a for-profit impact investor using FDI plus advisory fees, a structure that does not itself depend on FCRA registration.
verdicts.reason: The central fact holds. Two independent credible outlets say the CBI took action in 2022 and named Omidyar among about 10 NGOs in an FCRA-related case: TechCrunch in quoted text, and Inc42: "Omidyar was named as an accused by the Central Bureau of Intelligence (CBI) for allegedly conspiring to illegally facilitate the registration and renewal of ... FCRA licences". Contemporaneous headlines from The Hindu, NDTV and Rediff corroborate it. But the claim as written is wrong in two ways. (a) It says "no FIR ... located", yet The Hindu's headline (11 May 2022) is "CBI names 'promoters of NGO Omidyar' in FIR", and Inc42 says Omidyar was "named as an accused". (b) Its `d` field turns a SEBI insider-trading allegation against Roopa Kudva personally into a "CBI probe". It also calls the matter "alleged FCRA violations" when the case was an FCRA bribery/corruption FIR against MHA officials and middlemen. The claim therefore needs correction before it can stand. After correction, "reported" fits the existence of the enforcement action. Any statement that Omidyar committed wrongdoing must stay at "alleged" with a contra, because nothing has been adjudicated.
verdicts.corrections:
Suggested field fixes:
- text/lab: "CBI named 'promoters of' Omidyar Network (India) among ~10 NGOs in its May 2022 FIR on alleged bribery by MHA FCRA-division officials and middlemen for FCRA registrations/renewals; no chargesheet or outcome located."
- Delete "no FIR located".
- In `d`, replace "a CBI probe involving a former managing partner over alleged insider trading" with "a June 2021 SEBI insider-trading order against Roopa Kudva (ONI's former managing partner) and her husband Vivek Kudva, concerning Franklin Templeton — a personal matter unrelated to ONI".
