Do not link Gujarat HC WP(PIL) 97/2016, which is unrelated. 5. killIf: keep "Order quashed", and add "MHA order text shows a different ground". 6. Entity ngo:navsarjan-trust: fill in identity.fcra with the FCRA registration number when it is found.

verdicts.dateTest: Claim: the MHA (FCRA wing, Foreigners Division) cancelled Environics Trust's FCRA registration by an order dated 2024-03-04. The source (Devdiscourse carrying PTI, New Delhi, 2024-04-05 14:18 IST) quotes the court: "The petitioner has approached this court challenging an order dated March 4, 2024 cancelling the registration under FCRA." MHA administers FCRA without interruption, so there is no tenure-window problem. The date sequence is consistent: CBI FIR in January 2024, cancellation 2024-03-04, High Court notice 2024-04-05, listing 2024-05-10. A later primary record exists: Delhi HC order of 2026-05-15 (Kaurav J) in W.P.(C) 9059/2023 and W.P.(C) 5004/2024 (Environics Trust v Union of India, https://indiankanoon.org/doc/196640405/). It shows the challenge still pending, listed for 2026-08-04, with no quashing. So `to: null` is correct as of 2026-05.
verdicts.identityTest: The target matches: the source names "NGO Environics Trust", and the 2026 High Court order names the petitioner "ENVIRONICS TRUST" (Sr. Adv. Rakesh Khanna). The FCRA registration number is not in the source. The actor is inferred. The source says "the Centre" and the 2024 petition's respondent is "Union of India The Secretary". Attributing it to MHA's FCRA wing (Foreigners Division) is the standard reading, but the source does not name that unit. There is also a discrepancy about what kind of action this was. The 2026-05-15 High Court order describes the subject of both petitions as "The rejection of the petitioner's FCRA renewal application", not a s.14 cancellation. PTI (2024) calls it cancellation. The 2026 wording may simply cover both petitions together (the 2023 and 2024 actions), but whether the March 2024 order was a cancellation or a refusal to renew is not fully settled.
verdicts.baseRate: Loss of FCRA registration is common: over 20,000 cancellations since 2011, and 5,933 associations ceased registration on 2022-01-01 alone. So the event itself does not discriminate between critics and non-critics. That does not weaken this edge, which only records that one enforcement event happened. It supports no inference about targeting. The SPEC controls (VIF, India Foundation, Azim Premji, Tata, Reliance, Adani Foundation) have no comparable action in the file. Any selectivity reading belongs in analytic claims (c099, c018), not here.
verdicts.denialFound: The Trust's response is in the source. Its senior counsel told the Delhi HC on 2024-04-05: "They have to give us a personal hearing before they pass the order of cancellation. There was no hearing given to us." (https://www.devdiscourse.com/article/law-order/2878882-hc-seeks-centres-stand-on-plea-by-environics-trust-against-fcra-cancellation). The Trust is challenging the order, not denying it exists. MHA/Centre: the court asked for a reply within four weeks, but no public MHA statement was found. Asked (by the court); no reply on the public record.
verdicts.innocentReading: The boring explanation: a routine FCRA regulatory action following a CBI FIR over 2018 transfers and alleged use of funds for purposes other than those declared. It sits in the same post-2020 wave of cancellations and non-renewals that hit thousands of associations. The edge claims nothing beyond the cancellation and the Trust's procedural objection, so this reading does not conflict with it.
verdicts.reason: The one source, a PTI wire carried by Devdiscourse, states the exact fact, date and target, and records the Trust's response. A 2026 Delhi HC order confirms the litigation over Environics Trust's FCRA status is real and still pending, which rules out quashing so far. The claim is not refuted. It stays at reported rather than documented: syndicated copies of PTI are not independent outlets, the order text itself was not opened, and the 2026 order calls the action a renewal rejection, which leaves its legal type slightly unsettled. The search budget ran out, and the direct site searches that followed (LiveLaw, The Wire, Bar & Bench) found no second independent outlet.
verdicts.corrections: 1) Add to `d`: "Delhi HC W.P.(C) 5004/2024 (with W.P.(C) 9059/2023) still pending. Order of 2026-04-15 directed MHA, without prejudice, to consider an application for fresh registration. Order of 2026-05-15 (Kaurav J) describes the subject as 'rejection of the petitioner's FCRA renewal application', asks MHA for a sealed-cover report, and lists the case for 2026-08-04." Add the source ["Indian Kanoon — Environics Trust v Union of India, Delhi HC, 2026-05-15", "https://indiankanoon.org/doc/196640405/"]. 2) Note in `d` that the source names the actor as "the Centre" and that the Foreigners Division attribution is inferred. 3) Flag the ambiguity between cancellation (s.14) and refusal to renew (s.16), and word the `lab` as "cancellation (per PTI) of FCRA registration". 4) Change `upgradeIf` to "Text of the 2024-03-04 MHA order, or a Delhi HC order in W.P.(C) 5004/2024 reciting it, or a second independent outlet". Keep `killIf` as "Order quashed/set aside". 5) Replace the stale "hearing 2024-05-10 on interim relief" with the 2026 status.

verdicts.dateTest: Claim as a sentence: CBI (named agency) alleged in an FIR registered January 2024 (ThePrint: registered Tue 2024-01-16, reported 2024-01-19) that Environics Trust transferred Rs 1,250 each to 711 people on 2020-11-15. The Trust held FCRA registration in 2020. It was suspended in 2023 and cancelled on 2024-03-04, so the alleged act falls inside the registration window, and the FIR comes before the cancellation. The Devdiscourse/PTI copy is internally inconsistent: it says the FIR covers "several bank transfers carried out in 2018" and then gives the 15 November 2020 transfer. The claim correctly uses 2020-11-15, and ThePrint confirms "on 15 November, 2020". The record is stale: CBI filed a chargesheet on 2025-01-24 before a special court in New Delhi (ThePrint/PTI, Business Standard), and the claim does not mention it. That meets the claim's own upgradeIf ("Chargesheet"), although a chargesheet is still unadjudicated.
verdicts.identityTest: Entity matches. Every source names "Environics Trust" (New Delhi NGO; FIR accused managing director Ramamurthi Sreedhar, who died 2023-12-29, and finance director Vanitha Sreedhar). The chargesheet names Environics Trust, Vanitha Sreedhar, Nishant Kumar Alag and Prasanta Kumar Paikray under IPC 120-B, 417, 468 and 471 plus FCRA. No FCRA registration number was cited or checked (fcraonline is blocked). Subject problem: the edge's s is "agencies", but the source names the actor specifically as CBI. The cancellation (c090) is MHA's; the FIR allegation is CBI's.
verdicts.baseRate: This does not turn on a base rate. The claim is one specific, quantified allegation (711 x Rs 1,250 = Rs 8,88,750, so a = 0.0889 crore is arithmetically correct), not a shared property. Symmetry: the "diversion to protests" ground is not unique to this government or to critics. Under the UPA, the 2012 Kudankulam cluster and INSAF were actioned on the same kind of ground, and CPSC got a CBI FCRA FIR in 2022. The SPEC control (critical versus aligned associations) would record an identical CBI allegation against a neutral body the same way. The claim carries no framing by family, religion or ethnicity.
verdicts.denialFound: None found, and the Trust was asked. PTI emailed Environics Trust about both the FIR (2024-01) and the chargesheet (2025-01): "An email sent to ET by PTI seeking a response on the development remained unanswered by the time of filing this story." ThePrint (2024-01-19) also wrote: "ThePrint has reached Environics Trust on email for comment. This report will be updated if and when a response is received." The only recorded position is a procedural one from counsel in the Delhi HC on 2024-04-05: "They have to give us a personal hearing before they pass the order of cancellation. There was no hearing given to us" (Devdiscourse/PTI). That is not a denial of the payments.
verdicts.innocentReading: Dhinkia is in Jagatsinghpur district, which was reportedly among the Odisha coastal districts hit by Cyclone Amphan (May 2020). The same 711 villagers could have been genuinely cyclone-affected relief recipients and also participants in the long-running anti-JSW (formerly POSCO) agitation. A relief disbursement six months after the cyclone, made to residents of a protest village, fits both readings. CBI's case that the money was "actually paid to the protesters for JSW agitation" has not been tested in court.
verdicts.reason: The one cited source (Devdiscourse, syndicated PTI copy, 2024-04-05) states the claim almost verbatim: "According to the CBI, Environics Trust had allegedly transferred Rs 1,250 each in the bank accounts of 711 people on November 15, 2020, for distribution among Amphan cyclone-affected people in Odisha but actually the payments were made to protestors for JSW agitation at Dhinkia, Odisha." ThePrint (2024-01-19) confirms it independently. The claim is worded as an allegation, attributed to the CBI FIR and marked not adjudicated, so "alleged" is the correct tier. Nothing refutes it. The fixes needed are the actor field, a stale status (a chargesheet was filed 2025-01-24) and the contra, which should record that the Trust was asked and did not answer.
verdicts.corrections: 1) s: change "agencies" to the CBI entity (e.g., "ngo:cbi" / "agency:cbi"). 2) lab/text: say "Amphan cyclone relief" rather than generic "Odisha cyclone relief", to match the source. 3) d: add "CBI chargesheet filed 2025-01-24 before special court, New Delhi, against Environics Trust, Vanitha Sreedhar, Nishant Kumar Alag, Prasanta Kumar Paikray (IPC 120-B/417/468/471 + FCRA); also alleges forged MAA Plasto invoices of Rs 6.50 lakh + Rs 4 lakh; Rs 30,000 to Deme Oram. Not adjudicated." Also note the PTI copy's inconsistent "2018 transfers" line. Tier stays alleged. Keep killIf as "Closure report / discharge / acquittal" and change upgradeIf to "Conviction or court framing of charges". 4) srcs: add ThePrint 2024-01-19 FIR report (https://theprint.in/india/cbi-registers-fir-against-ngo-environics-trust-its-directors-for-funding-agitations-in-odisha/1930188/) and ThePrint/PTI 2025-01-24 chargesheet (https://theprint.in/india/cbi-files-chargesheet-against-ngo-environics-trust-for-fcra-violations/2461234/). 5) contra c092 d: add "Asked: PTI emailed ET (2024-01 and 2025-01) and ThePrint emailed ET (2024-01-19); no response recorded. Counsel's only recorded position is procedural (no personal hearing), not a denial of the payments." 6) Add innocentReading: Jagatsinghpur was an Amphan-affected district, so the recipients may have been both cyclone-affected and protesters.

verdicts.dateTest: The claim reads: MHA (Home Ministry FCRA wing) cancelled Bal Raksha Bharat's FCRA registration in 2023-09. Outlook's article is datePublished 2023-09-15T09:20 IST and names the date only as 'ahead of the September 30 deadline'. The ET original it relays is datePublished 2023-09-14T00:11 IST, so the cancellation happened on or before 13-14 Sept 2023. Unless it happened in late August, 2023-09 fits. The ₹163.18 crore figure is for FY2021-22 and was disclosed in an audited report filed in March 2023, so it comes before the action. The cancellation falls within the NDA government's term. Test passes.
verdicts.identityTest: Both sources name the same NGO. Outlook: "UK-based NGO Save The Children's India unit Bal Raksha Bharat's licence has been revoked." ET: "the government has cancelled the licence of Bal Raksha Bharat, also known as Save The Children". No FCRA registration number is given in either source, so the entity is matched by name only. That match is backed by the organisation's own confirmation (see denialFound). The actor is 'the government' / 'home ministry' per 'officials'. Mapping this to ngo:mha-foreigners-division, the division that houses the FCRA wing, is a reasonable institutional mapping, but no named officer is given. Caution: the co-cancelled 'SEWA' is a North East Delhi animal-husbandry NGO, not the Ahmedabad SEWA. This does not affect c093 but should be checked wherever SEWA appears.
verdicts.baseRate: An FCRA cancellation is not unusual in itself. Parliament was told that 6,677 registrations were cancelled in 2017-21 (quoted in Outlook). ET notes 16,497 active licences in Sept 2023, and a wave of non-renewals and cancellations came around the 30 Sept 2023 deadline. The claim does not assert targeting, only the event and its scale. Scale does discriminate: ₹163 crore a year puts Bal Raksha Bharat among the largest FCRA recipients. Symmetry control from the SPEC: UPA also cancelled or blocked registrations on a large scale (about 4,000+ in 2012 for non-filing, plus the Kudankulam-linked cases). So the fact of a cancellation alone says nothing about which government is doing it. The claim does not frame a family, religion or ethnicity as the actor.
verdicts.denialFound: No denial. The party was asked and confirmed the cancellation. ET, 2023-09-14, Rahul Tripathi (https://economictimes.indiatimes.com/news/india/home-ministry-cancels-fcra-licence-of-bal-trust/articleshow/103643895.cms): "A senior functionary of the trust confirmed that its FCRA licence has been cancelled but did not elaborate further." No public statement from Bal Raksha Bharat or Save the Children disputing the grounds was found. Further web search was blocked by the search budget.
verdicts.innocentReading: This may be a routine refusal or cancellation in the 30 Sept 2023 re-registration round after the 2020 FCRA amendments, for a technical or compliance reason (for example, the post-2020 SBI New Delhi FCRA account or utilisation-for-administration limits). It need not be a finding of misuse. The source's 'misuse or diversion' sentence is generic background on the law ("Any misuse or diversion of foreign funds by NGOs is considered a violation"). It is not a ground attributed to this NGO. The ₹163.18 crore figure is total bank receipts from an audited report. It shows size, not wrongdoing, and the source does not explicitly call it foreign contribution.
verdicts.reason: The source holds up. Outlook states the cancellation and the amount: "Bal Raksha Bharat's licence has been revoked... it had received Rs 163.18 crore in its bank accounts and Rs 66.66 lakh worth of in-kind contributions for the year 2021-22, ET reported". Outlook says 'reportedly' and relays ET's story rather than reporting independently. The ET original (Rahul Tripathi, ET Bureau, 2023-09-14) has 'officials said' sourcing and the exact figure '₹163,18,59,530'. It also has the NGO's own confirmation ("A senior functionary of the trust confirmed that its FCRA licence has been cancelled"). That is one credible outlet with named sourcing plus a party confirmation, which fits 'reported'. It is not 'documented': there are no two independent outlets (Outlook is derivative), and no MHA order or FCRA portal entry was opened. Nothing found shows the order was quashed.
verdicts.corrections:
1. srcs: add the ET original as the primary source, before Outlook: ["ET 2023-09-14 (Rahul Tripathi) — Home ministry cancels FCRA licence of Bal Raksha Bharat; trust functionary confirms", "https://economictimes.indiatimes.com/news/india/home-ministry-cancels-fcra-licence-of-bal-trust/articleshow/103643895.cms"]. Mark Outlook as derivative (it says 'reportedly' / 'ET reported'), not a second independent outlet.
2. d: change 'received in 2021-22' to 'total receipts in bank accounts per audited report filed March 2023 (₹163,18,59,530) plus ₹66,66,444 in kind, FY2021-22; source does not label it foreign contribution'. Replace 'grounds not specified beyond "misuse or diversion of foreign funds"' with 'no ground stated; the misuse/diversion sentence in both sources is generic background, not attributed to this NGO'.
3. from: keep 2023-09, but note 'on or before 2023-09-14 (ET publication)'.
4. c095 (contra): replace 'No response recorded — asked/not asked unknown' with 'Asked; a senior functionary confirmed the cancellation and did not elaborate (ET 2023-09-14)', and add the ET URL.
5. c094: no opened source attributes the misuse/diversion ground to Bal Raksha Bharat. Downgrade to a void/gap or kill it as an edge; do not keep it as an 'alleged ground'.
6. upgradeIf: 'MHA order, FCRA portal cancelled-list entry, or an independent second outlet'.

verdicts.dateTest: The claim reads: MHA Foreigners Division cited misuse or diversion of foreign funds as its ground for cancelling Bal Raksha Bharat's FCRA registration in 2023-09. The actor fits: MHA administers FCRA. The date is wrong. The Outlook piece (published 2023-09-15) rewrites an Economic Times report. The action was reported in early August 2023: Insights 2023-08-04, India CSR 2023-08-05 and LiCAS 2023-08-08, all describing the renewal as rejected and the order posted on MHA's website. So `from` should be 2023-08, not 2023-09. This affects c093 as well.
verdicts.identityTest: The entity is right. Outlook: "UK-based NGO Save The Children's India unit Bal Raksha Bharat's licence has been revoked." The FCRA registration number is not recorded (identity.fcra is null), and it should be added from the MHA order if one can be found.
verdicts.baseRate: Not discriminating, and the claim depends on that. The "misuse or diversion" sentence is the general FCRA test that applies to every registrant. Outlook: "If any misuse or diversion of foreign funds is reported within the NGO, it is considered a violation of the FCRA Act." The Wire has the same boilerplate: "Any misuse or diversion of foreign funds by NGOs is considered a violation of the FCRA Act." A sentence that is true of 100% of FCRA registrants cannot serve as a stated ground against one of them. For the control, the same Wire article names YWCA Delhi as a case where MHA actually cited fund diversion. That is the kind of case-specific attribution this claim lacks.
verdicts.denialFound: Yes, there is a response, so "no response recorded" is wrong. Bal Raksha Bharat's spokesperson "expressed surprise but assured that they would work closely with the government to resolve the matter" and committed to "continuing critical services to the community and children" (India CSR, 2023-08-05, https://indiacsr.in/bal-raksha-bharat-loses-fcra-permit/). The Wire also reports that a senior representative "confirmed the cancellation of its FCRA licence to the business daily, but did not provide further details" (https://m.thewire.in/article/rights/home-ministry-cancels-fcra-licence-of-bal-raksha-bharat-two-other-ngos).
verdicts.innocentReading: The Outlook sentence is explanatory background on how FCRA works, not an MHA ground for this organisation. No opened source states MHA's reason. Where press coverage links the action to anything, it is the November 2022 Ministry of Women and Child Development complaint calling Save the Children's malnutrition fundraising campaign "misleading", plus NCPCR's objection to how children were portrayed. That is a different allegation from fund diversion, and it is press context, not a stated ground in the order. It could also be an ordinary renewal refusal during the 2020–2023 re-registration window, when many renewals were refused.
verdicts.reason: The claim takes a generic sentence from the Outlook article ("If any misuse or diversion of foreign funds is reported within the NGO, it is considered a violation of the FCRA Act") and presents it as MHA's alleged ground against Bal Raksha Bharat. Neither Outlook nor The Wire (which carries the same boilerplate) says MHA cited diversion for this organisation. Under CONTRACT, `alleged` needs a named party making the assertion, and here nobody makes it. The record's own `d` field admits "No specific ground in an opened source." An edge that attributes an unsourced diversion allegation to a named NGO should be killed. The linked contra c095 is also wrong: a spokesperson response exists. The date 2023-09 is wrong too; the action was reported in 2023-08.
verdicts.corrections: 1) Kill c094 and its contra c095. 2) In c093, remove "grounds not specified beyond 'misuse or diversion of foreign funds'" and replace it with "grounds not stated in any opened source; press links it to MWCD's Nov 2022 'misleading' complaint about the malnutrition campaign (context, not a stated ground)". Change `from` from 2023-09 to 2023-08. Add sources: The Wire (https://m.thewire.in/article/rights/home-ministry-cancels-fcra-licence-of-bal-raksha-bharat-two-other-ngos) and India CSR 2023-08-05 (https://indiacsr.in/bal-raksha-bharat-loses-fcra-permit/). Both still trace back to ET, so a genuinely independent second outlet or the MHA order is needed before any upgrade to documented. 3) If a ground-type claim is wanted, create a new `alleged` claim with MWCD, not MHA, as the actor ("MWCD called the Save the Children malnutrition campaign 'misleading', 2022-11-02"). Its contra should quote the Bal Raksha Bharat spokesperson's response. 4) In the entity `sub` field, change "FCRA cancelled 2023-09" to "FCRA renewal rejected / registration cancelled, reported 2023-08-03/04". Add the FCRA registration number if the MHA order can be found.

verdicts.dateTest: Claim: MHA (Foreigners Division, FCRA wing) cancelled the FCRA registrations of three of twelve Kudankulam-area associations in 2012-02. MHA administered FCRA in 2012 and P. Chidambaram was Home Minister (2008-11 to 2012-07), so the actor and window overlap and the date passes. The Tribune print edition is dated 2012-02-25 with a 24 February dateline, and it reports the cancellation in the past tense, so it happened on or before 2012-02-24. The record's "Tribune 2012-02-24" label matches the dateline. The URL date (20120225) is the print date, which is fine.
verdicts.identityTest: This partly fails. The source never names the three associations. The "12 NGOs" are unnamed, so ngo:kudankulam-linked-associations is an aggregate node with no FCRA registration numbers. The statement also does not come from MHA. It comes from V. Narayanasamy, Minister of State in the PMO and for Personnel, a different ministry, who is relaying what MHA had supposedly done. Tribune's words are: "The Minister of State for Personnel said the home ministry had cancelled licences of three of the 12 NGOs whose fund utilisation was under scrutiny." The source says "operating licences", not "FCRA registrations". Reading it as FCRA is plausible but is our inference; it could also mean prior-permission or suspension. Home Minister Chidambaram, who was actually responsible, spoke on 2012-02-29 (Deccan Herald, published 2012-03-01). He described bank accounts of FOUR NGOs being frozen and CBI/TN police cases, and did not mention any cancellations. Deccan Herald on 2012-02-28 likewise reports four NGOs "booked" with accounts frozen, following MHA checks of "audited accounts of 12 NGOs", and again mentions no cancellations. Deccan Herald on 2012-02-24 reports Narayanasamy "blamed three NGOs for diverting foreign funds" and says "the government took action", but it does not say their licences were cancelled.
verdicts.baseRate: Cancellation itself does not single anyone out. The News Bharati figures (a weak source), reproduced by Hinduism Today, put MHA's cancellations at 4,141 of 39,236 registered associations in 2012-13, and 794 of those were in Tamil Nadu. Three cancellations in a year with thousands is routine volume. What would make this notable is the stated link to the Kudankulam protests, and that link rests only on ministers' statements. Chidambaram "refused to confirm that there was any link between inspection of accounts and activities of the NGOs and their support to the anti-KNPP movement" (DH 2012-03-01). On symmetry, this claim is itself the UPA-era control named in SPEC. The same lens applied to NDA cancellations (Greenpeace, Tuticorin Diocesan Association 2015) reads the same way: a government statement of grounds without a published order is at most alleged or reported, not documented. The claim does not name a religion as the actor, although DH calls them "Christian NGOs". Keep it that way.
verdicts.denialFound: Only the movement's general denial is on record. Tribune 2012-02-25 quotes S.P. Udayakumar of PMANE: "It is unfortunate that the Prime Minister has made the allegations without any documentary proof. We strongly deny his observation that the agitation is being funded by other countries." DH 2012-02-28 reports that Udayakumar sent a legal notice to the PM calling the imputation "totally false" (https://www.deccanherald.com/content/230728/4-ngos-booked-funding-protests.html). No response from the three unnamed associations exists, because they were never named; whether they were asked is unknown. The contrary official account is Chidambaram's (freezes and cases, no cancellations): https://www.deccanherald.com/india/pc-says-more-ngos-scanner-2317244
verdicts.innocentReading: Narayanasamy was not the minister responsible for FCRA. He may have conflated account freezes or suspensions of prior permission with "cancelled licences", or counted routine 2011-12 cancellations for non-filing of FC returns among Tamil Nadu associations that happened to be under the same scrutiny. The official version that followed (four accounts frozen, criminal cases, no cancellations mentioned) fits a picture in which no Kudankulam-specific FCRA cancellation had been completed by 24 February 2012.
verdicts.reason: The Tribune URL loads, and it does carry the sentence "the home ministry had cancelled licences of three of the 12 NGOs". But the claim turns a second-hand statement by a minister from another ministry (MoS PMO/Personnel Narayanasamy) into an MHA enforcement act. It also turns "operating licences" into "FCRA registrations". The Home Minister's own account five days later describes four NGOs with frozen accounts and criminal cases and mentions no cancellations. Contemporaneous DH reporting on 24 and 28 February does not corroborate any cancellation. As worded, the edge states as fact something that only one relayed ministerial assertion supports, and the responsible ministry's account does not match it. As an MHA enforce edge it should be alleged, carrying a contra. Keep it at reported only if it is recast as Narayanasamy's statement.
verdicts.corrections: 1. lab: "MoS (PMO/Personnel) V. Narayanasamy said MHA had cancelled 'operating licences' of three of 12 unnamed Kudankulam-area NGOs under scrutiny, 2012-02-24 (UPA)". Drop "FCRA registrations" unless an MHA record says so. 2. tier: reported -> alleged for the s=ngo:mha-foreigners-division enforce edge. Alternatively, set s=wel:v-narayanasamy (or a statement node) and keep reported. 3. Add a contra: Chidambaram 2012-02-29, bank accounts of four NGOs frozen and cases filed by CBI/TN police, no cancellations mentioned (DH https://www.deccanherald.com/india/pc-says-more-ngos-scanner-2317244). Add DH 2012-02-28 (https://www.deccanherald.com/content/230728/4-ngos-booked-funding-protests.html) as a second source for the "12 NGOs" scrutiny and the four cases. 4. d: note that the associations are unnamed and there are no FCRA registration numbers, so identity is unresolved. 5. upgradeIf: keep the requirement for a Parliament answer or MHA Annual Report 2011-12 naming the associations and the cancellation orders. killIf: add "MHA or Parliament record shows only freezes or prior-permission for the Kudankulam cluster in 2012-02, and no cancellations".

verdicts.dateTest: Claim: PM Manmohan Singh (in office 2004-05-22 to 2014-05-26) said in a Science interview in Feb 2012 that US/Scandinavian-funded NGOs were behind the Kudankulam agitation. Tribune (dateline New Delhi, Feb 24, 2012; edition dated 2012-02-25) says: "The Prime Minister had yesterday in an interview with a Science journal pointedly accused US-based NGOs". So he said it on about 2012-02-23, within his tenure. from=2012-02 is correct. The source label "Tribune 2012-02-24" matches the dateline, but the URL is the 25 Feb edition. Minor.
verdicts.identityTest: The speaker is right: the PM, in the Science (AAAS) interview. The target is off. The PM's words were aimed at foreign NGOs: "these NGOs, mostly I think based in the United States". The India-based recipients ("to some of the India-based NGOs ... close to the Kudankulam area, to Tuticorin, Tirunelveli") were named by MoS PMO V. Narayanasamy on 2012-02-24, not by the PM. The Tribune does not support the "Scandinavian" part for the PM. It says Narayanasamy "also added Scandinavian countries". The Science interview itself does (per ANS Nuclear Newswire): "There are NGOs, often funded by the U.S. and the Scandinavian countries...". So the quote holds against the primary interview, which is not in srcs. No FCRA registration numbers or names for the 12 associations appear in the opened source. The contra (c098) comes from PMANE/S.P. Udayakumar, a movement, not from the unnamed associations.
verdicts.baseRate: Non-discriminating as evidence of foreign funding. Governments of both blocs have said "foreign-funded NGOs are behind protests against a project": UPA on Kudankulam (2012), NDA in the 2014 IB report on Greenpeace and anti-development NGOs, and Sterlite/Thoothukudi (2018). This is the usual government response to a stalled project, so the statement shows a political stance, not a funding finding. Symmetry: the SPEC names the 2012 Kudankulam cancellations as the UPA control. Tiering this UPA claim as alleged is consistent with how NDA-era foreign-hand claims should be tiered. The same lens gives the same reading.
verdicts.denialFound: Yes, in the same source. PMANE's S.P. Udayakumar (Chennai, 2012-02-24): "It is unfortunate that the Prime Minister has made the allegations without any documentary proof. We strongly deny his observation that the agitation is being funded by other countries." (https://www.tribuneindia.com/2012/20120225/main2.htm). This is already recorded as contra fcra-actions:c098. Arun Jaitley (BJP) and D. Raja (CPI; the Tribune prints "A. Raja") asked the government to make the evidence public. The Tribune reports only that the NGOs "took a strong exception". The individual associations were not named, so whether they were asked is unknown.
verdicts.innocentReading: Several Tuticorin/Tirunelveli church and social-service associations were long-standing FCRA-registered recipients of Western church and development funding for relief, fishing-community and post-tsunami work. Local anti-nuclear mobilisation drew on the same parish networks. The overlap in geography and personnel is enough to fit the PM's remark without any foreign funds being diverted to the agitation. The statement is also consistent with political pressure to commission a stalled Indo-Russian project.
verdicts.reason: The substance survives as an allegation. The quoted sentence appears in the Tribune: "these NGOs, mostly I think based in the United States, dont appreciate the need for our country to increase the energy supply". The "US and Scandinavian" funding wording is in the PM's primary Science interview. The claim is dated inside his tenure, and a denial is recorded (c098). No adjudicated finding of diversion appears in any opened source, so alleged is the correct tier. The edge is mis-encoded, though. pred=enforce with s=wel:manmohan-singh says the PM took an enforcement action against the Kudankulam-linked associations. He did not: he gave a magazine interview aimed at foreign NGOs. The enforcement (3 of 12 licences cancelled, an MHA probe) is MHA's and is already edge c096. The "Scandinavian" attribution in the Tribune belongs to Narayanasamy.
verdicts.corrections: 1) pred: the PM's interview is a statement, not an enforcement action. Either re-encode s as MHA (ngo:mha-foreigners-division, "investigation") with the PM/PMO statement cited as the basis, or move the PM remark into the narratives array and keep c096 as the enforcement edge. 2) text/lab: quote the PM exactly: "these NGOs, mostly I think based in the United States, don't appreciate the need for our country to increase the energy supply". Attribute "often funded by the U.S. and the Scandinavian countries" to the Science interview, and "sent money close to the Kudankulam area ... to some of the India-based NGOs" plus the Tribune's "Scandinavian" addition to MoS PMO V. Narayanasamy (2012-02-24, ANI). 3) srcs: add the primary Science (AAAS) interview, Feb 2012, and a secondary such as https://www.ans.org/news/article-952/indian-pm-singh-alleges-anti-nuclear-protests-funded-by-u-s-ngos/. Relabel the Tribune as edition 2012-02-25, dateline 2012-02-24. 4) Target: the PM's remark targets foreign (US-based) NGOs. The India-based associations are Narayanasamy's target, so split or retarget. 5) contra c098: set s to a PMANE / S.P. Udayakumar node rather than ngo:kudankulam-linked-associations, since PMANE is not shown to be one of the 12 associations. 6) upgradeIf: add an MHA Parliament answer or MHA Annual Report 2011-12/2012-13 that names the associations whose accounts were frozen or cancelled.

verdicts.dateTest: Written as a claim: MHA Foreigners Division (UPA, Home Ministers Chidambaram and then Shinde, 2011 to 2014-05-26; NDA from 2014-05-26) applied FCRA grounds to registered associations, 2011 to 2026. The dated UPA acts fall inside UPA tenure: the Kudankulam cancellations were announced 2012-02-24 (Chidambaram), and the INSAF suspension order is dated 2013-04-30 (Shinde). The Delhi HC quashed that suspension on 2013-09-19. The NDA cases (Greenpeace 2015, CHRI 2022, Noel Harper 2022-04-08) fall inside NDA tenure. Date test passes. One nuance: the whole UPA comparison window, 2011-14, ran under the FCRA 2010, which was itself a new UPA statute in force from 2011-05-01. So "after 2020 the statute" leaves out that the statute also changed at the start of the comparison window.
verdicts.identityTest: The actor, MHA Foreigners Division (FCRA Wing), matches the INSAF judgment: "order dated 30.4.2013 issued by the Director to the Government of India, Ministry of Home Affairs, Foreigners Division (FCRA Wing)". The edge target does not match. The task payload gives t = "ngo:fcra-registered-associations", but the record in fcra-actions.json has t = "ngo:fcra-associations-aggregate". One of them is wrong. The srcs list also differs: the payload has 3 URLs, the file has 8 (FIDH, Mongabay, Scroll, hindutvawatch mirror, CSR Universe). The Kudankulam associations are not named in the Tribune piece, so their identities, and the grounds they were cancelled on, cannot be checked.
verdicts.baseRate: This fails as a comparison. It sets about 3 UPA cases against about 20 NDA cases, and only one UPA case has a stated ground on record (INSAF). The Tribune gives no statutory ground for the three Kudankulam cancellations, only "fund utilisation under scrutiny" and "did not follow the guidelines". No reachable source gives a ground for the three CPSC suspensions under the UPA. With n=1 stated UPA ground, "identical grounds" cannot be measured. Aggregate data (Factly, from MHA data) shows 3,922 cancellations in 2012 and 10,003 in 2015. More than 99.5% of 2011-2019 cancellations fell in 2012, 2015, 2017 and 2019, and most were for non-filing (s.18). Noel Harper records "more than 19,000" cancellations for 2011-2019, for statutory non-compliance. So the scale change is real, roughly 2-3x per year. However, the 2015 wave cleared non-filers of FY2009-12 returns (10,343 notices issued in Dec 2014), and the 2016 and 2022 cessations came from the five-year renewal introduced by the UPA's 2010 Act. The file says government-aligned associations (VIF, India Foundation, Ekal) were not examined, so the SPEC's critic/aligned control has only been run on one side.
verdicts.denialFound: None found; not asked. This analytic claim covers two governments and no party was asked. The closest statement from the government is the Union's position recorded in Noel Harper (SC, 2022-04-08): 20,600 "non-compliant" registrations cancelled and "no absolute right inheres in any one ... to receive foreign contribution". That supports the compliance/scale reading. On the UPA side, S.P. Udayakumar called the Kudankulam allegations "baseless" (Tribune 2012-02-25), but that answers c097, not this claim.
verdicts.innocentReading: A single statute (the 2010 Act, with its five-year renewal, s.14 "public interest" ground and the 2011 Rule 3 "political nature" test covering bandh/hartal) was enforced by one bureaucracy under both governments. Its public-interest ground was invoked against protest-funding intermediaries under the UPA (INSAF, Kudankulam) and under the NDA. The volume jump after 2014 reflects a backlog of non-filers from FY2009-12 and the first renewal cycle due in 2016, and the 2020 Amendment then outlawed sub-granting. That reading fits the evidence and does not need "identical" or "only scale changed".
verdicts.reason: The sources confirm the parts of the claim. They do not support the headline as worded. The INSAF judgment records the UPA ground: "foreign funds ... transferred to other FCRA registered as well as non-FCRA registered NGOs, which were utilizing the said fund for organizing the protest, etc. against the welfare policies of the Government and such utilization ... may prejudicially affect the public interest". The Tribune confirms "the home ministry had cancelled licences of three of the 12 NGOs", with the PM blaming US and Scandinavian funders. Noel Harper confirms the 2020 statute was upheld. But "identical grounds" is a conjunction inference drawn from one UPA case with a stated ground. Several NDA grounds have no UPA counterpart on record: "engagement with embassies and UN Special Rapporteurs" (CPSC 2016), economic-interest / IB-report grounds (Greenpeace), "harmony", and donor-side watch-list and prior-reference controls (Ford, Compassion). "What changed after 2014 is scale, and after 2020 the statute" presents one of several changes as the only one. It leaves out the 2010 UPA statute that drove the renewal-cycle cessations, the donor-side controls, and the 2016/2018 retrospective Finance Act amendments. It also cites a weak 4,141 figure while a better-sourced 3,922 (calendar 2012) exists. The analytic tier fits once the wording is narrowed; as worded, the claim overstates.
verdicts.corrections: 1) Change lab to: "Grounds on record overlap: onward transfer to fund protests / public interest was invoked under the UPA (INSAF 2013; Kudankulam 2012) and the NDA. After 2014 the volume rose (3,922 cancellations in 2012 vs 10,003 in 2015, mostly non-filing), the first renewal cycle under the 2010 UPA Act fell due in 2016, and in 2020 the statute was tightened." 2) In d, replace "4,141 cancellations in 2012-13 (weak source)" with "3,922 cancellations in calendar 2012 (Factly, from MHA data; 4,138 per Newslaundry/Factly 2015-04)" and add the source https://factly.in/the-history-of-fcra-and-the-trends-in-fcra-registration-cancellations/. 3) In d, state that the stated grounds for the Kudankulam cancellations and the UPA-era CPSC suspensions are not on record in the sources opened, so the UPA ground sample is n=1 (INSAF). 4) In d, list the NDA-only grounds and instruments: embassies/UN Special Rapporteurs (CPSC 2016), economic interest (Greenpeace), and the donor watch-list / prior-reference category (Ford, Compassion). 5) Settle the target id: ngo:fcra-associations-aggregate (file) vs ngo:fcra-registered-associations (payload). 6) Add the Noel Harper figure "more than 19,000 ... between 2011 and 2019" as a scale source. 7) Keep upgradeIf/killIf, and make upgradeIf also require running the government-aligned control (VIF, India Foundation, Ekal).

verdicts.dateTest: Claim: MHA (Union government, 2014-05-26 onward) cancelled, refused or suspended FCRA registrations of critics, 2015–2024. Home Ministers: Rajnath Singh (2014-05-26 to 2019-05-30), Amit Shah (2019-05-30 onward). Every NDA-era case listed falls inside that window: Greenpeace cancelled 2015-09-02 (Mongabay); Lawyers Collective order dated 27 Nov 2016 (FLD); Sabrang 16 Jun 2016, the day before the Gulberg verdict on 17 Jun (CJP); Navsarjan 15 Dec 2016, five months after Una on 11 Jul 2016 (Scroll); CPSC renewal rejected 29 Jan 2016 (FIDH); CHRI cancelled Apr 2022 after the Delhi HC declined to interfere on 14 Feb (Scroll); Environics cancelled 4 Mar 2024 (Devdiscourse); CPR Jan 2024 (National Herald). The counter-side dates are also correct: INSAF suspended 30.4.2013 (Indian Kanoon), Kudankulam cancellations Feb 2012 under Manmohan Singh (Tribune), Noel Harper decided 2022-04-08 (SC). No chronology failure.
verdicts.identityTest: The actor is an office with dates (MHA FCRA wing), not a family or religion, so there is no kill trigger. Two identity problems. (1) Amnesty (2020) did not lose an FCRA registration. The Amnesty press release is about accounts "frozen by the Enforcement Directorate" and never mentions FCRA. By MHA's account, Amnesty held FCRA permission only once, in 2000, and was refused under the UPA in 2009. So it is a different instrument (ED) and it also belongs on the symmetry side. (2) RGF/RGCT is counted twice. It appears in strongestCase as a critic and again in strongestCounter as "a Gandhi-family foundation on grounds identical in form". Its trustees are the leadership of the main opposition party, so it cannot serve as a neutral control. Also, the Tribune source has Shah "Addressing the media outside Parliament", not speaking "in Lok Sabha" as the source label says.
verdicts.baseRate: Counting targets does not distinguish critics from anyone else. The 22 named case files are about 0.1% of the 20,701 cancelled registrations (CSR Universe, 2024-04). Of the 5,968 organisations that lost FCRA on 2022-01-01, 5,789 (97%) simply did not apply for renewal and 179 were denied (ThePrint, confirmed). The only evidence that could discriminate is the distribution of grounds by target type, and that is a void because the MHA grounds table is not reachable. Even among the named critics, the grounds differ. Content-reaching grounds are documented for Navsarjan ("harmony", quoted in Scroll), Lawyers Collective (protests treated as "political activities", FLD), CPSC (engagement with UN Special Rapporteurs, FIDH), CPR (publication equated with current affairs, per CPR's own statement) and Environics (payments to protesters, per the CBI). CHRI's grounds were accounting ones: undisclosed projects, funds used abroad, consultancy fees booked as contributions (Scroll, citing unnamed officials). RGF's grounds were Chinese-embassy and IRF funding. The narrative's phrase "stated grounds that reach content" therefore overstates CHRI and RGF.
verdicts.denialFound: No government response is recorded in this narrative's sources. What exists elsewhere: MHA's statement on Amnesty (in this file as "Tribune 2020-09-30", which says Amnesty had FCRA only once, in 2000, and alleges FDI rerouting); a Minister of State saying "action has been taken after getting specific inputs" (reported via a Deccan Herald editorial; not opened); and MHA's defence of the FCRA amendments on internal-security grounds. Was the government asked about this narrative specifically? Not asked / unknown. Responses from the targets are recorded: Macwan says the "harmony" charge is "baseless" (Scroll); CPR called the decision "incomprehensible and disproportionate" (National Herald); Lawyers Collective "denies all of the accusations" (FLD).
verdicts.innocentReading: A licensing regime that got stricter after the 2020 Amendment, which ended onward transfers and the intermediary model. It is enforced mostly against non-filers and against intermediary structures whatever their politics: World Vision (Rs 170 crore), CASA and EFI were cancelled on the same "purposes other than declared objectives" grounds. The UPA used the same instrument on the same kinds of grounds: INSAF 2013 over transfers "for organizing the protest, etc. against the welfare policies of the Government"; Kudankulam 2012, with the PM naming US-based NGOs; Amnesty refused in 2009. Courts deferred after 2020 (the Delhi HC in CHRI's case; the SC in Noel Harper). On this reading, prominent critics are a small, visible subset of a broad tightening.
verdicts.reason: "Contested" is the right calibration and the narrative stands. The factual sequence in strongestCase holds up against the sources, with verbatim support for Navsarjan's "harmony" ground, the Sabrang/Gulberg dates, the CPSC UN-rapporteur ground, the Lawyers Collective "political activities" ground and the Environics protest payments. The factual base of strongestCounter also holds: ThePrint's 5,789 of about 6,000, the INSAF 2013 protest-transfer ground, Manmohan Singh on the Kudankulam NGOs, and the Noel Harper judgment. The claim itself asserts intent ("to silence"), and no document in hand establishes intent. It is asserted by named parties: Amnesty ("drive to silence critical voices"), Front Line Defenders ("political tool to suppress dissent") and CIVICUS. That makes it tier "alleged" at most, carrying a contra. The discriminating test (grounds by target type against the registered population) is a void. The government-aligned control (VIF, India Foundation, Ekal/Vidya Bharati) was not run in this file. Until both are done, it cannot move to well-supported or to speculative. Nothing refutes it, but several items are miscategorised (see corrections).
verdicts.corrections:
1. strongestCase: remove "Amnesty (2020)" from "critics losing registration". Recast it as an ED account freeze in 2020-09, and add Amnesty's UPA-era refusal (2009; FCRA granted only once, in 2000, per MHA) to strongestCounter's UPA symmetry list. The Amnesty press release says nothing about FCRA registration.
2. Remove RGF/RGCT ("a Gandhi-family foundation") from strongestCounter. A foundation run by opposition leaders cannot be a neutral control. Keep it in strongestCase, labelled "opposition-linked; stated grounds are funding source (Chinese embassy, IRF), not content".
3. Fix the RGF source label "Amit Shah in Lok Sabha" to "Amit Shah to media outside Parliament, 2022-12-13". The Tribune text reads "Addressing the media outside Parliament".
4. CHRI: the grounds reported by Scroll (via unnamed MHA officials) are accounting ones, not content ones. Move CHRI out of "grounds that reach content", or qualify it.
5. Label the Sabrang/Gulberg timing link as the Trust's own framing (CJP is Setalvad's organisation), and the Navsarjan/Una link as founder Macwan's belief ("believes", Scroll). The dates are confirmed; the causal link is the party's claim.
6. Compassion did not have a registration "cancelled". It exited on 2017-03-15 after its partners were restricted. Change "cancelled" to "restricted/exited" for Compassion.
7. Replace the hindutvawatch.org mirror with The Hindu's original URL for World Vision (partisan mirror).
8. Add a government-response source (MHA Amnesty statement 2020-09-29/30; the MoS "specific inputs" statement) to srcs. Record that the government was not asked about the narrative as such.
9. whatWouldChangeThis: add that the government-aligned control (VIF, India Foundation, Ekal/Vidya Bharati receipts and any enforcement) must be run with the same fields before any status change. Note that the Christian-body cancellations rebut "critics-only" specificity but not targeting in general; the religious-targeting narrative reads them the other way.

verdicts.dateTest: Restated as: Indian government actors said foreign-funded NGOs paid for protests that stalled projects, in 2012-02 (UPA: PM Manmohan Singh and MoS PMO V. Narayanasamy on Kudankulam), 2013-04-30 (UPA MHA on INSAF), 2016 (NDA MHA on Lawyers Collective), 2024-01-17 (NDA MHA on CPR) and CBI FIR 2024-01 / cancellation 2024-03-04 (Environics). Each speaker held office when they spoke: Singh was PM 2004-2014; Narayanasamy was MoS PMO in 2012. The Tribune piece is datelined New Delhi, February 24 (2012), in the 2012-02-25 edition, and quotes the PM interview "yesterday" (2012-02-23). The CBI allegation about Environics is dated to payments on 2020-11-15. The same wire text also says the FIR covered "bank transfers carried out in 2018". That is an inconsistency inside the source; our record does not introduce it. The dates pass.
verdicts.identityTest: Two attribution faults. (1) The narrative's strongestCase says "A Prime Minister said it on record in 2012-02 (US/Scandinavian-funded NGOs at Kudankulam)". The Tribune source quotes the PM saying only "these NGOs, mostly I think based in the United States, don't appreciate the need for our country to increase the energy supply." It then says: "He [Narayanasamy] also added Scandinavian countries to the list of sponsors." So the Scandinavian part belongs to MoS Narayanasamy, not the PM. The same conflation appears in narrative:0 strongestCounter, in the entity sub at line ~516, in the claim lab at ~3580 and in symmetryCheck. (2) The narrative says the stated grounds against INSAF, Lawyers Collective, CPR and Environics "all allege foreign money for protests or litigation against projects". The cited sources do not say this for three of the four. INSAF (Delhi HC 2013-09-19, para 2): funds used "for organizing the protest, etc. against the welfare policies of the Government", with no project named. Lawyers Collective (Front Line Defenders): "using foreign funding to organise peaceful protests and rallies, considered as political activities", again with no project. CPR (the cited Tribune/PTI 2024-01-17 story): "undesirable purposes likely to affect the country's economic interest", onward transfers and non-designated accounts, with no protests or litigation. The project/litigation ground for CPR is reported by ANI and ThePrint ("aid protests and legal battles against development projects"), but neither is cited. Only Environics is supported as written: the CBI alleges 711 x Rs 1,250 = Rs 8.89 lakh paid to "protestors for JSW agitation at Dhinkia", booked as Amphan cyclone relief. The arithmetic checks out (Rs 8.9 lakh = Rs 0.089 crore).
verdicts.baseRate: The property is "an FCRA action whose stated ground cites protests or litigation against projects". That property is rare, so it discriminates. Most of the 20,000+ cancellations are for not filing returns. The 2022-01-01 cessation was 97% non-application (5,789 of 5,968). The project-protest ground shows up in a handful of named cases: the Kudankulam cluster (3 of 12), Greenpeace, CPR and Environics. So the narrative rests on a few cases, not on the population of actions. A bipartisan check also cuts against it as a partisan tool: the UPA PM (2012) and the NDA-era IB report (2014-06-03) made the same claim.
verdicts.denialFound: Yes. S.P. Udayakumar (PMANE), Tribune 2012-02-24 (https://www.tribuneindia.com/2012/20120225/main2.htm): "It is unfortunate that the Prime Minister has made the allegations without any documentary proof. We strongly deny his observation that the agitation is being funded by other countries." CPR called the cancellation "incomprehensible and disproportionate" (https://thewire.in/rights/home-ministry-cancels-centre-for-policy-researchs-fcra-registration). Lawyers Collective "denies all of the accusations" (Front Line Defenders). In court INSAF denied transferring funds to non-FCRA NGOs, per the counter/rejoinder in the judgment. Activists also denied the 2014 IB report (https://www.business-humanrights.org/en/latest-news/india-intelligence-bureau-says-foreign-funded-ngos-are-stalling-development-activists-deny-says-attempt-to-undermine/).
verdicts.innocentReading: Local people with their own stakes organised these protests: Kudankulam fishing villages over safety after Fukushima, Dhinkia betel-vine farmers over land. The movements predate any foreign money alleged and do not depend on it. The amounts alleged are trivial against project scale (Rs 0.089 crore at Dhinkia). Project delays have many domestic causes: land acquisition, environmental clearance, courts and state politics. When a government facing a stalled flagship project cites a "foreign hand", that is a common political move and not evidence of what caused the delay. On the other side, NGOs that fund litigation or community mobilisation lawfully are doing advocacy, which FCRA restricts only for "political" activity as defined.
verdicts.reason: The narrative survives because it claims nothing beyond what the evidence supports. It is marked speculative, and the record in hand is only allegations by named state actors (PM, MoS, MHA, CBI FIR, IB) with no adjudicated finding. The only court that ruled (INSAF, Delhi HC 2013-09-19) quashed the suspension on procedure. The status is calibrated, and the right edge tier for the proposition is "alleged", with the PMANE, CPR and LC denials as contras. However, the strongestCase field misquotes its sources. It gives Narayanasamy's "Scandinavian" to the PM. It says four sets of MHA grounds "all allege" protest or litigation against projects, when the cited texts support that only for Environics. It also leaves out the strongest documentary basis for the narrative, the IB report of 2014-06-03 ("concerted effort by select foreign funded NGOs to 'take down' Indian developmental projects", 2-3% GDP impact claimed). In addition, strongestCounter says the INSAF court "rule[d] on the INSAF ground", but it did not reach the ground. It quashed for lack of a pending s.14 inquiry and unrecorded reasons.
verdicts.corrections: (1) narratives[1].strongestCase: replace "A Prime Minister said it on record in 2012-02 (US/Scandinavian-funded NGOs at Kudankulam)" with "PM Manmohan Singh said on record in 2012-02 that Kudankulam's difficulties were caused by NGOs 'mostly I think based in the United States'; MoS PMO V. Narayanasamy added Scandinavian funders the next day". Make the same PM/Scandinavian fix in narratives[0].strongestCounter, in the Manmohan Singh entity sub, in the claim lab "Alleged (PM Manmohan Singh, 2012-02): US- and Scandinavian-funded NGOs...", and in symmetryCheck. (2) narratives[1].strongestCase: replace "all allege foreign money for protests or litigation against projects" with "allege foreign money for protests (INSAF: 'against the welfare policies of the Government'; Lawyers Collective: 'protests and rallies' as political activity) and, for CPR and Environics, for protests or litigation against development projects". (3) Add a source for the CPR project ground, e.g. ANI 2024-01-17 https://aninews.in/news/national/general-news/mha-cancels-fcra-registration-of-centre-for-policy-research-for-misutilising-foreign-contribution-affecting-indias-economic-interests-other-violations20240117204511/ or ThePrint https://theprint.in/india/govt-scrapped-cpras-fcra-licence-over-funding-for-protests-paper-on-policy-challenges/1928172/. The cited Tribune/PTI story does not mention protests or litigation. (4) Add the IB report of 2014-06-03 to strongestCase as a leaked, unadjudicated government assessment, with source https://www.business-humanrights.org/en/latest-news/india-ib-report-concerted-efforts-by-select-foreign-funded-ngos-to-take-down-indian-development-projects/, and the activists' denial as a counter. (5) narratives[1].strongestCounter: replace "the one court to rule on the INSAF ground quashed the order as premature and unreasoned" with "the one court to review the INSAF action quashed the suspension as premature (no s.14 inquiry pending) and unreasoned, without reaching the merits of the ground". (6) Keep status speculative. If this is ever converted to an edge, tier it "alleged" with the Udayakumar, CPR and LC denials as contras. The narrative does not frame a family, religion or ethnicity as the actor, so there is no kill on that ground.

verdicts.dateTest: The claim has two parts. Part 1: RGF received money from the Chinese embassy/PRC government in FY2005-06 and FY2006-07. Part 2: that money shaped Congress's China policy, at an unstated time. Part 1 falls in UPA-I (2004-09), so Congress was in government and the dates are consistent. The receipt came under FCRA 1976, and the cancellation (2022-10) was under FCRA 2010. Part 2 has no date, no policy decision and no outcome, so it cannot be tested. The nearest candidate is the RGICS India-China FTA feasibility study (April 2009, per the BJP's own account). No India-China FTA was ever signed, so no policy outcome follows from it. The narrative's strongestCase says the trustees 'were the Prime Minister, the Congress president, the future party leader and the Finance/Home Minister of the time'. That fails the date test as sourced. India CSR (2022) lists Manmohan Singh and Chidambaram as current members ('The RGF even has former prime minister Manmohan Singh and former finance minister P Chidambaram as members'). ThePrint/PTI (2022-12-13) gives the 2022 trustee list. Neither source gives the board for 2005-07.
verdicts.identityTest: The donor is right: the RGF 2005-06 annual report names 'the Embassy of The People's Republic of China as one of the "partner organisations and donors"'. The BJP (Malviya, 2020-06-25) says the Government of the PRC is also listed as a separate donor. The recipient is also right: the Rajiv Gandhi Foundation, with the RGF-promoted think tank RGICS also listing China. The claim still merges RGF, RGICS and 'Congress' into one actor. RGF is a registered charity and the Indian National Congress is a party. No source shows a transfer or instruction from RGF to party policymaking. It also merges 'Chinese government money' with 'Chinese embassy money'. An embassy is a government mission, so that step is defensible. Source-chain error: the narrative says 'The Home Minister told the Lok Sabha (2022-12)'. Tribune (2022-12-14) says the opposite: 'Addressing the media outside Parliament, he said... Had he got the opportunity, said Shah, he would have told Parliament that during the 2005-06 and 2006-07 fiscals, the RGF had received Rs 1.35 crore from the Chinese embassy.' ThePrint/PTI and Daily Excelsior agree: 'Addressing reporters outside Parliament House'. The ₹1.35 crore figure is therefore a press remark, not a Parliament answer. According to press reports (search snippets only; I could not open the Zee5 page or the sansad.in PDF), the written Lok Sabha answer the same day by MoS Nityanand Rai (asked by V.K. Sreekandan and Benny Behanan) gave the RGF grounds as FCRA 2010 s.11 and s.12(4)(a)(vi), without naming China.
verdicts.baseRate: Not quantified in the file. Foreign embassies funding Indian think tanks and cultural bodies before the 2010 Act was routine. The narrative itself admits 'not sourced here'. What sets RGF apart is who sits on its board, not the fact of an embassy donation, and a board's political membership is not evidence of policy capture. Symmetry check not done: the same lens has not been applied to BJP-aligned bodies (India Foundation, VIF) and their foreign-government or CPC engagements, or to the 2016/2018 retrospective Finance Act amendments that legalised foreign donations to both the BJP and Congress. Until it is, the lens is only being run on one side.
verdicts.denialFound: Yes, found on the receipt/cancellation side. (1) Abhishek Manu Singhvi: 'The Rajiv Gandhi Foundation has nothing to add, nothing to fear... you don't ask these questions of many holy cows... You are harassing each opposition segment', with party leaders calling it a 'witch-hunt' (https://indiacsr.in/fcra-of-rajiv-gandhi-foundation-and-rajiv-gandhi-charitable-trust-cancelled/). (2) Randeep Surjewala, 2020-06-25: 'stop living in 2005 and start answering questions in 2020' (https://theprint.in/politics/bjp-says-rajiv-gandhi-foundation-took-funds-from-china-congress-says-stop-living-in-2005/448864/). (3) Shah himself acknowledged that 'the Congress claimed that the money from the embassy was meant to undertake research on ties between India and China' (https://theprint.in/india/fcra-registration-of-rajiv-gandhi-foundation-cancelled-after-it-received-funds-from-chinese-embassy-shah/1263670/). No RGF statement specifically answering the policy-influence allegation was found. The party was plainly asked, publicly, by the BJP.
verdicts.innocentReading: A foreign-policy think tank (RGF/RGICS) took a declared donation from the Chinese embassy in 2005-06, when India-China engagement was bipartisan government policy (the 2005 Strategic and Cooperative Partnership). It listed the donor openly in its annual report and published trade-policy studies, including one favourable to an FTA. The government never adopted that FTA. Seventeen years later, a committee formed in 2020 found FCRA compliance breaches (ss.11 and 12(4)(a)(vi) per the written answer) that form-wise match the grounds used against many other associations. The open listing of the donor fits disclosure better than concealment.
verdicts.reason: Refuted as recorded. The narrative is a conjunction, and only its first clause has any evidence. The receipt rests on RGF's own 2005-06 annual report donor list (reported by India CSR and ThePrint; the primary document was not opened) plus a figure the Home Minister gave to reporters outside Parliament. The causal clause ('shaped Congress policy on China') has no evidence in any source opened. It is asserted only by named BJP figures: Nadda ('This is a secret relationship between Congress and China'), Malviya, and Prasad (the trade-deficit argument). No policy decision is identified, and the one candidate outcome, an India-China FTA, never happened. The 'contested' status is too generous. Under cui-bono §4.3, no evidence separates intent from coincidence, so the causal narrative is 'unsupported'. The receipt clause belongs at 'reported' (upgradeable to 'documented' once the annual report is opened). The narrative's strongestCase also misstates its source: it says 'told the Lok Sabha', but Shah was speaking to the press. The formal Parliament answer reportedly does not mention China at all.
verdicts.corrections:
narratives[2].status: 'contested' -> 'unsupported' (causal clause). Alternatively, split into (a) 'RGF received a donation from the Chinese embassy in 2005-06', status well-supported, sourced to the RGF annual report donor list, and (b) 'this shaped Congress policy', status unsupported.

narratives[2].strongestCase: replace 'The Home Minister told the Lok Sabha (2022-12)' with 'The Home Minister told reporters outside Parliament House (2022-12-13) that RGF received ₹1.35 crore from the Chinese embassy in 2005-06 and 2006-07; RGF's own 2005-06 annual report lists the Embassy of the PRC among "partner organisations and donors"; RGICS later published an India-China FTA feasibility study (BJP cites it as the policy link)'. Delete 'the trustees were the Prime Minister... of the time' unless a 2005-07 board list is sourced, or reword to 'current trustees include...'.

narratives[2].strongestCounter: add (i) the written Lok Sabha answer (MoS Nityanand Rai, 2022-12-13) cites FCRA 2010 ss.11 and 12(4)(a)(vi) without naming China; (ii) no India-China FTA was ever signed, so there is no policy outcome to attribute; (iii) the donor was openly listed in RGF's annual report.

verdicts.dateTest: Restated, the claim is: MHA (FCRA wing) singled out Christian associations for enforcement, 2017–2024. The dates in the listed sources overlap with NDA rule, but the narrative misdates several items. (1) Missionaries of Charity was refused renewal on 2021-12-25 and restored about 2022-01-07 (ThePrint, 2022-01-08: "days after revoking it following some 'adverse inputs'"). That is not "2023–24". (2) ThePrint's 1,800/250/250 figures are not about the 2022-01-01 cessations (see identityTest). (3) EFI and CNI-SBSS are placed in 2023 by Christianity Today ("Last year, the Evangelical Fellowship of India (EFI) and the Church of North India lost their licenses"). CSR Universe (2024-05-01) and The Wire place EFI, CASA, CNI-SBSS, VHAI and IGSSS in a single cancellation batch about 2024-04. That conflict needs recording, not merging. (4) World Vision was cancelled 2024-01 and Vision India 2024-03, both per Christianity Today. Compassion 2017 is correctly marked. The file is dated 2026-09-26 but leaves out the 2026 FCRA Amendment Bill (introduced 2026-03-25). That bill is where the Christian-targeting allegation is now being argued on the record.
verdicts.identityTest: The strongestCase misquotes its main source. ThePrint (2022-01-01) says: "Among the 12,580 organisations whose licences have ceased to exist are 1,800 Christian NGOs, 250 Hindu NGOs and over 250 Muslim NGOs, according to the list on the MHA website." The group is the cumulative expired list of 12,580, not the 5,968 that ceased on 2022-01-01. The counter is the MHA list, not ThePrint. The primary-derived table is in CSR Universe (2022-01-02, "Source: MHA; As on 10.00 am; 02 January, 2022"): religious-category expired NGOs were Christian 1,626, Hindu 257, Muslim 195, Buddhist 60, Sikh 13, Others 106, total 2,257. That is about 18% of the expired list, so roughly 82% of expired registrations carry no religious tag. The "generic 2024 ground cites 'religious conversions'" line is CSR Universe's own lead sentence about six NGOs. Three of the six are not Christian: Institute of Economic Growth, Hemophilia Federation and Samuel/Sansam Foundation. It is not an MHA generic ground. The actual MHA text is the refusal-grounds notice reported by The Wire: "association is involved in induced/ forceful religious conversion/proselytization". That notice should be the cited source. The Christian identity of the named bodies (World Vision, CASA, EFI, CNI-SBSS, MoC, Compassion, Vision India) is correct.
verdicts.baseRate: This comparison is our own analysis. (a) Among religious-category NGOs on the expired list (MHA via CSR Universe, 2022-01-02), 72% were Christian (1,626 of 2,257). (b) Among new religious-category registrations 2014 to 2023-10-01, 48% were Christian (194 of 407; Hindu 139, 34%), per MHA data reported by Swarajya on 2023-10-15. In 2023 alone the split was 26 Christian and 27 Hindu. So a denominator does exist, which contradicts the narrative's strongestCounter ("not published in any opened source"). It is a flow of new registrations, though, not the registered stock, so the 72% vs 48% gap suggests over-representation without proving it. Also: 97% of the 2022-01-01 cessations were non-application (179 refusals of 5,968), and religious-category bodies are only about 18% of expired registrations. Swarajya reports that all four 2023 violation revocations were Christian bodies (Shekina Prophetic Mission, Holy Berachah Ministries, Kashmir Evangelical Fellowship, Bethel Charitable Trust). That supports the narrative and belongs in strongestCase. Symmetry control: the ngo SPEC lists World Vision, MoC and Compassion as the government-aligned or neutral control against the "critics" narrative. The same file cannot use them as the neutral control in narrative 0 and as the targeted class here without saying so. No Hindu-aligned control (Ekal, Vidya Bharati) was examined for enforcement, so the symmetry check for religion is incomplete.
verdicts.denialFound: Yes, found. Minority Affairs Minister Kiren Rijiju, 2026-03-30 (IANS via NewsGram, https://www.newsgram.com/india/2026/03/30/fcra-row-escalates-as-church-congress-target-centre-rijiju-denies-targeting): "Allegations that the law was aimed at controlling Christian institutions were 'baseless'". He said the amendments "do not target any particular religious group". This concerns the 2026 Amendment Bill, not past cancellations. For MoC, MHA's 2021-12-27 statement says the refusal was on eligibility grounds and "adverse inputs", and that MHA froze no account because MoC itself asked SBI to (ThePrint 2022-01-08). Named accusers: Christianity Today's interviewees (EFI, CASA's Bishop Mondal, CBCI's Archbishop Couto); Catholicos Baselios Marthoma Mathews III and Congress president Kharge, 2026-03/04. None of these responses appear in the narrative.
verdicts.innocentReading: Christian bodies have long been the largest foreign-funded relief and welfare associations in India (CASA since 1947; World Vision, Compassion and Catholic diocesan societies). Any regime that ends near-perpetual registrations, bans onward transfers (2020 Amendment) and cancels for non-filing or misuse will therefore hit Christian bodies hardest in absolute numbers and rupees. Most cessations were non-application under the 2020 re-registration requirement, which is religion-neutral. The same period's cancellations fell equally on secular health, research and advocacy bodies (VHAI, IEG, HFI, CPR, Oxfam) and on a Gandhi-family foundation. MoC's refusal was reversed within two weeks.
verdicts.reason: Decisive point: the claim that Christian associations are "the real target" is a claim about intent, and the evidence does not establish it. The narrative's lead figure is also mis-cited. ThePrint's 1,800/250/250 come from the cumulative 12,580 expired list on the MHA site, not the 2022-01-01 cessations, and the "generic 2024 ground" is an outlet paraphrase covering three non-Christian NGOs. There is suggestive support: 72% Christian among expired religious-category NGOs against 48% of new religious registrations; all four 2023 violation revocations were Christian; the MHA grounds notice names "induced/forceful religious conversion"; and the MoS cited conversions when introducing the 2026 Bill. But the stock denominator is still missing, and 97% of the 2022 cessations were non-application. As an intent claim made by named parties (EFI, CASA, the Church, Kharge) and denied by the minister, it is alleged at most. It should remain a contested narrative and never become an edge. It names a religion as the target, not the actor, so a kill is not required as a narrative; any edge of the form "enforce → Christian associations as a class" should be killed.
verdicts.corrections:
1. strongestCase: replace "Among the 2022-01-01 cessations ThePrint counted ~1,800 Christian, ~250 Hindu and ~250 Muslim associations" with "Of 12,580 registrations listed as ceased on the MHA site on 2022-01-01, ~1,800 were Christian, ~250 Hindu and >250 Muslim (ThePrint, citing the MHA list). The MHA religious-category table (as of 2022-01-02) gives Christian 1,626 / Hindu 257 / Muslim 195 / Buddhist 60 / Sikh 13 / Others 106 of 2,257 (CSR Universe 2022-01-02)." Add src https://thecsruniverse.com/articles/fcra-overhaul-major-blow-for-christian-ngos-70-religious-ngos-deemed-to-have-ceased-aligned-to-christian-programmes-.
2. Replace "the generic 2024 ground cites 'religious conversions'" with the MHA refusal-grounds notice ("association is involved in induced/ forceful religious conversion/proselytization"), src https://m.thewire.in/article/government/anti-development-acts-protests-forced-conversions-govt-lists-reasons-of-fcra-cancellations. Drop the CSR Universe paraphrase as the support for this point.
3. Date each named case: MoC refused 2021-12-25 and restored ~2022-01-07; World Vision 2024-01; Vision India 2024-03; EFI/CASA/CNI-SBSS ~2024-04 per CSR Universe/The Wire, but 2023 per Christianity Today (record the conflict); Compassion 2017.
4. Add to strongestCase: all four 2023 violation revocations were Christian bodies; 194 of 407 new religious-category registrations 2014–2023 were Christian (Swarajya 2023-10-15, https://swarajyamag.com/politics/almost-half-of-fresh-fcra-registrations-under-religious-category-are-for-christian-ngos-home-ministry-data). Add the 2026 FCRA Amendment Bill (MoS Nityanand Rai citing conversions on 2026-03-25).
5. strongestCounter: remove "not published in any opened source". Say instead that only the flow of new religious-category registrations (48% Christian) is known, not the registered stock, and that religious-category bodies are ~18% of expired registrations.
6. Add a contra: Rijiju 2026-03-30, "baseless" (NewsGram/IANS URL above); MHA 2021-12-27 MoC statement.
7. whatWouldChangeThis: specify the stock of active registrations by religious category versus refusals and cancellations (not cessations), including the Hindu-aligned control bodies (Ekal, Vidya Bharati) named in the SPEC.
