verdicts.dateTest: Restated as: FCRA-registered associations received ₹22,137 cr of foreign contribution in FY2014-15, per an answer tabled on 26.07.2016. The answer was LS Unstarred Q.1603, dated 26.07.2016, 16th Lok Sabha, Session 9, answered by MoS Home Kiren Rijiju. It was found via the sansad.in API and its annexure PDF (https://sansad.in/getFile/lsapps/loksabhaquestions/annex/9/AU1603.pdf?source=lsapps) was opened. The FY2014-15 window is correct: Annexure-III is headed "during 2014-15". The companion series in the claim's `d` field is wrong, though. The answer's annexures cover 2012-13 (₹10,339.82 cr), 2013-14 (₹12,057.30 cr), 2014-15 (₹22,136.77 cr) and 2015-16 (₹788.73 cr, "As per returns filed as on 21.07.2016"). They do not cover 2011-12. The "₹45,300 cr over 2011-12→2014-15" is actually the sum for 2012-13 to 2015-16 (partial) of the four annexures, which is ₹45,322 cr.
verdicts.identityTest: The claim fails here. Its edge runs from ngo:foreign-sources-aggregate to ngo:fcra-associations-aggregate, which reads as total foreign contribution to all FCRA associations. The ₹22,137 cr figure is not that. It is the sum of the 34 state rows in Annexure-III, whose heading is "State wise number of associations who have received foreign contribution more than one crore rupees during 2014-15". That covers 3,068 associations, not all ~33,091 registered. Summing the rows gives ₹22,136.77 cr, which matches ISignal's ₹22,137 cr exactly. ISignal's own chart carries the note "For NGOs with contributions more than Rs one crore", and the claim dropped that qualifier. The answer body gives only one all-association figure: "the total funds received from abroad during the last three years and current year is Rs.50944.54 crore". It gives no per-year totals. There is also an independent official-data conflict. Factly's reading of the FCRA Online Portal (Feb 2021) says "The highest amount of Foreign Contribution amounting to Rs. 17,671 crores were received in 2015-16". That puts the all-association FY2014-15 total below ₹17,671 cr, less than this subset figure. The annexure number is therefore an accurate transcription of the tabled document, but it is not a national total and cannot be put alongside c001 (₹11,548.28 cr for all associations in FY2011-12) or c005.
verdicts.baseRate: Not applicable as a discrimination test. This is an aggregate statistic with no accused actor. The relevant check is series comparability. The same >₹1 cr annexure lens gives 10,340 → 12,057 → 22,137 cr across 2012-13 to 2014-15, while the FCRA portal all-association series (Factly) peaks at 17,671 cr in 2015-16. The ISignal claim that funding "doubled" rests only on the subset series. Symmetry control: the UPA-era figure (c001, RS *199 of 18.12.2013) is an all-association total. Setting it beside this subset figure, as ISignal's "doubled" framing does, compares unlike quantities.
verdicts.denialFound: Not applicable. No party is accused. There is no MHA statement reconciling the annexure's 2014-15 subset figure with the portal totals: none found, not asked.
verdicts.innocentReading: The number is exactly what MHA tabled, but for a narrower population: associations that each received more than ₹1 crore, listed state by state. The FY2014-15 jump (Delhi 2,863 → 4,984 cr; Andhra Pradesh 1,231 → 2,632 cr) may be a data artefact, for example from the 2015 move to online returns or from returns counting more than one year. It should not be read as a real doubling of foreign funding. The portal series does not show a doubling.
verdicts.reason: The primary source now opens (sansad.in API and annexure PDF AU1603.pdf), and ₹22,136.77 cr is confirmed as the sum of Annexure-III. But that annexure covers only the 3,068 associations that each received more than ₹1 crore in 2014-15, not all FCRA associations. The claim's aggregate edge and its label "FC received FY2014-15" therefore overstate the scope. They also conflict with official portal data (via Factly) that puts the peak all-association year at FY2015-16 with ₹17,671 cr. The `d` field's year attributions (FY2011-12 ~₹12,000 cr; ₹45,300 cr over 2011-12→2014-15) are also wrong. As written the claim is refuted. Once the scope is corrected it can be upgraded to documented.
verdicts.corrections: 1. Target: change `t` from ngo:fcra-associations-aggregate to a subset node such as ngo:fcra-associations-over-1cr-aggregate, or add a scope qualifier. 2. Label: change `lab` to "FC received FY2014-15 by associations receiving >₹1 cr each (3,068 associations) — ₹22,136.77 cr (sum of LS Q.1603 Annexure-III)". 3. Amount: set `a` to 22136.77. 4. Tier: move to documented and add the primary sources https://sansad.in/getFile/lsapps/loksabhaquestions/annex/9/AU1603.pdf?source=lsapps and the sansad.in API record (16th LS, Session 9, Q.1603, 26.07.2016, MoS Kiren Rijiju). Keep ISignal as secondary. Remove "answer not opened" and clear `upgradeIf`. 5. Rewrite `d` to give the correct subset series: 2012-13 ₹10,339.82 cr (2,186 associations); 2013-14 ₹12,057.30 cr (2,301); 2014-15 ₹22,136.77 cr (3,068); 2015-16 ₹788.73 cr (178, partial, returns as on 21.07.2016). State that the answer's only all-association total is ₹50,944.54 cr for 2012-13 to 2016-17 to date. Delete "FY2011-12 ~₹12,000 cr" and "₹45,300 cr over 2011-12→2014-15"; the latter is ₹45,322 cr over 2012-13 to 2015-16 (partial). 6. Add a `contra`/note: the FCRA portal via Factly (Feb 2021) gives FY2015-16 ₹17,671 cr as the peak all-association year, so the FY2014-15 all-association total is below ₹17,671 cr. 7. Do not use this figure in any series or ratio with c001, c002, c004 or c005, and do not repeat ISignal's "doubled". 8. Apply the same scope correction to c050 and any narrative that cites ISignal's ₹22,137 cr or ₹45,300 cr. 9. Set `killIf` to "an all-association FY2014-15 total from MHA/FCRA portal is cited as this edge's value".

verdicts.dateTest: Claim: foreign sources (aggregate) paid ₹15,355.17 cr to FCRA registrants and prior-permission holders (aggregate) in FY2016-17 (1 Apr 2016 to 31 Mar 2017). The same form covers ₹16,940.57 cr in FY2017-18 (c007) and ₹16,490.88 cr in FY2018-19 (c008). The from/to fields match each FY. The source is dated 29 Mar 2021 and uses MHA statistics 'available till March 16 this year'. The FC-4 filing deadline for FY2016-17 to FY2018-19 (nine months after FY close) had passed well before that date, so these are near-final snapshots. Only FY2019-20 (₹2,190.52 cr) was partial, and c009 already supersedes it. The dates are consistent.
verdicts.identityTest: Both nodes are statistical aggregates, so there is no CIN, DIN or FCRA number to match. The source's scope is 'NGOs and volunatary organisations registered under the Foreign Contribution Regulation Act (FCRA) or through prior permission granted by the government'. That matches the target node's sub-label ('registered or holding prior permission'). The donor side matches 'donors were from 130 countries', which is recorded on ngo:foreign-sources-aggregate. No actor is misidentified.
verdicts.baseRate: Not applicable as a discriminating test, because this is a national total, not a property of one entity. Plausibility check: Factly's FCRA-portal tally (c005 source, opened) says FY2015-16 was the peak at ₹17,671 cr and 'After the year 2015-16, the amount of foreign contribution has fallen'. The DH series (₹15.4k, ₹16.9k, ₹16.5k cr) fits that, and so does c009's FY2019-20 figure of ₹16,359 cr. Symmetry: the same MHA-returns lens gives the UPA-era FY2011-12 figure (₹11,548 cr) in the same file. The tier treats both periods alike. The claim frames no family, religion or ethnicity as an actor.
verdicts.denialFound: No denial applies: the figures are the MHA's own statistics, and no party is accused. Contrary reporting was found: the PTI report of the 9 Feb 2021 Lok Sabha written reply (MoS Home Nityanand Rai), carried by Business Today on 10 Feb 2021, says 'Over Rs 58,000 crore foreign funds were received by NGOs registered under the FCRA between 2016-17 and 2018-19' (https://www.businesstoday.in/latest/economy-politics/story/govt-nixed-fcra-licences-of-20600-ngos-in-a-decade-home-ministry-287230-2021-02-10). The DH figures for the same three years add up to ₹48,786.62 cr, about ₹9,200 cr (19%) lower. It is not clear from PTI's wording that the ₹58,000 cr figure appears in the reply text itself, and I did not open the reply PDF. This is an unresolved contradiction, not a refutation.
verdicts.innocentReading: This is a plain restatement of MHA's aggregate FC-4 return statistics as published by one national newspaper, with no implication of wrongdoing. The PTI ₹58,000 cr figure has a boring explanation too. It could be a rounding or aggregation by the PTI desk, a different cut (for example including other channels or a different year window), or an error. Factly's portal series supports the DH magnitudes (about ₹15–17k cr a year after the FY2015-16 peak), not a roughly ₹19.3k cr yearly average.
verdicts.reason: I opened the source (Deccan Herald, Shemin Joy, 29 Mar 2021; the amp URL redirects to /amp/story/india/...). It states each figure word for word: 'The year 2016-17 witnessed Rs 15,355.17 crore foreign funds reaching NGOs... the following fiscal saw it growing to Rs 16,940.57 crore. In 2018-19, it fell to Rs 16,490.88 crore'. It also states: 18,304 / 18,235 / 17,540 entities; Delhi 'Rs 3,607.91 crore in 2016-17, Rs 4,462.80 crore in 2017-18, Rs 4,370.44 crore in 2018-19'; Karnataka 'Rs 1,796.09 crore'; four-year total 'Rs 50,997.16 crore'; US 'Rs 19,942.22 crore or 39.11 per cent'. Amount, FY, currency and actors all match. Only one outlet reports these figures, citing MHA statistics, and no primary record was opened, so 'reported' is the correct tier. It cannot be upgraded. Nothing refutes it: Factly's portal data is consistent with it. The PTI '₹58,000 cr for 2016-17 to 2018-19' line conflicts with it, but that line is a single outlet's paraphrase. It should be recorded as a contra/void rather than used to kill the claim.
verdicts.corrections: 1) c006/c007/c008 upgradeIf: DH never mentions a Parliament answer. It says 'statistics collated by the Ministry of Home Affairs (MHA) based on the annual returns filed by NGOs' (that is, the fcraonline portal). Change 'The underlying RS/LS answer (March 2021) opened on sansad.in' to 'fcraonline.nic.in year-wise FC-4 statistics (as of 16 Mar 2021) or the LS written reply of 09.02.2021 (Nityanand Rai) opened'. Also drop 'Parliament answer not opened' from the narrative text, or rephrase it as 'primary MHA table not opened'. 2) c008 d or the file's voids: add a contradiction note. PTI/Business Today (10 Feb 2021) reports 'Over Rs 58,000 crore' for 2016-17 to 2018-19, against the DH sum of ₹48,786.62 cr, a gap of about ₹9,213 cr, unresolved. Add killIf: 'LS reply 09.02.2021 table gives year totals summing to ~₹58,000 cr'. 3) /home/user/india-corporate-intelligence/research/raw/ngo/fcra-actions.json line 174 tags 'foreign contribution received 2016-17 to 2018-19: over ₹58,000 crore (same reply) [documented]' on the strength of one PTI/Business Today article. Downgrade it to [reported], and cross-reference the conflict with fcra-receipts c006–c008. 4) Source URL: record the canonical redirect https://www.deccanherald.com/india/ngos-received-over-rs-50000-crore-foreign-donations-since-2016-17-967863.html alongside the amp URL. 5) Karnataka FY2018-19 is printed in the source as 'Rs 1,709.74c crore' (typo in the original). If it is ever used, quote it as ₹1,709.74 cr.

verdicts.dateTest: The claim reads: "MHA (team led by Home Secretary Govind Mohan) told the FCRA Amendment Bill JPC (chair Sanjay Jaiswal) at its first meeting, reported by PTI on 18 Sep 2026, that FCRA associations received ₹22,974 cr in FY2024-25." The dates fit. Mohan is the sitting Home Secretary. The Bill was introduced on 25 Mar 2026 and referred to the JPC on 12 Aug 2026, so a September meeting is plausible. The receipt window 2024-04-01 to 2025-03-31 is right for the amount. The problem is the count: 14,466 is not an FY2024-25 figure. PTI says "there are 14,466 FCRA registered active NGOs", and India CSR says "India currently has 14,466". That is the stock in September 2026. PIB's number is dated to the year: "In 2024-25, around 16,200 associations were actively registered and received approximately Rs 22,963 crore" (PIB FAQ, posted 22 Jul 2026). So the two counts refer to different points in time. The record's note that PIB's figure came "two months earlier" confuses the date PIB published with the date its figure refers to. The claim text "FY2024-25 total ... / 14,466 active" attaches a September 2026 stock to FY2024-25.
verdicts.identityTest: Both figures cover the same entity: the national total of FCRA-registered associations, reported by MHA, the nodal authority. No registration number applies to an aggregate. One wording problem in PTI: "14,466 FCRA registered active NGOs across 15 states". This is most likely loose phrasing, because later in the same article PTI says "the number of active NGOs dipped from 29022 to 14466" as the national figure. Still, it adds doubt about what the 14,466 covers. The task version of the claim lists the PIB URL as a source. PIB does not say ₹22,974 cr or 14,466; it supports only the comparison figure (₹22,963 cr / ~16,200). The record in the file lists ThePrint and India CSR instead. India CSR (20 Sep) is a rewrite of the PTI story ("According to data presented by the Ministry of Home Affairs before a Joint Parliamentary Committee..."), not an independent second outlet.
verdicts.baseRate: Not applicable. This is a national aggregate edge that does not single out any entity, so no discriminating property is being claimed. The ₹22,974 cr and ₹22,963 cr figures differ by ₹11 cr (0.05%). Totals built from FC-4 returns normally move by that much as late or revised returns come in. There is no discrepancy of substance on the amount.
verdicts.denialFound: None found; nobody was asked, and none is needed. MHA is the source of both figures and nobody is accused of anything. PTI reports no statement from MHA or the JPC chair about the difference from the PIB figures. Jaiswal is quoted only on the meeting's cordial atmosphere and the report deadline. My web-search budget was used up, so I could not run a contrary-reporting search beyond the pages already cached. No second independent outlet was found in the scratchpad cache.
verdicts.innocentReading: This is the boring explanation, and it fits all the evidence. The amount did not change in any meaningful way: ₹22,963 cr "approximately" (PIB, July) and ₹22,974 cr (MHA to the JPC, September) are the same FC-4 total, updated slightly as late returns arrived. The counts do not really conflict either. About 16,200 were "actively registered" during FY2024-25, and 14,466 are active now, in September 2026. The gap of roughly 1,700 fits continuing cancellations and lapsed renewals: PTI reports 21,983 cancellations to date, 91.3% of them for not filing annual returns. It could also be a difference in definition ("actively registered" versus "active", meaning filing returns). Either way the counts are sequential or definitional, not contradictory. Nothing here is framed around a family, religion or ethnicity; the religion breakdown in the PTI piece is not part of this edge.
verdicts.reason: Checked word for word, the headline amount survives. verdicts.dateTest: The claim reads: Compassion International (US) gave ₹183.83 cr to FCRA-registered Indian associations in FY2011-12 (2011-04-01 to 2012-03-31), the most of any single donor. The source is Deccan Herald (DHNS), published 20 March 2014, reporting the MHA annual report "Receipt and Utilisation of Foreign Contribution by Voluntary Associations" for 2011-12. It says: "Rs 11,546.29 crore was received in 2011-12." Compassion was operating in India throughout FY2011-12. Its India funding stopped only in 2016 and it left in 2017. So the claimed year falls inside the period Compassion was active, and the from/to fields match FY2011-12. The date test passes.
verdicts.identityTest: The source names "the Compassion International of the US". That matches the entity ngo:compassion-international (Colorado-based child-sponsorship charity). The source gives no registration number because it names the donor, not an Indian registrant. The source does NOT say which Indian associations received the money. The benefit.who field names Compassion East India (CEI) and Caruna Bal Vikas (CBV) as recipients and cites ~580 centres. Those details come from Compassion's 2016 US House testimony, not from the FY2011-12 source. They are plausible but unsourced for this year.
verdicts.baseRate: This does not apply in the usual way. "Largest single donor" belongs to exactly one entity by definition, so the claim is a ranking fact, not a marker that separates suspect entities from others. The second-ranked donor in the same source is a religious body: "Church of Jesus Christ of Latter day Saints of the US (Rs 130.77 crore)". So faith-based donors at the top of the list is normal. The claim supports no inference of wrongdoing and should not carry one.
verdicts.denialFound: None found; not asked. None is needed: this is a neutral figure from a government report, and no one accuses Compassion of anything here. As a rough check, Compassion's own 2016 House testimony gives about US$50m a year to India. ₹183.83 cr at about ₹48–50 per US$ in 2011-12 is about US$37–38m, which is in the same range. verdicts.innocentReading: The ranking reflects Compassion's large, open child-sponsorship programme, which paid per-child sponsorships through many Indian partner associations. verdicts.reason: The source was opened and it confirms the claim word for word: "Foreign donors were topped by the Compassion International of the US (Rs 183.83 crore) followed by Church of Jesus Christ of Latter day Saints of the US (Rs 130.77 crore)" (Deccan Herald, 20 March 2014, reporting the MHA FCRA annual report 2011-12). verdicts.dateTest: The claim as written: Compassion International sent ~US$50m/yr to CEI/CBV from 2011 to April 2016. The Oakley statement (6 Dec 2016, p.2) says: "Until 2016, Compassion sent nearly $50 million per year in humanitarian aid to India". It gives no start year, so "from: 2011" is not in the source; 2011 is only the year the CBV tax audit began. It also does not say "April". April comes from CT, quoting Mellado: "since April blocked roughly $3.5 million in monthly aid". Oakley and Compassion's PRWeb release both say May 2016. The same testimony says the CIT "seized CBV's bank account, forcing them to cease operations in May of 2014", so CBV could not have been receiving US$50m/yr up to 2016. The ₹65/US$ rate only fits roughly 2015–16. Annual averages were about ₹47 (2011), ₹53 (2012), ₹59 (2013) and ₹61 (2014), so ₹325 cr/yr overstates the earlier years of the edge's own window by 25–40%.
verdicts.identityTest: Fails. The source names "India" as the recipient, not CEI or CBV. Compassion's own PRWeb release (March 2017) says: "In May of 2016, India's Ministry of Home Affairs (MHA) began blocking Compassion from sending money to its two country offices and 589 church partners throughout the country." Oakley adds: "Compassion only works through churches which possess a valid license to receive foreign aid." The US$50m therefore went to CEI, CBV and about 589 FCRA-registered church partners combined. An edge ending at ngo:compassion-east-india with a=325 wrongly puts the whole national figure on one association, and one that CBV-side funding had not passed through since May 2014. No FCRA registration number for CEI or CBV is cited. The claim joins two true facts (US$50m/yr to India, and CEI and CBV being the field partners) into a conclusion neither source states.
verdicts.baseRate: Discriminating on scale. The file's own c022 (MHA annual report FY2011-12, via Deccan Herald) names Compassion as the single largest foreign donor, at ₹183.83 cr to all Indian recipients. That national total from MHA data is itself well below the ₹325 cr/yr this edge assigns to CEI/CBV alone. At the FY2011-12 rate (about ₹48/US$), ₹183.83 cr is roughly US$38m. Figures from FCRA returns quoted by IndiaFacts, a partisan source, are ₹133–230 cr/yr for 2009–14 across all FCRA recipients. The claim does not frame a religion or family as the actor; it is an edge between two organisations.
verdicts.denialFound: No one disputes the amount. The dispute is about the ground for the restriction. A senior Home Ministry official told India Today that Compassion was "put under 'prior permission category' for alleged violation of [FCRA]". An MEA spokesperson said "India welcomes lawful operation of foreign NGOs in India". Both are quoted in Christianity Today, 9 Dec 2016: https://www.christianitytoday.com/2016/12/compassion-international-child-sponsorship-india-christmas/. There is no government statement on the US$50m figure; it is the affected party's own number.
verdicts.innocentReading: "Nearly $50m per year" is Compassion's rounded, present-tense figure for its whole India programme, given in advocacy testimony to Congress. It covers two country offices plus about 589 church partners, and it is not an audited transfer to any one Indian association. CT's US$3.5m/month (about US$42m/yr) and the MHA FY2011-12 figure of about US$38m suggest the true annual flow was closer to US$40m, spread across many recipients.
verdicts.reason: The source does not support the recipient, and the recipient is the part that matters for this edge. Oakley says US$50m/yr went "to India", and Compassion's own release says the money went to "two country offices and 589 church partners". Putting ~₹325 cr/yr on the CEI node, over a 2011–April 2016 window, misstates who received the money. The window is also wrong: CBV stopped operating in May 2014, and the source gives no start year. The rupee figure uses a 2016 exchange rate across years when the rupee was much stronger, and it conflicts with the file's own MHA-sourced ₹183.83 cr national total for FY2011-12. The underlying US$ figure does hold at "reported" as the affected party's sworn written statement, repeated by CT. But it has to be an aggregate edge to India, not a CEI/CBV edge.
verdicts.corrections: t: change ngo:compassion-east-india to ngo:fcra-associations-aggregate (or a Compassion-India-partners aggregate node), and keep CEI/CBV only in a benefit.who note with confidence "estimated". text/lab: "Compassion says it sent nearly US$50m/yr to India (two country offices + ~589 FCRA-registered church partners) until transfers were blocked in April–May 2016 — affected party's own figure". a: set to null, or give it per FY using the RBI reference rate for each year (about ₹240 cr at ₹48 in FY2011-12, about ₹330 cr at ₹66 in FY2015-16), and do not apply a single ₹65 rate across 2011–16. from: set to null, since the source gives no start year (drop 2011). to: "2016-05", with a note that Oakley and PRWeb say May and CT says April. d: add that CBV ceased operations in May 2014 when the CIT seized its bank account (Oakley p.3). d: flag the conflict with c022, where MHA's FY2011-12 figure is ₹183.83 cr. srcs: add Compassion's PRWeb release https://www.prweb.com/releases/compassion_international_begins_withdrawing_its_operations_in_india/prweb14105277.htm for the recipient structure, and update the CT URL to https://www.christianitytoday.com/2016/12/compassion-international-child-sponsorship-india-christmas/. verdicts.dateTest: The claim reads: Ayana Charitable Trust declared about ₹826 cr of foreign contribution for FY2015-16 (1 Apr 2015 to 31 Mar 2016), with Gospel for Asia, Hong Kong named in its return as the source of most of it. One error: the Asianet Newsable citation is dated "31 Mar 2018" in srcs[2], but the page's datePublished is 2017-03-20T12:32:00+05:30, the same day as TOI, TNM and Matters India. It is a same-day rewrite of TOI, not a follow-up a year later.
verdicts.identityTest: Recipient: the sources name Ayana Charitable Trust, Thiruvalla, Pathanamthitta. TOI calls it "the new name under which US charity Gospel for Asia is reportedly funding projects in India." No FCRA registration number appears in any source, so identity rests on name and place only. Donor: TOI names "Gospel for Asia, Hong Kong". That is a different legal entity from Gospel for Asia Inc (Wills Point, Texas) and from GFA Canada. The node ngo:gospel-for-asia is labelled "Gospel for Asia (Hong Kong / US)", which merges the two. The claim text then hangs the US lawsuits and the Canadian ~$94m fraud allegation on the donor edge. Those allegations concern GFA US and GFA Canada, not the HK entity the return lists. That is a conjunction problem: the edge implies the allegations attach to this money flow, and no source says they do.
verdicts.baseRate: "Largest FCRA recipient in FY2015-16" describes one entity by definition, so it is not a base-rate property. What matters here is scale and a single foreign donor. The same TOI article gives the symmetry controls with identical fields: Param Shakthi Peeth (Sadhvi Rithambara, "associated in the past with RSS and VHP") was #2 at about ₹417 cr, Believers Church #3 at ₹342.63 cr, World Vision India #4 at ₹319.26 cr, followed by CARE India, RDT, Kiran Nadar Museum of Art, PHFI (Gates a top donor) and The Hans Foundation. Mostly-one-donor funding is common across the top 10 (Compassion to CEI, Gates to PHFI, WVI's parent to WVI), so a dominant foreign parent donor does not discriminate. The edge has to be judged on amount and identity alone, and Param Shakthi Peeth should get a parallel edge with the same fields.
verdicts.denialFound: None found, and they were not asked. TOI, TNM, Matters India and Asianet carry no comment from Ayana, GFA or K.P. Yohannan, and none says they were approached. On the US and Canadian allegations, GFA's own public position (for example, that the 2019 US class-action settlement admitted no wrongdoing) was not opened in this pass because the web-search budget was used up. That position must be sourced before any allegation text stays attached to this record.
verdicts.innocentReading: Ayana is the Indian field arm of the Gospel for Asia network, renamed from GFA India. Mission agencies routinely route donor money through a regional hub (here Hong Kong) to their national partner, and declaring it in FC-4 is exactly what FCRA requires. A large, legally declared, single-parent transfer to an affiliate is how international NGO networks are funded. WVI, Compassion partners and CARE India are funded the same way. The size of the receipt alone shows no wrongdoing.
verdicts.reason: The core edge survives. The TOI original (timesofindia.indiatimes.com/india/christian-ngos-top-in-foreign-funding/articleshow/57723766.cms), opened, says: "A look at Ayana's FCRA returns, which declare its total foreign funding in 2015-16 at a whopping Rs 826 crore, lists Gospel for Asia, Hong Kong, as the source of most of its foreign funds." All three outlets derive from one TOI report, so there is one outlet with named documentary sourcing (the FCRA returns). That is reported, not documented. Several fields are wrong: (1) ₹826.27 cr appears in no source, only "Rs 826 crore"/"Rs 8.26 billion". verdicts.baseRate: Being #2 among roughly 20,000+ FCRA filers is rare by definition, so the property does discriminate. On the other hand, "a religious trust in the top list" is the norm: Ayana, Believers, WVI and RDT are all faith-linked, so having one Hindu entry among them says nothing unusual. The symmetry check passes: the claim applies the same fields and the same TOI/TNM source to the Hindu control as to the Christian recipients in c0xx. verdicts.innocentReading: The figure is what the trust itself reported in its FC-4 return as uploaded to the MHA site. verdicts.dateTest: Claim: World Vision India received about ₹170 cr in foreign contribution in 2022. The Hindu original is by Vijaita Singh, published 21 Jan 2024 and opened at https://www.thehindu.com/news/national/mha-cancels-fcra-registration-of-world-vision-india/article67760041.ece. It says WVI has held FCRA registration since 1986, that the registration was suspended in November 2022 and extended in May 2023, and that it was cancelled in January 2024. So WVI was registered during 2022 and the dates overlap. The article does not say whether "2022" is the calendar year or FY2021-22/FY2022-23. It also does not say "before suspension". That phrase in the claim text is our inference. It is plausible, because WV itself says it has been "unable to receive international funds ... since November 2022". The file's note "likely FY2021-22" is a guess.
verdicts.identityTest: The target node is correct: World Vision India, a society registered under the Tamil Nadu Societies Registration Act, FCRA-registered since 1986. The source node is not supported. The Hindu's sentence is: "In 2022, WVI received around ₹170 crore in foreign donations from its partners in the U.S., Switzerland, and Germany, among others. It also received ₹8 lakh as a donation from the Consulate General of the Federal Republic of Germany." It does not say the money came from World Vision International. The only mention of the parent is that WVI can no longer receive "including from its parent organisation". The node "World Vision International (US)" also mixes up two bodies: World Vision International, the partnership secretariat, and World Vision US, a separate national office. The ₹170 cr is WVI's total foreign contribution from several countries' partners, which may include non-WV donors. It is not a grant from one entity. As an edge from world-vision-international, this is a conjunction the source does not make: the parent exists, and the money was received, but the source never says the parent paid it. No FCRA registration number was given or checked.
verdicts.baseRate: This figure is not evidence of anything. Large Indian affiliates of international NGO federations (Compassion partners, Save the Children/Bal Raksha Bharat, Oxfam India, CARE, Plan, ActionAid, CRY) routinely receive ₹100–400 cr a year from their federation partners, so nearly all comparable entities share the property. The file's symmetry check already records that, measured by money, the largest enforcement events fell on service charities that do not criticise the government, and that the non-filing problem predates 2014 (the UPA control). Applying the same lens to the SPEC's domestic control, the Azim Premji Foundation at ₹1,639 cr a year, shows foreign contribution is a minor stream. The edge implies no wrongdoing and needs none.
verdicts.denialFound: World Vision International statement by Pradeep Daniel, 19 Jan 2024, at https://www.wvi.org/newsroom/world-visions-globally-funded-programming-in-india. It says WV is "profoundly disappointed", that WVI "has been unable to receive international funds into the bank account designated to receive them since November 2022", that the cancellation "only affects our internationally-funded work", and that WVI "is registered under the Tamil Nadu Societies Registration Act, with its own Board of Directors". The Hindu also quotes WVI's financial statement, which says it "has submitted its detailed responses to the MHA for all matters raised ... relating to the periods from 2012-13 to 2020-21". Neither disputes the ₹170 cr figure. It is not known whether The Hindu put the figure to WVI.
verdicts.innocentReading: WVI is a 70-year-old child-sponsorship charity. Its foreign income is pooled sponsorship and grant money routed through the World Vision national offices in the US, Switzerland, Germany and elsewhere, plus a small German consulate grant. Receiving ₹170 cr a year is ordinary for an Indian affiliate of an international federation, and receiving it was lawful while the registration was valid. The suspension and cancellation concern alleged compliance violations for 2012-13 to 2020-21. They do not concern the 2022 receipts.
verdicts.reason: The Hindu original confirms the amount and the recipient: "In 2022, WVI received around ₹170 crore in foreign donations from its partners in the U.S., Switzerland, and Germany, among others". The edge as built does not hold. It records a ₹170 cr grant from ngo:world-vision-international, but the source attributes the money to several unnamed partners in several countries, not to the parent. The source node, and so the edge's meaning, is unsupported. The fact of the receipt survives at the reported tier: one credible outlet, a named reporter, and a figure apparently drawn from WVI's own statements. It does not survive as a grant edge from WV International.

verdicts.dateTest: Actor: MHA, NDA government (2014 onward). Act: placed Compassion International, as a foreign donor, in the prior-permission category, so Indian associations needed MHA clearance before taking its money. When: 2016. The date falls inside the government's tenure, so it passes at year level. The month is disputed. Oakley's testimony (6 Dec 2016, p.3): "In May of 2016, MHA placed Compassion on a list of international NGOs that had to seek prior clearance". India Today (9 Dec 2016) also says "May last". Mellado's piece in The Hill, quoted by CT, says "a secret order issued in February", and CT says transfers were blocked "since April". The record's from:"2016-02" rests only on Mellado. The two sworn or reported sources say May. The ground in the claim, 'not conducive to national interest', belongs to a different act on a different date. It comes from the Times of India of 5 Nov 2016, about MHA refusing to renew the FCRA registrations of 25 associations. It is not about the prior-permission listing.
verdicts.identityTest: The entity is correct. Compassion International Inc. (Colorado Springs) is the foreign donor that was listed. Its Indian partners are Compassion East India and Caruna Bal Vikas, and India Today names both. The attribution is wrong. The claim says the ground is "known only through Compassion's own testimony". The testimony does not contain the phrase 'not conducive to national interest'. It says the reverse: "MHA has never provided Compassion or its partners with any explanation for the prior clearance order" (p.3). Its only national-interest wording is Compassion's own guess: "MHA evidently views Christian values as a threat to the national interest". CT takes the 'not conducive' phrase from the Times of India, not from Compassion: "The official explanation is that Compassion's activities are 'not conducive to national interest,' reported the Times of India". The TOI article (articleshow/55254613, 5 Nov 2016) says MHA "refused to renew the registration of 25 NGOs ... for their alleged indulgence in 'activities not conducive to national interest'". It is about renewal refusals. It does not name Compassion, and it says nothing about the donor listing. The record's d also says "listed May 2016 under s.11(3)(iv)". The testimony says the opposite. Compassion argues that s.11(3)(iv) requires a Gazette notification, that no such notice was given, and that the actual notice was an RBI prior-clearance notice issued on MHA direction under s.46. The claim joins facts that are each true: the donor was listed (May), and MHA gave a generic ground for the renewal refusals (Nov). Put together, they produce a ground for the listing that no source states.
verdicts.baseRate: Being placed in the prior-permission category is rare and targeted. Only a handful of foreign donors were listed in 2015–16: Ford Foundation in April 2015, Greenpeace International, and Compassion. It is far below the 80% non-discriminating threshold. The 'not conducive to national interest' formula is different. It was the standard wording MHA used for a whole batch of 25 renewal refusals in Nov 2016, so it does not tell us why Compassion in particular was listed. On symmetry, the same prior-permission tool was used against the secular Ford Foundation, which funded government critics. The pattern therefore does not show action against Christian donors alone. The claim does not name a religion as the actor, so no kill is needed on that rule.
verdicts.denialFound: A government-side ground is on record, and the claim leaves it out. A senior MHA official told India Today (9 Dec 2016): "We are ready to reconsider the case of Compassion International, the US donor, which was put under 'prior permission category' for alleged violation of Foreign Contribution Regulation Act (FCRA)". The article adds that Compassion "is accused of funding non-Foreign Contribution Regulation Act registered NGOs" (https://www.indiatoday.in/india/delhi/story/us-ngo-compassion-international-foreign-contribution-regulation-act-356547-2016-12-09). The MEA spokesperson, also to India Today and quoted in CT, said "India welcomes lawful operation of foreign NGOs in India" and called the hearing "based on limited understanding of India". Compassion's position is in the testimony: no explanation was ever given, and the renewal refusals cited only "On the basis of Field Agency Report".
verdicts.innocentReading: The government's own account is a compliance problem, not an ideological one. MHA says Compassion was listed because it allegedly sent money to Indian associations that were not registered under FCRA, which the Act restricts. There is some support for this in Compassion's own history. It worked through thousands of partner churches, and its partner CBV had a long-running income-tax dispute (from 2011–13) over transfers to religious-registered charities. The 'national interest' wording belongs to the batch of 25 renewal refusals, not to this listing. Neither the compliance account nor Compassion's discrimination account has been tested in a published order or a court ruling.
verdicts.reason: The central part of the claim is wrong on both points. (1) The ground 'not conducive to national interest' does not come from Compassion's testimony. The testimony says no explanation was ever given. CT gets the phrase from a Times of India story on 25 FCRA renewal refusals, which does not name Compassion or deal with the donor listing. (2) The ground is not 'known only through' Compassion. A senior MHA official is on record in India Today saying the listing was "for alleged violation of FCRA", meaning funding associations not registered under FCRA. The underlying event, MHA putting Compassion in the prior-permission category in 2016, is solid. The testimony, India Today with MHA confirmation, and CT all agree on it, so it holds at 'reported'. Treat it as a single outlet with named sourcing: CT relies on India Today and Compassion rather than doing its own reporting. The ground and the attribution must be rewritten.
verdicts.corrections: text: replace it with "MHA placed Compassion International (US donor) in the FCRA prior-permission category in May 2016 (Oakley testimony; India Today). A senior MHA official gave the ground as 'alleged violation of FCRA' (funding non-FCRA-registered associations). Compassion says no explanation was ever given and alleges religious targeting. MEA: India 'welcomes lawful operation of foreign NGOs'." Drop 'not conducive to national interest' from this edge. That phrase belongs to the Nov 2016 renewal refusals (TOI, 5 Nov 2016) and at most goes on c038 as the batch-level ground, with a note that TOI does not name Compassion's partners. lab: remove "ground 'not conducive to national interest' (per Compassion)". d: remove "listed May 2016 under s.11(3)(iv)". Replace it with "listed May 2016 by an RBI prior-clearance notice issued on MHA direction under s.46. Compassion argues no s.11(3)(iv) Gazette notification was issued." Keep the Mellado/CT claim of a February order as a disputed alternative. from: change "2016-02" to "2016-05", and note the February claim. tier: raise from alleged to reported for the listing event. srcs: add India Today, 9 Dec 2016 (https://www.indiatoday.in/india/delhi/story/us-ngo-compassion-international-foreign-contribution-regulation-act-356547-2016-12-09), the source of the MHA official's statement. c037: add the MHA official's ground and his offer to reconsider next to the MEA quote. Its d currently implies there was no government-side ground. killIf/upgradeIf: keep upgradeIf (an MHA order or a Parliament answer). Change killIf to "order or Parliament answer shows a ground other than FCRA violation / non-registered recipients".

verdicts.dateTest: Claim as written: "MHA refused FCRA renewal of CEI and CBV, Nov 2016". Actor window: MHA under the NDA government (Rajnath Singh was Home Minister May 2014 to May 2019), so the dates overlap and this core passes. The bundled facts do not. (a) The CBV income-tax audit was notified in 2011, the >US$18m assessment came in May 2013 and the bank account was seized in May 2014. The source says: "In 2011, [Compassion's] field-partner in South India, Caruna Bal Vikas (CBV), was notified that it was selected for an audit by the Commissioner of Income Tax (CIT). In May of 2013 ... the CIT assessed CBV more than $18 million". That action was taken by the Income Tax Department under the UPA government, before NDA took office. It is not an MHA act and it falls outside the NDA window. (b) The ED probe of CEI (Aug 2016) is an Enforcement Directorate action. ED sits under the Finance Ministry's Department of Revenue, not MHA. The 'from: 2016-11' date is correct for the refusal only. Note that the source says Compassion "learned" of the refusal in November 2016. The actual order date is not given.
verdicts.identityTest: Weak. The source names "Compassion East India (CEI)" and "Caruna Bal Vikas (CBV)" with no FCRA registration number, city or registered address. Both nodes have identity.fcra = null but are marked resolved:true. The node subtitles "Kolkata-based" (CEI) and "Chennai-based" (CBV) are not in the source, which says only "field-partner in South India" for CBV and gives no location for CEI. The edge target is CEI only, but the text also asserts a refusal and a tax demand against CBV (ngo:caruna-bal-vikas), so the edge covers two entities.
verdicts.baseRate: Compassion's own account, relayed by Christianity Today on 9 Dec 2016, says renewals were refused for "Compassion and at least 24 other NGOs" in the 2016 renewal cycle. That is about 25 refusals against a renewal pool of thousands. Separately, thousands of registrations lapsed for non-application. So a refusal is rare (well under 80%) and discriminating in itself. A refusal preceded by a donor prior-permission listing (Compassion was one of a handful of donors so listed in 2016, alongside Ford Foundation in 2015) is rarer still. Symmetry: the CBV tax action this claim bundles in began under UPA (2011–13), and sibling records (fcra-actions.json symmetryCheck) show UPA using the same unreasoned suspension and cancellation instrument on INSAF, CPSC and the Kudankulam associations. The anti-Compassion reading is therefore not NDA-specific for the tax component.
verdicts.denialFound: An MHA-side response exists, so c039's "no response recorded" is wrong. Times of India (Bharti Jain), 13 Dec 2016: "'We have no immediate plans to reconsider the case of Compassion International ... which was put under prior permission category for alleged violation of Foreign Contribution Regulation Act (FCRA),' a senior home ministry official said"; "put under prior permission category in March this year after intelligence agencies flagged its alleged role in encouraging religious conversions and proselytisation through Indian NGOs funded by it." https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/india/No-prior-permission-relief-for-US-NGO-Compassion-International/articleshow/55966483.cms . The Hindu, 13 Dec 2016: "accused of promoting religious conversion and funding of non-FCRA registered NGOs." https://www.thehindu.com/news/national/Home-Ministry-firm-on-Compassion/article16801760.ece . MEA via CT: "There is a well-established legal framework for NGOs to conduct their operations in India." These responses address the prior-permission listing, not specifically the CEI/CBV non-renewals. On the CEI/CBV refusals themselves, the source quotes the refusal letter's ground: "On the basis of Field Agency Report, the competent authority has decided to refuse your application". Whether the partners were asked for comment by any outlet: not found.
verdicts.innocentReading: MHA refused renewal on an adverse field-agency (IB) report. That is the ground quoted in the letter the source cites, and it matches MHA's public position that Compassion's partners passed foreign money to churches and NGOs not registered under FCRA, which is an FCRA s.7 onward-transfer problem. The CIT 2013 assessment concerned a charitable-vs-religious trust classification under income-tax law, a routine revenue dispute, and it began under the previous government. On this reading the refusals follow from a funding-structure compliance issue (Compassion's church-partner intermediary model), not from religious animus. The later 2020 FCRA amendment banning sub-granting to anyone points the same way.
verdicts.reason: The source (Oakley's written testimony, opened and read in full) does support the core fact as Compassion's account: "in November of 2016, Compassion learned that both its partners, CBV and CEI, had been denied FCRA renewal without explanation", the ED probe of CEI for "anti-national activity" in Aug 2016, and the CIT assessment of more than $18 million. The claim fails as written for four reasons. (1) The same document contradicts "without explanation" by quoting the refusal letter's stated ground: "On the basis of Field Agency Report ...". The record's own killIf is "Orders show a stated ground". The ground shown is formulaic and was not shared, so this is a correction rather than a kill. (2) It is a conjunction edge that credits MHA with an ED action (Finance Ministry) and a CIT assessment from 2011–13 (Income Tax Department, under UPA). (3) The "MHA side: no response recorded" is false: senior MHA officials on record in TOI and The Hindu (13 Dec 2016) cite an alleged FCRA violation, intelligence flags on conversion, and funding of non-FCRA-registered NGOs. (4) The only source is the affected party's own advocacy testimony. Under the CONTRACT a named party asserting something is 'alleged', not 'reported'. No independent outlet or MHA order corroborating the CEI/CBV refusals was opened; CT only relays Compassion's statement.
verdicts.corrections: 1. tier: reported -> alleged (sole source is Compassion's own congressional testimony), and keep the contra. 2. Text/d: replace "denied ... 'without explanation'" with "refused, per Compassion, on the stated ground 'On the basis of Field Agency Report' (report not shared with the partners); Compassion calls this 'without explanation'". 3. Remove the ED probe and the CBV CIT demand from this MHA 'enforce' edge. Record them as separate edges: ED (Finance Ministry / Dept of Revenue) -> CEI, Aug 2016, alleged; and Income Tax Dept (CIT) -> CBV, audit 2011, assessment May 2013 (UPA period), bank account seized May 2014, alleged. 4. Split the target: add a separate MHA -> ngo:caruna-bal-vikas enforce edge for CBV's non-renewal, so this edge covers CEI only. 5. c039: change from "No response recorded" to a contra quoting the senior MHA official (TOI and The Hindu, 13 Dec 2016): alleged FCRA violation, intelligence flags on conversion, funding of non-FCRA-registered NGOs. Note that this addresses the prior-permission listing and that no MHA statement specific to the CEI/CBV refusals was found. Add the MEA line from CT. 6. Nodes: drop "Kolkata-based" and "Chennai-based" (not in source), or add a source for them. Set resolved:false until FCRA registration numbers are found. 7. Add base-rate context: about 25 renewal refusals in the Nov 2016 cycle (per Compassion via CT). 8. upgradeIf: add "FCRA portal status or refusal orders for CEI/CBV with registration numbers; any Delhi HC appeal record".

verdicts.dateTest: Claim: MHA cancelled the FCRA registrations of Believers Church, Ayana Charitable Trust, Love India Ministries and Last Hour Ministry "in Oct 2017". The Christian Post piece is dated 7 Oct 2017 and says only that MHA "has cancelled the registrations". It gives no date for the cancellation itself. The spokesperson says the registrations had been "under revision for the last one year" under a "standing revision order". So the action, or the process leading to it, may be earlier than Oct 2017. MHA is a standing ministry, so there is no tenure-overlap problem. The date problem is precision: "Oct 2017" is when it was reported, not a proven date of the order.
verdicts.identityTest: The source names "the southern India-based Believers Church and three of its affiliates — Ayana Charitable Trust (formerly Gospel for Asia India), Love India Ministries and Last Hour Ministry". The node ngo:believers-eastern-church uses the church's later name (Believers Eastern Church). That is the same body, but the edge covers four associations, each with its own FCRA registration number. The only target node is the church, and no registration numbers were recorded, so the other three are carried in text only. No DIN or CIN applies.
verdicts.baseRate: Cancellation is not a discriminating property. The article itself says MHA cancelled 10,011 licences in 2015 and six in 2016. Tens of thousands of registrations were cancelled or lapsed under the NDA government, and more than 4,000 were cancelled under the UPA government in 2011–14, including the 2012 Kudankulam-linked ones. The groups hit include Christian ones (Compassion partners 2016) and secular and critical ones (Greenpeace, Amnesty, Lawyers Collective). One cancellation shows nothing about targeting. The edge does not claim targeting, so it passes, provided no narrative stacks it into a "crackdown on Christians" pattern without the SPEC controls.
verdicts.denialFound: A response exists, in the same source. Believers Church spokesperson Fr Sijo Panthapallil: "Our FCRA registrations are under revision for the last one year. They had sent us a letter asking for documents and we have submitted the required documents" and "We are sure that we will get the registrations back next week." This is recorded as c041. It describes the process and expects restoration; it does not deny that the registrations were cancelled or suspended. MHA gave no stated ground in the piece, and whether MHA was asked for comment is unknown.
verdicts.innocentReading: This is an ordinary regulatory action. The affiliated Gospel for Asia network faced US allegations of misusing donations, including a US class action settled in 2019, and the registrations were under a year-long document "revision". A cancellation or non-renewal for compliance or accounting reasons fits the facts. So does the church's own account that this was a pending review it expected to be reversed. Nothing in the source ties the action to religion, apart from the outlet's editorial lede about a "Hindu nationalist party".
verdicts.reason: The opened source supports the core claim, attributed: MHA cancelled the FCRA registrations of these four named associations, the ground is not stated, and the church spokesperson expected restoration. The claim uses a neutral agency→association framing with no religion as actor, and a response is recorded as c041. That supports "reported". It is not "documented": Christian Post is itself relaying one outlet (The Times of India, not opened, and the fetch failed), and no MHA order or Parliament answer was opened. The two defects are precision, not substance: the date is the report date, and the scope may be a revision or suspension rather than a final cancellation.
verdicts.corrections: 1) Date: change "from":"2017-10" to show it is a reported-by date. Either set d to "cancellation reported 7 Oct 2017 (Christian Post citing Times of India); order date not stated", or put "by 2017-10-07" in the text. The claim text "in Oct 2017" should read "reported Oct 2017". 2) Source chain: note in d or srcs that Christian Post is relaying The Times of India ("according to The Times of India"), so this is one outlet, second-hand. Add the TOI original as the primary report if it can be retrieved. 3) Scope: add to d that the spokesperson called it a "standing revision order" with registrations "under revision for the last one year", so the status may be cancellation pending revision; killIf already covers this. 4) Identity: record the FCRA registration numbers for all four associations. Either add nodes/edges for Ayana Charitable Trust, Love India Ministries and Last Hour Ministry, or state in d that the edge target stands for the group. 5) Amount: if the Ayana figure (~US$206m, "last financial year", per TOI) is used anywhere, mark it as TOI-sourced, give its FY, and convert it to ₹ crore with the rate cited. 6) c041: relabel it as a response rather than a denial. It does not dispute the cancellation; it expects restoration. 7) Follow-up: check whether the registrations were in fact restored (later reporting on Believers Eastern Church FCRA status, e.g. the 2020 IT searches) and add a supersede edge if they were not.

verdicts.dateTest: The claim reads: MHA cancelled CPR's FCRA registration, and CPR received the notice on 2024-01-10. The act falls under the current NDA government, with Amit Shah as Home Minister since 2019-05-30 (c065), so the dates overlap. The Tribune (dateline New Delhi, 19 Jan 2024; updated 20 Jan) quotes CPR: "On January 10, CPR received a notice from the Ministry of Home Affairs cancelling its FCRA status." Tribune calls the public event "the January 17 action". PTI (The Week, 17 Jan 2024) matches. from=2024-01-10 is when CPR received the notice. The date of the order itself was not seen, so it may be a few days earlier. That is not a conflict. It came after two 180-day suspensions that began in Feb 2023, and after the Income Tax 'survey' of Sept 2022, which the Tribune also mentions.
verdicts.identityTest: The source names "well-known think tank Centre for Policy Research (CPR)". CPR's own statement names the "Ministry of Home Affairs" as the authority that cancelled, which matches s=min:ministry-of-home-affairs and t=ngo:centre-for-policy-research. No FCRA registration number was given in any source opened, so the entity match rests on the name and CPR's own statement. There is no ambiguity. The claim is not a conjunction of separate facts: the cancellation and CPR's quote both come from one sentence in the same article, and CPR itself confirms the notice, which goes against its own interest.
verdicts.baseRate: Tribune, citing MHA data, reports that more than 16,000 FCRA licences were cancelled in 2015–2024, and 1,827 were cancelled for violations in 2018–22 (RS answer, March 2023). Being cancelled is therefore common and does not single CPR out. That is fine, because the edge records one event and draws no inference from it. Symmetry: the same lens gives the same 'enforce' edge for the UPA-era cancellations in 2012, including the Kudankulam-linked NGOs, which is the SPEC control. The claim makes no claim about political targeting, and none should be added to it. No family, religion or ethnicity is framed as the actor. (OpIndia's 'run by Mani Shankar Aiyar's daughter' framing must not be imported.)
verdicts.denialFound: CPR's response is already in the claim and is verbatim in the Tribune: "The basis of this decision is incomprehensible and disproportionate and some of the reasons given challenge the very basis of the functioning of a research institution. This includes the publication on our website of policy reports emanating from our research being equated with current affairs programming." CPR said it would seek legal remedy. It then challenged the cancellation in the Delhi HC, and Justice Chandra Dhari Singh issued notice to the Centre (Bar & Bench, 26 Mar 2024: https://www.barandbench.com/news/delhi-high-court-seeks-governments-reply-plea-centre-for-policy-research-fcra-cancellation). MHA's side, via officials quoted by PTI (https://www.theweek.in/wire-updates/national/2024/01/17/del65--mha-fcra-2ndld-cpr.html): CPR was "misutilising foreign funds to affect India's economic interests, and aid protests and legal battles against development projects"; it "diverted foreign donation to non-FCRA entity"; and "Publishing current affairs programme using foreign funding is prohibited under section 3 of the Act". The claim does not include these grounds.
verdicts.innocentReading: This is a routine regulatory action under FCRA sections 3, 8 and 14, after a year of suspension and an Income Tax survey. MHA gave specific grounds: transfers to non-FCRA entities, funding litigation and paralegals against coal projects, and publishing 'current affairs' content. CPR disputes those grounds, and the dispute is before the Delhi HC. The edge only records that the enforcement happened. It does not say whether the grounds were valid or the action was proportionate, so it should not be read as proving harassment.
verdicts.reason: The one cited source (Tribune, 19 Jan 2024) states the cancellation, the 10 Jan notice date, MHA as the actor and CPR's quoted words, all in one quoted sentence. The fact is independently confirmed by PTI (The Week), Business Standard and CPR's own statement, and the Delhi HC challenge confirms an order exists. Nothing refutes it. 'Reported' fits the evidence in the file, since only one outlet is cited. It qualifies for 'documented' once a second independent outlet (PTI/Business Standard) or the MHA order or HC record is added to srcs. The one weakness is balance: the text gives CPR's rebuttal but not MHA's stated grounds.
verdicts.corrections: 1) Add MHA's stated grounds to text/d, attributed to officials via PTI, and note they are still disputed: diverting foreign contribution to non-FCRA entities; funding litigation and protests against development projects; section 3 'current affairs programme'. Keep them at alleged status because the case is sub judice. 2) Add PTI/The Week (17 Jan 2024) and Business Standard (https://www.business-standard.com/india-news/mha-cancels-fcra-registration-of-cpr-for-charging-violation-of-norms-124011700289_1.html) to srcs. With a second independent outlet the fact of cancellation can move to 'documented'. 3) In d, record that from=2024-01-10 is the date CPR received the notice, not the date of the order. Public disclosure was 2024-01-17, and Tribune calls it "the January 17 action". Also record the prior suspensions from Feb 2023 (180 days plus a 180-day extension). 4) Add a Delhi HC writ entry (notice issued Mar 2024, Justice Chandra Dhari Singh) as a pending contra or status, and set killIf/upgradeIf to include the HC outcome: an HC order quashing the cancellation should supersede the edge. 5) The text should say 'Centre/MHA' as Tribune does. Do not bring in OpIndia's family framing.

verdicts.dateTest: Claim: MHA withheld RDT's FCRA renewal (2024) and cleared it (March 2026). Deccan Chronicle (Nagabhushanam Hoskote, published 2024-03-23T13:19+05:30) says the renewal "is still pending" and "This has led to denial of renewal", so a 2024 start holds. The South First (Raj Rayasam, 25 Mar 2026) says Ferrer met Naidu on "Tuesday, 24 March" to thank him for the "restoration of foreign funding", and TOI, Indian Express, NIE and The Hindu all ran renewal reports on 24–25 Mar 2026. So March 2026 holds. The record leaves out the middle of the timeline. NIE (30 Apr 2025, fetched) reports "non-renewal of its FCRA licence" as a crisis, which suggests the formal refusal came around April 2025 and the 2024 status was 'pending'. A Hans India headline dated 9 Oct 2025 ("Central govt renews FCRA approval for RDT") conflicts with the March 2026 clearance date. It returned 404 and I could not check it; it may have been an interim or prior-permission step. The date window from 2024 to 2026-03 has no overlap problem: Shah has been Home Minister throughout and Naidu has been CM since June 2024.
verdicts.identityTest: It is the right entity. Both sources name the Rural Development Trust, Anantapur, founded in 1969 by Vicente Ferrer, with programme director Moncho (DC spells it 'Manchu') Ferrer. Neither source gives an FCRA registration number, so the node is identified by name and place only. On the actor: the ground comes from an IB report, but MHA is the FCRA authority, so s=min:ministry-of-home-affairs is the right node for the non-renewal. It should not be read as MHA stating the conversion ground.
verdicts.baseRate: Weak discrimination. Many NGOs with Christian roots or foreign founders lost or failed to renew FCRA registration between 2021 and 2025, and several were restored after lobbying (Missionaries of Charity: renewal refused Dec 2021, restored Jan 2022). Non-renewal after a conversion complaint is common in this class and says nothing specific about RDT. Politicians intervening for large regional service NGOs is also common. On symmetry, the lobbying came from all sides. TDP MPs/MLAs met Shah (Aug 2025, The Hindu/DC/NIE). Opposition YSRCP chief Jagan also thanked the Centre for the renewal (The Hindu, 24 Mar 2026). Credit also went to BC minister S. Savitha/Yadav (Hans India, 2 Apr 2026). The 'beneficiary-by-intervention' reading therefore applies to the whole AP political spectrum, not just the NDA ally.
verdicts.denialFound: RDT denial, Deccan Chronicle 23 Mar 2024 (https://www.deccanchronicle.com/news/non-renewal-of-rdts-fcra-threatens-3k-jobs-medical-aid-886199): "the Rural Development Trust has maintained that it has never encouraged any religious conversions in the past 55 years of its existence. The organisation said it has even dismissed persons from its employment in case they have a tendency of converting people." This is already recorded as c047. No MHA or IB statement of the ground was found, and MHA was not asked in either source.
verdicts.innocentReading: The renewal may have been held up by routine MHA verification after complaints, and by the April 2025 refusal. It was later granted once the file was reviewed, and cross-party representations from both TDP and YSRCP may only have sped it up. Clearing a large secular hospital and development trust that serves 8.5 lakh patients a year is consistent with the merits, and a clearance 'after' lobbying does not show it happened 'because of' lobbying.
verdicts.reason: Both sources say what the claim says. DC: "Intelligence Bureau (IB) has reportedly filed a report that RDT is involved in religious conversions in Pathikonda area of Kurnool district, based on inquiries made after anonymous persons had complained. This has led to denial of renewal." South First: "Chief Minister Chandrababu Naidu is learnt to have personally raised the matter with Union Home Minister Amit Shah... the Centre has now granted the necessary clearances." The ground comes from a 'reportedly' IB report and not from an MHA order, so the tier stays alleged. It has a named denial (c047), and the clearance is correctly split out as reported (c048). The claim is not refuted, but it has timeline and framing gaps that need correcting.
verdicts.corrections: 1) Timeline: say "renewal pending/not granted from early 2024 (DC 23 Mar 2024); formal non-renewal reported Apr 2025 (NIE 30 Apr 2025); renewed Mar 2026". Add the NIE Apr 2025 source. Check and reconcile the Hans India 9 Oct 2025 "Central govt renews FCRA approval" headline against the Mar 2026 date. 2) Complainants: 'anonymous complaints' is DC's wording. A named complainant, Legal Rights Protection Forum (LRPF), publicly sought cancellation in March 2024 (Organiser 28 Mar 2024; Commune 24 Mar 2024; Indian Express 28 Mar 2024, 'NGO accuses 2 organisations of religious conversions'). Add LRPF to the record, and add Commune's Apr 2025 reporting of 'fund misuse' allegations as a possible second ground. 3) The c046 record's srcs array lists only DC, while the narrative text also cites South First. Either add the SF URL or move the clearance sentence to c048 only. 4) Framing: 'beneficiary-by-intervention' should record that the intervention was cross-party (TDP MPs/MLAs Aug 2025; YSRCP's Jagan thanked the Centre, The Hindu 24 Mar 2026) and that SF says Naidu "is learnt to have" raised it, which is hedged, not confirmed. 5) Spelling: programme director is 'Moncho Ferrer' (DC writes 'Manchu'). 6) killIf/upgradeIf are fine. Keep tier alleged; do not upgrade until an MHA order or Parliament answer states the ground.

verdicts.dateTest: Claim: the MHA renewed RDT's FCRA registration in March 2026 after AP CM Naidu (and Lokesh) raised it with Amit Shah. Tenures overlap. Naidu has been CM since June 2024, Lokesh has been IT/Education minister since June 2024, and Shah has been Home Minister since 2019. South First is dated 25 Mar 2026 (datePublished 2026-03-25T14:19:54+05:30), and the Ferrer–Naidu meeting was on Tue 24 Mar. Deccan Chronicle reports the renewal ran from 23 Mar 2026 to 22 Mar 2031. IANS (via NewsGram, 24 Mar 2026) quotes Jagan saying permissions were 'halted on April 21, 2025'. That conflicts with sibling claim c046, which dates the non-renewal to 2024 from a DC article of 23 Mar 2024. c046 should be reconciled, possibly as a 2024 withholding followed by a 21 Apr 2025 rejection. c048's 'from: 2026-03' is correct.
verdicts.identityTest: Entity match: every source names 'Rural Development Trust (RDT)', based in Anantapur and founded in 1969 by Vicente Ferrer, and programme director Moncho Ferrer is named. No FCRA registration number appears in any source or in the record, so this is a name match only. Add the FCRA regn no. from the fcraonline registered-association list. Actors: 'Andhra Pradesh Chief Minister N. Chandrababu Naidu', 'Union Home Minister Amit Shah', 'IT and Education Minister Nara Lokesh'. All three are correctly identified by office.
verdicts.baseRate: Cross-party and state-government lobbying for a big regional employer's FCRA renewal is common and does not discriminate by party. Here ruling TDP MLAs/MLCs, the opposition YSRCP, the CPI and CPM, and civil society ran a joint campaign, with about 1 lakh postcards and delegations to Delhi. Jagan (YSRCP, the AP opposition) also thanked Modi and Shah. Symmetry control from SPEC: Missionaries of Charity's FCRA registration was also refused (Dec 2021) and restored within about two weeks (Jan 2022, Tribune) with no state lobbying on record. So restoration after refusal happens with or without a state CM's intervention. We have no MHA count of how many refused renewals are later granted, so the discriminating power of 'intervention preceded clearance' is unknown and probably low.
verdicts.denialFound: MHA: none found. No order, reasons or PIB release was located, and there is no record that MHA was asked. Contrary account: YS Jagan Mohan Reddy (IANS via NewsGram, 24 Mar 2026, https://www.newsgram.com/india/2026/03/24/andhra-jagan-thanks-pm-modi-for-fcra-renewal-for-rural-development-trust) says 'the renewal was achieved through public pressure and collective struggle, not through any initiative from the ruling leadership' and calls Naidu's claim 'credit appropriation'. Supporting account: Naidu's own X post (quoted by IANS) says that after 'submitting a petition to the Union Home Minister ... with his special intervention, the hurdles have been cleared today'. Deccan Chronicle reports that the IB cleared the renewal proposal.
verdicts.innocentReading: MHA reviewed the April 2025 refusal. Per DC, the IB then cleared the renewal proposal, and a five-year renewal was issued on 23 Mar 2026. A state government lobbying for a 55-year-old NGO that employs about 3,000 people and runs hospitals is routine federal advocacy. The campaign crossed party lines, including the rival YSRCP and the Left. The timing fits a review process, public pressure, lobbying, or all three. Naidu claiming credit is ordinary political positioning, and his rival disputes it.
verdicts.reason:
The core fact holds and is corroborated by several outlets: South First, Deccan Chronicle, Hans India, and IANS/NewsGram, which quotes Naidu's own X post. The reported facts are that the MHA renewed RDT's FCRA registration around 23 Mar 2026 and that Naidu petitioned Shah beforehand. Three parts of the claim text go beyond the cited source.
(1) The cited source does not say Lokesh intervened with Shah. It says only that Lokesh 'had earlier assured intervention after the issue was brought to his attention' and that he called his role 'minimal'.
(2) South First hedges Naidu's role: 'Chief Minister Chandrababu Naidu is learnt to have personally raised the matter with Union Home Minister Amit Shah'. The flat causal claim 'political intervention restoring access' is Naidu's own claim. Jagan disputes it, and the IB-clearance account offers a process explanation.
(3) The edge predicate 'enforce' is wrong for a grant of renewal.
These are fixes, not grounds to kill. The event survives at reported. The causation must be attributed to Naidu, and Jagan's contra must be recorded.
verdicts.corrections:
1. Text: rewrite as "MHA renewed RDT's FCRA registration (effective 23 Mar 2026 to 22 Mar 2031) after a refusal on 21 Apr 2025; CM Naidu says he petitioned Home Minister Amit Shah, whose 'special intervention' cleared it (Naidu on X, via IANS); South First says Naidu 'is learnt to have' raised it with Shah; Lokesh had 'assured intervention'. Opposition leader Jagan attributes the renewal to cross-party public pressure."
2. Remove "Nara Lokesh intervened with Home Minister Amit Shah" unless the DC article is opened and states it.
3. pred: change 'enforce' to a grant/approve/renew predicate. The renewal is not enforcement.
4. Add srcs: Deccan Chronicle https://www.deccanchronicle.com/southern-states/andhra-pradesh/naidu-thanks-modi-amit-shah-for-resolving-rdt-foreign-funding-1945895 ; Hans India https://www.thehansindia.com/andhra-pradesh/central-govt-renews-fcra-approval-for-rdt-leaders-efforts-bear-fruit-1013052 ; IANS/NewsGram https://www.newsgram.com/india/2026/03/24/andhra-jagan-thanks-pm-modi-for-fcra-renewal-for-rural-development-trust . With independent outlets on the renewal itself, the renewal fact alone could be tiered 'documented'. The causal intervention stays reported/attributed.
5. Add a contra edge: Jagan (YSRCP) disputing the causation.
6. Benefit: keep who/how, but note the benefit comes from the renewal itself. Do not record a benefit as flowing from political intervention without an MHA order stating its grounds.
7. Add the FCRA registration number.
8. Flag c046's '2024' vs IANS's 'halted April 21, 2025' for reconciliation.
9. innocentReading: add the cross-party campaign and the reported IB clearance.

verdicts.dateTest: Claim as a sentence: MHA (Home Secretary Govind Mohan's team) told the JPC on the FCRA Amendment Bill, 18 Sep 2026, that 21,983 registrations had been cancelled "so far". The actor and the date line up: the first JPC meeting, PTI/ThePrint 18 Sep 2026. However, the record's "from":"2011" is our own inference. The source says only "so far" and gives no start year, so "cumulative since 2011" cannot be sourced. The comparison window (RS Q.3253: 2020 to 22.03.2023) sits inside the cumulative window. Overlapping windows cannot by themselves produce a contradiction.
verdicts.identityTest: The actor is correct. PTI: "This was conveyed by the Ministry of Home Affairs at the first meeting of the Joint Committee of Parliament ... A team of MHA officials, led by Union Home Secretary Govind Mohan, told the JPC". The target is an aggregate of FCRA associations, so no FCRA registration number applies. IndiaCSR is not an independent second source. It reproduces the PTI sentence word for word ("The government has so far cancelled FCRA registration of 21983 NGOs — 91.3 per cent for not filing annual returns, 7.9 per cent for being inactive, 0.4 per cent for legal violations."), so the figure rests on a single wire report. "Reported" is the right tier for the figures, not "documented".
verdicts.baseRate: Non-filing of FC-4 returns is the dominant cancellation ground in every period for which MHA has given figures. Examples: the mass cancellations of 2015–17, and the 2020 s.50 one-time exemption for associations "cancelled u/s 14 for non-submission of annual returns". A 91% non-filing share is therefore expected and tells you nothing about any government or target. The figure is an aggregate, so the UPA-vs-NDA and critical-vs-aligned controls from the SPEC cannot be applied to it. It does not frame any family, religion or ethnicity as the actor.
verdicts.denialFound: None found. MHA was not asked. The "non-reconciliation" is our own inference and has never been put to MHA. No contrary reporting found.
verdicts.innocentReading: RS Q.3253 (d) reads: "Section 14 ... provides for cancellation of certificate of FCRA registration of an association for violations of provisions of the Act ... 1,828 associations have been cancelled under section 14 ... due to violation of the provisions of the Act and rules made thereunder." Section 14 is the Act's only cancellation route. Failing to file FC-4 returns breaches s.18 read with Rule 17, which is a "violation of the Act and rules". So cancellations for non-filing are s.14 "violation" cancellations. Inactivity cancellations also fall under s.14 (s.14(1)(c): defunct or no reasonable activity). The JPC breakdown splits s.14 cancellations by ground: non-filing 91.3%, inactive 7.9%, substantive "legal violations" 0.4%. The Q.3253 figure of 1,828 is the s.14 total for 2020–23 across all grounds. The two classifications nest; they do not conflict. Since 1,828 is about 8.3% of 21,983, the numbers are consistent with each other.
verdicts.reason: The source confirms the underlying figures exactly (21,983; 91.3%; 7.9%; 0.4%; MHA to JPC). But the claim's decisive clause, that this "does not reconcile with RS Q.3253's 1,828 s.14 'violation' cancellations 2020–23", appears in neither source. It is our own inference, and it rests on a misreading. Q.3253 uses "violation" for every s.14 cancellation ("violation of the provisions of the Act and rules made thereunder"), and that includes non-filing of annual returns. The JPC's "legal violations" is a narrower sub-ground. Joining two true facts produced a contradiction that neither source contains. As phrased, the claim is refuted. The bare figures survive at the "reported" tier.
verdicts.corrections: 1) text: delete "— does not reconcile with RS Q.3253's 1,828 s.14 'violation' cancellations 2020–23". Replace with the figures only: "MHA told JPC (18 Sep 2026) 21,983 FCRA registrations cancelled so far — 91.3% non-filing of annual returns, 7.9% inactive, 0.4% legal violations." 2) d: remove "the two classifications do not reconcile". Replace with: "Q.3253's 1,828 are all s.14 cancellations 2020–23, and 'violation of the Act and rules' there includes non-filing (s.18/Rule 17); the JPC percentages sub-classify s.14 grounds. 0.4% of 21,983 ≈ 88 substantive-violation cancellations; base period not stated." 3) from: change "2011" to null or "unstated". PTI says only "so far". 4) srcs: mark IndiaCSR as a verbatim copy of PTI, not an independent corroboration. 5) Remove the matching entry in the file's gaps array, or rewrite it as the nesting explanation. 6) If any comparison with Q.3253 is kept, make it a separate analytic claim with the innocentReading above. 7) Keep upgradeIf "JPC record / MHA presentation published". killIf stays "Record differs".

verdicts.dateTest: The claim, written out: MHA (MoS Nityanand Rai) told the Rajya Sabha on 15 Mar 2023 that 16,383 associations held valid FCRA registration as on 10 Mar 2023, and DH (15 Mar 2023, 21:25 IST) reported the West Bengal state row of that same answer as all-India totals. The dates line up. The primary source is RS Unstarred Q.1662 (Satish Chandra Dubey), answered 15.03.2023. The file cites RS Q.3253 instead. That is a different question, answered two weeks later on 29.03.2023 and built from returns filed as on 22.03.2023, so its figures are slightly different. The file's `d` says 'RS answer of 15 Mar 2023' and then cross-checks against the 29 Mar answer. That is a date mismatch inside the source chain, although it does not change the substance.
verdicts.identityTest: The entity is the national aggregate of FCRA associations, and the West Bengal row is a named row in the state-wise annexure, so there is no identity ambiguity. Rai is correctly named as MoS Home in both answers. The exact numbers check out. In RS Q.1662 Annexure I (15.03.2023), row 34 'West Bengal' reads 727.16 / 798.18 / 905.50 for FY2019-20 / 2020-21 / 2021-22. These match DH exactly, and DH's lede 'total of Rs 2,430.84 crore in the last three years' is exactly the sum of that West Bengal row. In the cited Q.3253 (29.03.2023), the West Bengal row is 727.20 / 798.18 / 906.12. That is close, but it is not the figures the claim text quotes.
verdicts.baseRate: Not applicable. This is a media-accuracy and source-chain claim, not a claim that an entity shares a suspicious property. No discriminating inference about any actor depends on a base rate.
verdicts.denialFound: None found; DH was not asked. The DH article, still live, carries no correction note. Its text reads: 'Rai said an amount of Rs 905.50 crore in foreign funding was received by NGOs in 2021-22, Rs 798.18 crore in 2020-21 and Rs 727.16 crore in 2019-20' and 'Indian NGOs received a total of Rs 2,430.84 crore in foreign funding in the last three years.' (https://www.deccanherald.com/amp/story/india%2Ffcra-of-1827-ngos-cancelled-between-2018-22-1200438.html). I could not run a web search for a later correction or for contrary reporting because the search budget was exhausted.
verdicts.innocentReading: This was a reporting slip. The annexure is a state-wise table with no total row, and West Bengal is its last row (Sl. 34). A reporter reading to the bottom of the table plausibly took that row as the total. Nothing suggests intent. The actual national sums in Q.1662 are ₹16,306.04 / 17,058.64 / 22,085.10 cr, about 22-24x the West Bengal row. The file's innocentReading ('~20x') is consistent with that.
verdicts.reason: The claim survives. The primary Parliament answer for the date DH reported on, RS USQ 1662 of 15.03.2023, confirms every part of it. It says 'As on 10/03/2023, FCRA registration certificate of 16383 number of Associations is valid, out of which 14966 ... have submitted mandatory Annual Returns for FY 2021-22.' Its Annexure I West Bengal row is exactly 727.16 / 798.18 / 905.50, and DH's '₹2,430.84 crore total' is the sum of that row. So DH did report a single state's row as national totals. The defect is in the source chain. The cited MHA source (Q.3253, 29.03.2023) gives West Bengal as 906.12 / 798.18 / 727.20, so it only approximately supports the exact figures the claim quotes, and the matching primary answer is not cited. Analytic is the correct tier because this is our own comparison and it implies no wrongdoing. Its components (the 16,383 count and the annexure rows) are documented in a primary Parliament answer.
verdicts.corrections: 1) Add the primary source to srcs: ['MHA — Rajya Sabha Unstarred Q.1662, 15.03.2023 (Nityanand Rai): 16,383 valid FCRA associations as on 10.03.2023; 14,966 filed FY2021-22 returns; state-wise FC received FY2019-20 to FY2021-22 (Annexure I)', 'https://www.mha.gov.in/MHA1/Par2017/pdfs/par2023-pdfs/RS15032023/1662.pdf']. Keep Q.3253 only as a later revision (returns as on 22.03.2023). 2) In `d`, replace 'cf. RS Q.3253 Annexure I' with 'RS USQ 1662 (15.03.2023) Annexure I, row 34 West Bengal: 727.16 / 798.18 / 905.50; DH's "₹2,430.84 cr total" is the sum of that row.
